{"body":"## Purpose

Close the source input lifecycle for gov-package-output production so `inputLockDigest` covers every source path that can affect a packet.

Parent phase issue: #79

## Scope

This is an issue for a future governance implementation PR. Do not open or implement the PR from this issue alone.

## Requirements

- Define the producer input manifest or accepted equivalent.
- Include repo metadata input paths.
- Include package inventory input paths.
- Include package assertion input paths.
- Include receipt input paths.
- Include README projection receipt input paths.
- Include provider CI intent/state input paths.
- Include findings input paths.
- Include admission input paths.
- Include producer configuration input paths.
- Compute deterministic `inputLockDigest` from the declared source closure.
- Compute deterministic `outputDigest` from generated packet output.
- Fail when a declared input path is missing.
- Fail when an undeclared input affects generated output.
- Fail when output is non-deterministic for the same input closure.
- Preserve packet/projection as non-authority evidence.

## Done when

request.text:
{"body":"## Purpose

Define the final fine-grained target shape for editable JSONL diagrams before implementation work starts.

This issue is the canonical planning issue for turning the current generator into an editable semantic roundtrip kernel:

```text
events.jsonl -> reduce -> DVM -> projection/editor -> edit -> JSONL append -> re-reduce -> proof
```

The goal is not to build a diagram editor from scratch. The goal is to keep `events.jsonl` as the source of truth and make existing editors/layout engines subordinate to that source.

---

## Current repo anchors

The repository already has the correct base direction:

- `events.jsonl` is the only authority.
- generated artifacts are not authority.
- generated artifacts must carry proof metadata and be regenerated from JSONL.
- core does not import adapters; adapters import core.
- current flow is `JSONL events -> tokenizer -> reducer -> DVM -> ports -> adapter fixtures/examples -> SVG proof artifacts`.

Current gap:

- generated SVG / drawio exists, but semantic edit write-back does not.
- layout dispatch is still partly `diagram.kind -> engine`.
- there is no stable `Plane + Rules + Profile + Adapter` contract yet.
- generated artifacts can be viewed, but edits do not append semantic JSONL and re-reduce.

---

## Highest-level decision

Do not treat diagram names as engines.

Treat diagram names as presets/profiles over a smaller semantic core.

```text
Diagram Preset -> Layout Intent -> Plane/Profile/Rules -> Projection Adapter -> Editor/Renderer
```

Core keeps meaning.
Adapters handle UI/rendering/layout/editor-specific details.

---

## Final core model

| Core concept | Meaning | Must be editor-independent? |
|---|---|---:|
| EventLog | append-only `events.jsonl` authority | yes |
| Reducer | events -> DVM | yes |
| DVM | diagram view model, not tied to SVG/drawio/React Flow | yes |
| Plane | semantic 2D space | yes |
| Axis | horizontal/vertical meaning | yes |
| Lane | actor/resource/participant/state/group row or column | yes |
| Mark | point/box/task/event/state marker | yes |
| Span | interval with start/end | yes |
| Edge | dependency/message/transition/relation | yes |
| Container | group/package/boundary/lane/table | yes |
| Port | stable connection point | yes |
| Region | area/overlap/set/map-like grouping | yes |
| Constraint | order/time/containment/align/no-overlap/fixed/manual | yes |
| Rules | domain semantics such as schedule/causal/BPMN/state | yes |
| Profile | named diagram behavior over core primitives | yes |
| Skin | visual styling only | no authority |
| Projection Adapter | DVM -> editor/render model | adapter |
| Edit Translator | editor change -> semantic command/event | adapter boundary, core command |
| Proof | semantic parity, hashes, quality receipts | yes |

---

## Final plane taxonomy

| Plane | Owns | Derived diagrams |
|---|---|---|
| LaneProgressPlane | lane x progress placement | swimlane, gantt-like, horizontal sequence, timeline, roadmap, kanban, BPMN lane surface |
| GraphPlane | relation graph placement | flow, state, architecture, dependency, mindmap, nested ports |
| TablePlane | row/column/table structure | ERD table, matrix, spreadsheet-like diagrams |
| RegionPlane | set/overlap/area semantics | venn, overlap, map-like grouping |
| Router | edge/message/dependency/connector routing | shared by all planes |
| ConstraintSolver boundary | fixed/align/no-overlap/order/containment | may depend on existing solvers; do not hand-roll full solver unless proven necessary |

Do not add a new plane unless a new diagram cannot be expressed by these primitives and profiles.

---

## Preset/profile mapping

| User-facing diagram | Internal expression |
|---|---|
| swimlane | LaneProgressPlane + ordinal/graph-rank progress + LaneFlowProfile |
| gantt | LaneProgressPlane + metric time + Span marks + ScheduleRules |
| horizontal sequence | LaneProgressPlane + causal progress + participant lanes + CausalRules |
| timeline | LaneProgressPlane or ProgressPlane subset + metric time |
| roadmap | LaneProgressPlane + coarse time/phase progress |
| kanban | LaneProgressPlane + discrete stage progress |
| BPMN | LaneProgressPlane + GraphRules + BPMNRules; future bpmn-js adapter for standard BPMN |
| flow | GraphPlane |
| state | GraphPlane + StateRules |
| architecture | GraphPlane + ContainerRules |
| dense_dependency | GraphPlane + DensityPolicy |
| mindmap | GraphPlane + TreeProfile |
| ERD | TablePlane + GraphPlane + Router |
| matrix | TablePlane |
| venn | RegionPlane |
| nested_ports | GraphPlane + ContainerRules + PortRules + Router |

Important: `swimlane`, `gantt`, and horizontal `sequence` must not become separate reducers or layout engines. They share LaneProgressPlane and differ by rules/profile/projection.

---

## Dependency policy

### Depend / reuse

| Area | Dependency policy |
|---|---|
| graph editor UI | React Flow for MVP; yFiles/GoJS/JointJS as later enterprise candidates |
| graph layout | ELK/elkjs first; Graphviz only where useful for dense/dependency validation/fallback |
| BPMN editor | bpmn-js, not custom BPMN editor |
| real Gantt scheduling | external Gantt/scheduler product if true scheduling is required |
| draw.io compatibility | diagrams.net embed or mxGraph XML adapter, not draw.io clone |
| constraint solving | existing solver if LaneProgressPlane exceeds simple coordinate projection |

### Own

| Area | Ownership |
|---|---|
| JSONL event authority | own |
| reducer | own |
| DVM | own |
| Plane/Profile/Rules vocabulary | own |
| semantic edit command model | own |
| editor edit -> JSONL append translator | own |
| validation/proof/CI receipts | own |
| adapter contracts | own |

### Explicitly do not build

- custom canvas editor
- custom graph layout engine
- custom BPMN editor
- custom Gantt scheduling engine
- draw.io clone
- editor-native file format as authority
- SVG/drawio reverse-engineering as the main write-back path

---

## Event namespaces

| Namespace | Authority? | Purpose |
|---|---:|---|
| `semantic.*` | yes | domain meaning changes |
| `visual.*` | yes, but non-semantic | manual layout/style patch separated from meaning |
| `proof.*` | receipt only | generated proof records |
| `projection.*` | generated/receipt | projection metadata, not semantic authority |
| `adapter.*` | receipt/config only | adapter evidence, not semantic authority |

Semantic and visual changes must not be mixed.

---

## Required semantic event kinds

Minimum event kinds needed for the PoC:

| Event kind | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `diagram.define` | create/declare diagram and profile |
| `node.upsert` | create/update node/mark |
| `node.delete` | delete node when allowed |
| `edge.upsert` | create/update edge |
| `edge.delete` | delete edge when allowed |
| `edge.reconnect` | update source/target/port |
| `label.update` | update label for node/edge/container |
| `lane.upsert` | create/update lane |
| `lane.assign` | move node/mark/span to lane |
| `axis.define` | define progress axis type |
| `span.update` | update start/end/duration |
| `container.upsert` | create/update group/package/table/boundary |
| `port.upsert` | create/update connection point |
| `constraint.upsert` | create/update semantic constraint |
| `profile.set` | set diagram profile/preset |
| `rules.set` | attach schedule/causal/state/BPMN rules |

Minimum visual event kinds:

| Event kind | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `visual.position.set` | manual node/mark position override |
| `visual.size.set` | manual size override |
| `visual.edge.bendpoint.set` | manual edge bendpoints |
| `visual.lock.set` | lock/unlock manual placement |
| `visual.style.set` | visual style override, non-semantic |

---

## Edit command contract

Editor changes must first become an editor-independent command, then pass validation, then append JSONL.

```text
editor event -> EditCommand -> validate(command, current DVM) -> JSONL event -> reduce -> proof
```

Required command types:

| Command | Output event |
|---|---|
| Rename node | `label.update` |
| Rename edge | `label.update` |
| Reconnect edge | `edge.reconnect` |
| Connect new edge | `edge.upsert` |
| Move to lane | `lane.assign` |
| Change span start/end | `span.update` |
| Move node visually | `visual.position.set` |
| Resize visually | `visual.size.set` |
| Change bendpoint | `visual.edge.bendpoint.set` |
| Change profile | `profile.set` |

Reject invalid commands before append.

---

## Roundtrip flow

```text
1. read events.jsonl
2. tokenize
3. reduce to DVM
4. classify layout intent into Plane/Profile/Rules
5. project DVM to editor model
6. user edits editor model
7. translate editor change to EditCommand
8. validate command against DVM and rules
9. append semantic.* or visual.* event to events.jsonl
10. re-reduce to DVM
11. re-project
12. emit proof receipt
13. CI checks semantic diff, projection parity, and generated artifacts
```

---

## MVP PoC name

`poc-001-semantic-roundtrip-kernel`

This is not a rendering PoC. It is a boundary proof.

---

## Required fixtures

### Fixture 1: `lane-progress-triptych`

One event log must produce three projections from the same DVM:

| Projection | Purpose |
|---|---|
| swimlane LR | lane x ordinal/flow progress |
| gantt-like | lane x metric time + spans |
| horizontal sequence | participant lane x causal progress |

Acceptance:

- no separate reducer for swimlane/gantt/sequence
- same stable IDs across all projections
- same lane assignment source
- profile/rules decide differences
- editing one label/lane/span updates all relevant projections after re-reduce

### Fixture 2: `graph-roundtrip`

Minimal graph with:

- 5 nodes
- 5 edges
- 1 container
- 2 ports
- one edge reconnect command
- one invalid reconnect case

Acceptance:

- GraphPlane uses ELK adapter when available
- semantic node/edge parity is proven
- reconnect appends `edge.reconnect`
- invalid connect is rejected before append

### Fixture 3: `visual-patch-isolation`

Acceptance:

- node drag appends `visual.position.set`
- semantic hash does not change
- visual hash changes
- re-layout does not overwrite locked manual position unless explicitly unlocked

### Fixture 4: `table-region-boundary`

Minimum proof that TablePlane and RegionPlane are not accidentally forced into GraphPlane:

- tiny ERD/table relation case
- tiny Venn/overlap case
- no new engine added
- projection profile only

---

## Proof outputs

Each fixture must emit a proof file containing at least:

| Proof field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `schema` | proof schema version |
| `authority` | `events.jsonl` |
| `generatedIsAuthority` | false |
| `dvmBeforeHash` | before edit hash |
| `editCommand` | normalized command |
| `appendedEventHash` | appended event hash |
| `dvmAfterHash` | after edit hash |
| `semanticHashBefore` | meaning hash before |
| `semanticHashAfter` | meaning hash after |
| `visualHashBefore` | visual hash before |
| `visualHashAfter` | visual hash after |
| `semanticDiff` | allowed semantic diff |
| `visualDiff` | allowed visual diff |
| `projectionParity` | stable node/edge/lane IDs across projections |
| `layoutEngine` | selected layout adapter |
| `fallbackUsed` | whether fallback was used |
| `rejectCases` | invalid edits rejected |
| `adapterBoundary` | editor/layout dependency did not enter core |

---

## CI gates

| Gate | Requirement |
|---|---|
| G1 authority | no editor model, SVG, drawio, layout.json, or HTML is authority |
| G2 roundtrip | append -> re-reduce -> projection succeeds |
| G3 semantic diff | only intended semantic fields change |
| G4 visual isolation | visual changes do not alter semantic hash |
| G5 projection parity | same stable IDs across swimlane/gantt/sequence projections |
| G6 invalid edit reject | invalid commands do not append |
| G7 core boundary | core imports no adapter/editor/layout package |
| G8 adapter boundary | React Flow/ELK/drawio-specific code is adapter-only |
| G9 no custom canvas | no bespoke editor engine introduced |
| G10 no graph layout reinvention | graph layout delegated to ELK/Graphviz/SDK |
| G11 no BPMN/Gantt reinvention | standard BPMN/Gantt remain external adapter scope |
| G12 generated artifact quality | existing SVG/drawio quality gates still pass |
| G13 proof determinism | repeated run gives same proof hashes except allowed timestamps if any |
| G14 profile extension rule | new diagram type must map to existing Plane/Profile first |
| G15 fallback clarity | deterministic fallback is explicit and fails under strict mode where required |

---

## Implementation split proposal

### PR A: contract/doc/schema only

- add architecture decision doc
- add schema docs for EventLog, DVM, Plane, Profile, Rules, EditCommand, Proof
- add examples as JSONL fixtures without UI
- no React Flow dependency yet

### PR B: core reducer extension

- add Plane/Profile/Rules classification
- add LaneProgressPlane primitives
- add semantic/visual hash separation
- add command validation surface

### PR C: roundtrip non-UI proof

- simulate edit commands from JSON fixtures
- append events
- re-reduce
- prove semantic diff / visual isolation / projection parity

### PR D: React Flow adapter PoC

- project DVM to React Flow model
- translate minimal editor changes to EditCommand
- keep adapter out of core

### PR E: layout adapter cleanup

- change `diagram.kind -> engine` dispatch into `layoutIntent -> adapter` dispatch
- keep ELK/Graphviz as backends, not diagram concepts

### PR F: CI artifact/proof integration

- publish roundtrip proof artifacts
- include manifest/report in CI artifact gallery
- fail if proof or adapter boundary breaks

---

## Non-goals for this issue

- full collaborative editing
- full undo/redo design
- production UI polish
- full BPMN compliance
- full Gantt scheduling
- draw.io full reverse-writeback
- replacing existing SVG/drawio generation
- packaging for npm/PyPI

---

## Definition of done

This issue can close only when:

- [ ] `events.jsonl` remains the only authority.
- [ ] DVM remains editor/render/layout independent.
- [ ] LaneProgressPlane proves swimlane/gantt-like/horizontal-sequence projection from one source.
- [ ] GraphPlane proves minimal reconnect roundtrip.
- [ ] semantic and visual changes are separated.
- [ ] editor operations become JSONL append events through EditCommand.
- [ ] invalid edits are rejected before append.
- [ ] generated proof contains before/after semantic and visual hashes.
- [ ] core imports no editor/layout adapter.
- [ ] CI fails on proof drift, semantic unintended diff, or boundary violation.
- [ ] React Flow/ELK remain replaceable adapters.
- [ ] no custom canvas, layout engine, BPMN engine, or Gantt scheduler is introduced.

---

## Design rule after this issue

New diagram support must follow this order:

1. express with existing Plane/Profile/Rules
2. add a Profile if only behavior/preset differs
3. add Rules if domain validation differs
4. add Projection Adapter if editor/render target differs
5. add a core primitive only if existing primitives cannot express the meaning
6. add a new Plane only after a written contradiction proves all existing planes fail

The expected steady-state is:

```text
Diagram name = product vocabulary
Plane/Profile/Rules = semantic core
Adapter = dependency boundary
Editor/layout/render artifact = projection
JSONL = authority
Proof = trust boundary
```"}

{"body":"## Purpose

Define the final fine-grained target shape for editable JSONL diagrams before implementation work starts.

This issue is the canonical planning issue for turning the current generator into an editable semantic roundtrip kernel:

```text
events.jsonl -> reduce -> DVM -> projection/editor -> edit -> JSONL append -> re-reduce -> proof
```

The goal is not to build a diagram editor from scratch. The goal is to keep `events.jsonl` as the source of truth and make existing editors/layout engines subordinate to that source.

---

## Current repo anchors

The repository already has the correct base direction:

- `events.jsonl` is the only authority.
- generated artifacts are not authority.
- generated artifacts must carry proof metadata and be regenerated from JSONL.
- core does not import adapters; adapters import core.
- current flow is `JSONL events -> tokenizer -> reducer -> DVM -> ports -> adapter fixtures/examples -> SVG proof artifacts`.

Current gap:

- generated SVG / drawio exists, but semantic edit write-back does not.
- layout dispatch is still partly `diagram.kind -> engine`.
- there is no stable `Plane + Rules + Profile + Adapter` contract yet.
- generated artifacts can be viewed, but edits do not append semantic JSONL and re-reduce.

---

## Highest-level decision

Do not treat diagram names as engines.

Treat diagram names as presets/profiles over a smaller semantic core.

```text
Diagram Preset -> Layout Intent -> Plane/Profile/Rules -> Projection Adapter -> Editor/Renderer
```

Core keeps meaning.
Adapters handle UI/rendering/layout/editor-specific details.

| Core concept | Meaning | Must be editor-independent? |

| Reducer | events -> DVM | yes |

| Axis | horizontal/vertical meaning | yes |
| Lane | actor/resource/participant/state/group row or column | yes |
| Mark | point/box/task/event/state marker | yes |
| Span | interval with start/end | yes |
| Edge | dependency/message/transition/relation | yes |
| Container | group/package/boundary/lane/table | yes |
| Port | stable connection point | yes |
| Region | area/overlap/set/map-like grouping | yes |
| Constraint | order/time/containment/align/no-overlap/fixed/manual | yes |
| Rules | domain semantics such as schedule/causal/BPMN/state | yes |
| Profile | named diagram behavior over core primitives | yes |
| Skin | visual styling only | no authority |
| Projection Adapter | DVM -> editor/render model | adapter |

| TablePlane | row/column/table structure | ERD table, matrix, spreadsheet-like diagrams |
| RegionPlane | set/overlap/area semantics | venn, overlap, map-like grouping |
| Router | edge/message/dependency/connector routing | shared by all planes |
| ConstraintSolver boundary | fixed/align/no-overlap/order/containment | may depend on existing solvers; do not hand-roll full solver unless proven necessary |

| timeline | LaneProgressPlane or ProgressPlane subset + metric time |
| roadmap | LaneProgressPlane + coarse time/phase progress |
| kanban | LaneProgressPlane + discrete stage progress |
| BPMN | LaneProgressPlane + GraphRules + BPMNRules; future bpmn-js adapter for standard BPMN |
| flow | GraphPlane |
| state | GraphPlane + StateRules |
| architecture | GraphPlane + ContainerRules |
| dense_dependency | GraphPlane + DensityPolicy |
| mindmap | GraphPlane + TreeProfile |
| ERD | TablePlane + GraphPlane + Router |

state.body:
## Purpose

Define the final fine-grained target shape for editable JSONL diagrams before implementation work starts.

This issue is the canonical planning issue for turning the current generator into an editable semantic roundtrip kernel:

```text
events.jsonl -> reduce -> DVM -> projection/editor -> edit -> JSONL append -> re-reduce -> proof
```

The goal is not to build a diagram editor from scratch. The goal is to keep `events.jsonl` as the source of truth and make existing editors/layout engines subordinate to that source.

---

## Current repo anchors

The repository already has the correct base direction:

- `events.jsonl` is the only authority.
- generated artifacts are not authority.
- generated artifacts must carry proof metadata and be regenerated from JSONL.
- core does not import adapters; adapters import core.
- current flow is `JSONL events -> tokenizer -> reducer -> DVM -> ports -> adapter fixtures/examples -> SVG proof artifacts`.

Current gap:

- generated SVG / drawio exists, but semantic edit write-back does not.
- layout dispatch is still partly `diagram.kind -> engine`.
- there is no stable `Plane + Rules + Profile + Adapter` contract yet.
- generated artifacts can be viewed, but edits do not append semantic JSONL and re-reduce.

---

## Highest-level decision

Do not treat diagram names as engines.

Treat diagram names as presets/profiles over a smaller semantic core.

```text
Diagram Preset -> Layout Intent -> Plane/Profile/Rules -> Projection Adapter -> Editor/Renderer
```

Core keeps meaning.
Adapters handle UI/rendering/layout/editor-specific details.

---

## Final core model

| Core concept | Meaning | Must be editor-independent? |
|---|---|---:|
| EventLog | append-only `events.jsonl` authority | yes |
| Reducer | events -> DVM | yes |
| DVM | diagram view model, not tied to SVG/drawio/React Flow | yes |
| Plane | semantic 2D space | yes |
| Axis | horizontal/vertical meaning | yes |
| Lane | actor/resource/participant/state/group row or column | yes |
| Mark | point/box/task/event/state marker | yes |
| Span | interval with start/end | yes |
| Edge | dependency/message/transition/relation | yes |
| Container | group/package/boundary/lane/table | yes |
| Port | stable connection point | yes |
| Region | area/overlap/set/map-like grouping | yes |
| Constraint | order/time/containment/align/no-overlap/fixed/manual | yes |
| Rules | domain semantics such as schedule/causal/BPMN/state | yes |
| Profile | named diagram behavior over core primitives | yes |
| Skin | visual styling only | no authority |
| Projection Adapter | DVM -> editor/render model | adapter |
| Edit Translator | editor change -> semantic command/event | adapter boundary, core command |
| Proof | semantic parity, hashes, quality receipts | yes |

---

## Final plane taxonomy

| Plane | Owns | Derived diagrams |
|---|---|---|
| LaneProgressPlane | lane x progress placement | swimlane, gantt-like, horizontal sequence, timeline, roadmap, kanban, BPMN lane surface |
| GraphPlane | relation graph placement | flow, state, architecture, dependency, mindmap, nested ports |
| TablePlane | row/column/table structure | ERD table, matrix, spreadsheet-like diagrams |
| RegionPlane | set/overlap/area semantics | venn, overlap, map-like grouping |
| Router | edge/message/dependency/connector routing | shared by all planes |
| ConstraintSolver boundary | fixed/align/no-overlap/order/containment | may depend on existing solvers; do not hand-roll full solver unless proven necessary |

Do not add a new plane unless a new diagram cannot be expressed by these primitives and profiles.

---

## Preset/profile mapping

| User-facing diagram | Internal expression |
|---|---|
| swimlane | LaneProgressPlane + ordinal/graph-rank progress + LaneFlowProfile |
| gantt | LaneProgressPlane + metric time + Span marks + ScheduleRules |
| horizontal sequence | LaneProgressPlane + causal progress + participant lanes + CausalRules |
| timeline | LaneProgressPlane or ProgressPlane subset + metric time |
| roadmap | LaneProgressPlane + coarse time/phase progress |
| kanban | LaneProgressPlane + discrete stage progress |
| BPMN | LaneProgressPlane + GraphRules + BPMNRules; future bpmn-js adapter for standard BPMN |
| flow | GraphPlane |
| state | GraphPlane + StateRules |
| architecture | GraphPlane + ContainerRules |
| dense_dependency | GraphPlane + DensityPolicy |
| mindmap | GraphPlane + TreeProfile |
| ERD | TablePlane + GraphPlane + Router |
| matrix | TablePlane |
| venn | RegionPlane |
| nested_ports | GraphPlane + ContainerRules + PortRules + Router |

Important: `swimlane`, `gantt`, and horizontal `sequence` must not become separate reducers or layout engines. They share LaneProgressPlane and differ by rules/profile/projection.

---

## Dependency policy

### Depend / reuse

| Area | Dependency policy |
|---|---|
| graph editor UI | React Flow for MVP; yFiles/GoJS/JointJS as later enterprise candidates |
| graph layout | ELK/elkjs first; Graphviz only where useful for dense/dependency validation/fallback |
| BPMN editor | bpmn-js, not custom BPMN editor |
| real Gantt scheduling | external Gantt/scheduler product if true scheduling is required |
| draw.io compatibility | diagrams.net embed or mxGraph XML adapter, not draw.io clone |
| constraint solving | existing solver if LaneProgressPlane exceeds simple coordinate projection |

### Own

| Area | Ownership |
|---|---|
| JSONL event authority | own |
| reducer | own |
| DVM | own |
| Plane/Profile/Rules vocabulary | own |
| semantic edit command model | own |
| editor edit -> JSONL append translator | own |
| validation/proof/CI receipts | own |
| adapter contracts | own |

### Explicitly do not build

- custom canvas editor
- custom graph layout engine
- custom BPMN editor
- custom Gantt scheduling engine
- draw.io clone
- editor-native file format as authority
- SVG/drawio reverse-engineering as the main write-back path

---

## Event namespaces

| Namespace | Authority? | Purpose |
|---|---:|---|
| `semantic.*` | yes | domain meaning changes |
| `visual.*` | yes, but non-semantic | manual layout/style patch separated from meaning |
| `proof.*` | receipt only | generated proof records |
| `projection.*` | generated/receipt | projection metadata, not semantic authority |
| `adapter.*` | receipt/config only | adapter evidence, not semantic authority |

Semantic and visual changes must not be mixed.

---

## Required semantic event kinds

Minimum event kinds needed for the PoC:

| Event kind | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `diagram.define` | create/declare diagram and profile |
| `node.upsert` | create/update node/mark |
| `node.delete` | delete node when allowed |
| `edge.upsert` | create/update edge |
| `edge.delete` | delete edge when allowed |
| `edge.reconnect` | update source/target/port |
| `label.update` | update label for node/edge/container |
| `lane.upsert` | create/update lane |
| `lane.assign` | move node/mark/span to lane |
| `axis.define` | define progress axis type |
| `span.update` | update start/end/duration |
| `container.upsert` | create/update group/package/table/boundary |
| `port.upsert` | create/update connection point |
| `constraint.upsert` | create/update semantic constraint |
| `profile.set` | set diagram profile/preset |
| `rules.set` | attach schedule/causal/state/BPMN rules |

Minimum visual event kinds:

| Event kind | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `visual.position.set` | manual node/mark position override |
| `visual.size.set` | manual size override |
| `visual.edge.bendpoint.set` | manual edge bendpoints |
| `visual.lock.set` | lock/unlock manual placement |
| `visual.style.set` | visual style override, non-semantic |

---

## Edit command contract

Editor changes must first become an editor-independent command, then pass validation, then append JSONL.

```text
editor event -> EditCommand -> validate(command, current DVM) -> JSONL event -> reduce -> proof
```

Required command types:

| Command | Output event |
|---|---|
| Rename node | `label.update` |
| Rename edge | `label.update` |
| Reconnect edge | `edge.reconnect` |
| Connect new edge | `edge.upsert` |
| Move to lane | `lane.assign` |
| Change span start/end | `span.update` |
| Move node visually | `visual.position.set` |
| Resize visually | `visual.size.set` |
| Change bendpoint | `visual.edge.bendpoint.set` |
| Change profile | `profile.set` |

Reject invalid commands before append.

---

## Roundtrip flow

```text
1. read events.jsonl
2. tokenize
3. reduce to DVM
4. classify layout intent into Plane/Profile/Rules
5. project DVM to editor model
6. user edits editor model
7. translate editor change to EditCommand
8. validate command against DVM and rules
9. append semantic.* or visual.* event to events.jsonl
10. re-reduce to DVM
11. re-project
12. emit proof receipt
13. CI checks semantic diff, projection parity, and generated artifacts
```

---

## MVP PoC name

`poc-001-semantic-roundtrip-kernel`

This is not a rendering PoC. It is a boundary proof.

---

## Required fixtures

### Fixture 1: `lane-progress-triptych`

One event log must produce three projections from the same DVM:

| Projection | Purpose |
|---|---|
| swimlane LR | lane x ordinal/flow progress |
| gantt-like | lane x metric time + spans |
| horizontal sequence | participant lane x causal progress |

Acceptance:

- no separate reducer for swimlane/gantt/sequence
- same stable IDs across all projections
- same lane assignment source
- profile/rules decide differences
- editing one label/lane/span updates all relevant projections after re-reduce

### Fixture 2: `graph-roundtrip`

Minimal graph with:

- 5 nodes
- 5 edges
- 1 container
- 2 ports
- one edge reconnect command
- one invalid reconnect case

Acceptance:

- GraphPlane uses ELK adapter when available
- semantic node/edge parity is proven
- reconnect appends `edge.reconnect`
- invalid connect is rejected before append

### Fixture 3: `visual-patch-isolation`

Acceptance:

- node drag appends `visual.position.set`
- semantic hash does not change
- visual hash changes
- re-layout does not overwrite locked manual position unless explicitly unlocked

### Fixture 4: `table-region-boundary`

Minimum proof that TablePlane and RegionPlane are not accidentally forced into GraphPlane:

- tiny ERD/table relation case
- tiny Venn/overlap case
- no new engine added
- projection profile only

---

## Proof outputs

Each fixture must emit a proof file containing at least:

| Proof field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `schema` | proof schema version |
| `authority` | `events.jsonl` |
| `generatedIsAuthority` | false |
| `dvmBeforeHash` | before edit hash |
| `editCommand` | normalized command |
| `appendedEventHash` | appended event hash |
| `dvmAfterHash` | after edit hash |
| `semanticHashBefore` | meaning hash before |
| `semanticHashAfter` | meaning hash after |
| `visualHashBefore` | visual hash before |
| `visualHashAfter` | visual hash after |
| `semanticDiff` | allowed semantic diff |
| `visualDiff` | allowed visual diff |
| `projectionParity` | stable node/edge/lane IDs across projections |
| `layoutEngine` | selected layout adapter |
| `fallbackUsed` | whether fallback was used |
| `rejectCases` | invalid edits rejected |
| `adapterBoundary` | editor/layout dependency did not enter core |

---

## CI gates

| Gate | Requirement |
|---|---|
| G1 authority | no editor model, SVG, drawio, layout.json, or HTML is authority |
| G2 roundtrip | append -> re-reduce -> projection succeeds |
| G3 semantic diff | only intended semantic fields change |
| G4 visual isolation | visual changes do not alter semantic hash |
| G5 projection parity | same stable IDs across swimlane/gantt/sequence projections |
| G6 invalid edit reject | invalid commands do not append |
| G7 core boundary | core imports no adapter/editor/layout package |
| G8 adapter boundary | React Flow/ELK/drawio-specific code is adapter-only |
| G9 no custom canvas | no bespoke editor engine introduced |
| G10 no graph layout reinvention | graph layout delegated to ELK/Graphviz/SDK |
| G11 no BPMN/Gantt reinvention | standard BPMN/Gantt remain external adapter scope |
| G12 generated artifact quality | existing SVG/drawio quality gates still pass |
| G13 proof determinism | repeated run gives same proof hashes except allowed timestamps if any |
| G14 profile extension rule | new diagram type must map to existing Plane/Profile first |
| G15 fallback clarity | deterministic fallback is explicit and fails under strict mode where required |

---

## Implementation split proposal

### PR A: contract/doc/schema only

- add architecture decision doc
- add schema docs for EventLog, DVM, Plane, Profile, Rules, EditCommand, Proof
- add examples as JSONL fixtures without UI
- no React Flow dependency yet

### PR B: core reducer extension

- add Plane/Profile/Rules classification
- add LaneProgressPlane primitives
- add semantic/visual hash separation
- add command validation surface

### PR C: roundtrip non-UI proof

- simulate edit commands from JSON fixtures
- append events
- re-reduce
- prove semantic diff / visual isolation / projection parity

### PR D: React Flow adapter PoC

- project DVM to React Flow model
- translate minimal editor changes to EditCommand
- keep adapter out of core

### PR E: layout adapter cleanup

- change `diagram.kind -> engine` dispatch into `layoutIntent -> adapter` dispatch
- keep ELK/Graphviz as backends, not diagram concepts

### PR F: CI artifact/proof integration

- publish roundtrip proof artifacts
- include manifest/report in CI artifact gallery
- fail if proof or adapter boundary breaks

---

## Non-goals for this issue

- full collaborative editing
- full undo/redo design
- production UI polish
- full BPMN compliance
- full Gantt scheduling
- draw.io full reverse-writeback
- replacing existing SVG/drawio generation
- packaging for npm/PyPI

---

## Definition of done

This issue can close only when:

- [ ] `events.jsonl` remains the only authority.
- [ ] DVM remains editor/render/layout independent.
- [ ] LaneProgressPlane proves swimlane/gantt-like/horizontal-sequence projection from one source.
- [ ] GraphPlane proves minimal reconnect roundtrip.
- [ ] semantic and visual changes are separated.
- [ ] editor operations become JSONL append events through EditCommand.
- [ ] invalid edits are rejected before append.
- [ ] generated proof contains before/after semantic and visual hashes.
- [ ] core imports no editor/layout adapter.
- [ ] CI fails on proof drift, semantic unintended diff, or boundary violation.
- [ ] React Flow/ELK remain replaceable adapters.
- [ ] no custom canvas, layout engine, BPMN engine, or Gantt scheduler is introduced.

---

## Design rule after this issue

New diagram support must follow this order:

1. express with existing Plane/Profile/Rules
2. add a Profile if only behavior/preset differs
3. add Rules if domain validation differs
4. add Projection Adapter if editor/render target differs
5. add a core primitive only if existing primitives cannot express the meaning
6. add a new Plane only after a written contradiction proves all existing planes fail

The expected steady-state is:

```text
Diagram name = product vocabulary
Plane/Profile/Rules = semantic core
Adapter = dependency boundary
Editor/layout/render artifact = projection
JSONL = authority
Proof = trust boundary
```

state.body:
## Purpose

Create canonical package receipt rows so CI/check output becomes evidence with packageId, contractId, decisionDigest, assertionDigest, checkId, status, and evidenceDigest instead of an ambiguous green signal.

## Post-merge state

After attached PRs merge:
- package checks can emit joinable receipt rows.
- raw `nix flake check` success is not treated as final pass.
- receipts can be matched against assertions and ADRS decisions.

## Completion audit impact

Contributes to:
- `receiptAudit`: required assertions have matching receipts.
- `receiptDigestSet`: canonical receipt row digest set.
- `completionCertificate.receiptDigestSet`.

## Merge blockers

Do not merge child PRs when:
- receipt rows omit packageId, contractId, decisionDigest, assertionDigest, checkId, status, or evidenceDigest.
- raw CI green is described as final compliance.
- stale or mismatched receipts cannot be detected.
- the PR changes branch protection or final gate authority.

## Required evidence

- receipt schema or producer path.
- clean fixture receipt matching assertion/decision digest.
- stale/wrong digest fixture path.
- CI/check proving receipt generation and validation.

## Boundary

This issue closes canonical receipt production only. It does not close final join or required check cutover.

state.body:
## Purpose

Create canonical package receipt rows so CI/check output becomes evidence with packageId, contractId, decisionDigest, assertionDigest, checkId, status, and evidenceDigest instead of an ambiguous green signal.

## Post-merge state

After attached PRs merge:
- package checks can emit joinable receipt rows.
- raw `nix flake check` success is not treated as final pass.
- receipts can be matched against assertions and ADRS decisions.

## Completion audit impact

Contributes to:
- `receiptAudit`: required assertions have matching receipts.
- `receiptDigestSet`: canonical receipt row digest set.
- `completionCertificate.receiptDigestSet`.

## Merge blockers

Do not merge child PRs when:
- receipt rows omit packageId, contractId, decisionDigest, assertionDigest, checkId, status, or evidenceDigest.
- raw CI green is described as final compliance.
- stale or mismatched receipts cannot be detected.
- the PR changes branch protection or final gate authority.

## Required evidence

- receipt schema or producer path.
- clean fixture receipt matching assertion/decision digest.
- stale/wrong digest fixture path.
- CI/check proving receipt generation and validation.

## Boundary

This issue closes canonical receipt production only. It does not close final join or required check cutover.

specification.instruction: Read only the complete literal body, including HTML comments, tables, formulas and templates. Decide whether it contains at least one statement presented as a specification or operative contract: a rule, expected or acceptable condition, responsibility, functional capability, input/output mapping, interface purpose, or condition or limitation of use. A stated expected-outcome caption or interface text declaring an action's purpose can qualify. No formal specification label, generality, adoption, implementation, must-word or future tense is required. Distinguish the role of the relationship being stated. Declaring what a function does or what condition applies counts; merely describing what happened, is happening, used to happen or regularly happens in observed execution does not by itself declare a specification. A performed configuration, measured value, comparison or causal explanation does not supply an unstated applicable contract. These are role distinctions, not rules excluding particular headings, formats, tenses or words: a report may also contain a genuine specification, and an ordinary capability statement can declare one without requesting a change. Read each statement in context; one qualifying declaration anywhere is sufficient and observations elsewhere do not cancel it. Quoted or hypothetical text counts when used to declare the specification, but not when displayed only as an illustration. Synthetic contrast: 'This dial sets the sampling interval' declares a function; 'I turned the dial and the reading changed' alone reports an observation. A request or a subject's goal alone does not establish this specification role. Do not consult external content.

options.yes: The complete body contains at least one statement presented as a specification or operative contract of the kind defined in the instruction. It declares the relationship itself; merely reporting a performed action, observed configuration or value, observed result, or a causal explanation of an observed event does not by itself establish that role. A genuine declaration still counts inside a report, quotation or template when the body uses it to declare that relationship.
options.no: The complete body contains no statement presented as a specification or operative contract of the kind defined in the instruction. Answer no only for absence throughout the body; observations elsewhere do not cancel a genuine declaration.

request.instruction: Read only the complete literal body, including HTML comments, tables, formulas and templates. Decide whether it contains at least one genuine request for an action, answer, submission, improvement or remedy, or explicitly presents an action or state as a subject's intended goal or need. Count indirect requests and actual conditional reporting or submission directions, including directions carried by a template or HTML comment whether or not the requested information has been supplied. No addressee, stated reason, fully identified final goal, solution, adoption or implementation is required. Distinguish a relationship presented as a target or request from wording that only locates the circumstances of a reported event or explains a necessary response to it. An incident, inability, missing feature, risk, complaint, category or recipient mention alone does not declare the desired opposite or request its correction. Merely explaining what was necessary to obtain an observed result or work around it does not by itself declare an intended goal. Do not exclude a genuine goal or request merely because it appears within a report or a subordinate clause; do not infer one solely from modality, tense, a heading, mention, imperative form or question mark. A specification or expected caption alone does not establish this request or subject-goal role. One qualifying statement anywhere is sufficient and observations elsewhere do not cancel it. Quoted or hypothetical text counts when the body uses it to make an actual request or goal declaration, but not when shown only as an illustration. Synthetic contrast: 'I need a cost estimate before ordering the materials' declares a goal or need; 'The estimate arrived late, so I postponed the order' alone reports an event and response. Do not consult external content.

options.yes: The complete body contains at least one genuine request or declaration of a subject's intended goal or need of the kind defined in the instruction. This includes actual reporting or submission directions before the requested information is supplied. Merely naming a category or recipient, reporting an incident or inability, or explaining a necessary workaround does not itself establish this role.
options.no: The complete body contains no genuine request or declaration of a subject's intended goal or need of the kind defined in the instruction. Answer no only for absence throughout the body; a report or subordinate clause does not cancel an actual request or goal.

{"body":"Parent: #99

Depends on: #67

## Purpose

Reconstruct one run from canonical durable evidence so its structural request context, lifecycle, final answer/path, error, and native session reference remain understandable after restart and without terminal scrollback.

## Purpose lineage

| generation | purpose | contribution | relation |
|---:|---|---|---|
| G0 scope | Inspect one worker run in detail. | Adds a read-only detail command over canonical evidence. | direct |
| G1 correctness | Explain missing or invalid final state instead of fabricating an answer. | Structured errors and lifecycle diagnostics remain non-green. | direct |
| G2 boundary | Reuse #67 identity/status reduction. | Show adds detail formatting, not another run authority or redaction policy. | direct |
| G3 product | Recover useful output after execution. | Final text/path, errors, events, and native-session hints are visible. | direct |
| G4 system | Remove terminal-memory dependence. | All detail is rebuilt from durable instruction/result rows. | direct |
| G5 organization | Make review and handoff evidence self-contained. | Another operator can understand what ran and what happened. | direct |
| G6 business | Lower supervision and rework cost. | Results need not be rediscovered in each target UI. | direct |
| G7 transfer | Let a new owner audit one run without tribal knowledge. | Stable JSON and plain text expose the evidence chain. | indirect |
| G8 due diligence | Make final-answer and failure claims reproducible. | Binary proof reads the same canonical rows a reviewer can inspect. | indirect |
| G9 asset value | Preserve operational value in small durable contracts. | No database/TUI authority is required. | indirect |
| G10 meta | Increase company value and saleability. | Lower key-person, secret-exposure, and evidence-loss risk improves transferability. | indirect |

## Scope

- Add `hq-worker show --run <run_id>` or equivalent.
- Reuse the #67 ledger row for run identity, status, timing, and summary.
- Include only safe structural instruction context by default: id, target, op, cwd, created time, and `reply_to` when present.
- Exclude arbitrary instruction payload, reason, and label text from default observation until an explicit redacted projection contract exists.
- Include ordered canonical `result.v1` events.
- Include final text/path or structured error when present; #101 must redact result content before it becomes durable.
- Include native-session id and a target-neutral read/attach hint when present.
- Support plain text and one `worker.run-detail.v1` JSON object.

## Non-scope

- Live follow; #70 owns that.
- Full target payload disclosure by default.
- A second redaction implementation inside observation.
- Target-specific attach implementation.
- Retry, resume, replay, reconciliation, approval, or dispatch.
- Browser UI or database.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] One completed run shows structural request context, full lifecycle, and final answer/path.
- [ ] Failed/blocked/timeout/cancelled runs show structured error code and message.
- [ ] A queued/running run clearly explains that no final answer exists yet.
- [ ] Native-session reference is visible when canonical result rows contain it.
- [ ] Missing run returns `worker.error.v1` with `run_not_found` and non-zero status.
- [ ] Existing but invalid/unlinked run returns typed `invalid_run_evidence`, not `run_not_found`.
- [ ] Invalid lifecycle or missing linked instruction cannot appear as a healthy detail view.
- [ ] Event order is canonical `seq`, not timestamp or file-discovery guesswork.
- [ ] Text and JSON views describe the same run and terminal state.
- [ ] Default output contains no arbitrary instruction payload, reason, or label text.
- [ ] Show performs zero durable writes and zero adapter calls.
- [ ] Linux binary proof and Windows build/command tests pass.

## Destructive cases

The issue is not complete if any succeeds:

1. final answer exists only in terminal scrollback;
2. show invents a final answer for queued/running/failed work;
3. show hides the structured error behind plain terminal text;
4. event order differs from canonical sequence;
5. a native-session hint changes run identity or authority;
6. missing run exits green;
7. an existing invalid run is mislabeled as merely missing;
8. invalid evidence appears as a completed run;
9. show requires a live target process;
10. raw instruction payload, reason, or labels are copied into default output;
11. unredacted result content bypasses #101;
12. show mutates durable state, retries, redacts, or attaches automatically.

## Dependencies

- #67 unified ledger.
- #101 redaction must protect durable result/final evidence before observation.
- #52-#66 adapters must map final/error/native session data only through canonical `result.v1`.
- #98 owns lifecycle/reconciliation states.
- #81-#84 own integrated binary/readback evidence.

## Evidence

- Completed, failed, blocked, queued/running, missing-run, and invalid-run command tests.
- Exact event ordering fixture.
- Final text/path and native-session fixture.
- Secret-bearing instruction fixture proving prompt/argv/reason/labels are absent from output.
- Binary-level JSON detail artifact.
- Zero-write/zero-dispatch proof.

## Merge condition

Merge only when one run can be understood from durable canonical evidence alone, including why no final answer exists when the run is not completed, without creating a second authority or exposing arbitrary instruction text."}

Parent: #99

Depends on: #67

## Purpose

Reconstruct one run from canonical durable evidence so its structural request context, lifecycle, final answer/path, error, and native session reference remain understandable after restart and without terminal scrollback.

## Purpose lineage

| generation | purpose | contribution | relation |
|---:|---|---|---|
| G0 scope | Inspect one worker run in detail. | Adds a read-only detail command over canonical evidence. | direct |
| G1 correctness | Explain missing or invalid final state instead of fabricating an answer. | Structured errors and lifecycle diagnostics remain non-green. | direct |
| G2 boundary | Reuse #67 identity/status reduction. | Show adds detail formatting, not another run authority or redaction policy. | direct |
| G3 product | Recover useful output after execution. | Final text/path, errors, events, and native-session hints are visible. | direct |
| G4 system | Remove terminal-memory dependence. | All detail is rebuilt from durable instruction/result rows. | direct |
| G5 organization | Make review and handoff evidence self-contained. | Another operator can understand what ran and what happened. | direct |
| G6 business | Lower supervision and rework cost. | Results need not be rediscovered in each target UI. | direct |
| G7 transfer | Let a new owner audit one run without tribal knowledge. | Stable JSON and plain text expose the evidence chain. | indirect |
| G8 due diligence | Make final-answer and failure claims reproducible. | Binary proof reads the same canonical rows a reviewer can inspect. | indirect |
| G9 asset value | Preserve operational value in small durable contracts. | No database/TUI authority is required. | indirect |
| G10 meta | Increase company value and saleability. | Lower key-person, secret-exposure, and evidence-loss risk improves transferability. | indirect |

## Scope

- Add `hq-worker show --run <run_id>` or equivalent.
- Reuse the #67 ledger row for run identity, status, timing, and summary.
- Include only safe structural instruction context by default: id, target, op, cwd, created time, and `reply_to` when present.
- Exclude arbitrary instruction payload, reason, and label text from default observation until an explicit redacted projection contract exists.
- Include ordered canonical `result.v1` events.
- Include final text/path or structured error when present; #101 must redact result content before it becomes durable.
- Include native-session id and a target-neutral read/attach hint when present.
- Support plain text and one `worker.run-detail.v1` JSON object.

## Non-scope

- Live follow; #70 owns that.
- Full target payload disclosure by default.
- A second redaction implementation inside observation.
- Target-specific attach implementation.
- Retry, resume, replay, reconciliation, approval, or dispatch.
- Browser UI or database.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] One completed run shows structural request context, full lifecycle, and final answer/path.
- [ ] Failed/blocked/timeout/cancelled runs show structured error code and message.
- [ ] A queued/running run clearly explains that no final answer exists yet.
- [ ] Native-session reference is visible when canonical result rows contain it.
- [ ] Missing run returns `worker.error.v1` with `run_not_found` and non-zero status.
- [ ] Existing but invalid/unlinked run returns typed `invalid_run_evidence`, not `run_not_found`.
- [ ] Invalid lifecycle or missing linked instruction cannot appear as a healthy detail view.
- [ ] Event order is canonical `seq`, not timestamp or file-discovery guesswork.
- [ ] Text and JSON views describe the same run and terminal state.
- [ ] Default output contains no arbitrary instruction payload, reason, or label text.
- [ ] Show performs zero durable writes and zero adapter calls.
- [ ] Linux binary proof and Windows build/command tests pass.

## Destructive cases

The issue is not complete if any succeeds:

1. final answer exists only in terminal scrollback;
2. show invents a final answer for queued/running/failed work;
3. show hides the structured error behind plain terminal text;
4. event order differs from canonical sequence;
5. a native-session hint changes run identity or authority;
6. missing run exits green;
7. an existing invalid run is mislabeled as merely missing;
8. invalid evidence appears as a completed run;
9. show requires a live target process;
10. raw instruction payload, reason, or labels are copied into default output;
11. unredacted result content bypasses #101;
12. show mutates durable state, retries, redacts, or attaches automatically.

## Dependencies

- #67 unified ledger.
- #101 redaction must protect durable result/final evidence before observation.
- #52-#66 adapters must map final/error/native session data only through canonical `result.v1`.
- #98 owns lifecycle/reconciliation states.
- #81-#84 own integrated binary/readback evidence.

## Evidence

- Exact event ordering fixture.
- Final text/path and native-session fixture.

- Binary-level JSON detail artifact.
- Zero-write/zero-dispatch proof.

Parent: #37

## Purpose

Replace fragile text-based boundary checks with a Go import graph boundary check.

Why this contributes: it makes the core/adapter split auditable and prevents hidden coupling from reducing the value of the reusable completion core.

## Current gap

`boundary_check.py` checks required files and forbidden strings in `lib/jpcmp/core/*.go`, but it does not parse the actual Go import graph.

## Required work

- Add a check that reads Go packages/imports under `packages/auto-complete`.
- Fail if any package under `lib/jpcmp/core` imports `adapters/*`, `app/*`, `cmd/*`, `adapters/transport/lsp`, Vim, Helix, JSONL source adapter packages, or OS/file parsing packages not explicitly allowed.
- Fail if `lib/jpcmp/ports` imports concrete source/transport/editor adapters.
- Keep source adapters allowed to import `lib/jpcmp/core` and `lib/jpcmp/ports`.

## False-positive prevention

The rule must be package-path based, not substring based. It should allow standard library imports that are intentionally part of core.

## False-negative prevention

Add a fixture or test mode that would fail if a forbidden import is introduced.

## Done when

- CI runs the import graph check.
- `core -> adapters/app/cmd` imports are mechanically rejected.
- `ports -> concrete adapters` imports are mechanically rejected.

Parent: #37

## Purpose

Replace fragile text-based boundary checks with a Go import graph boundary check.

Why this contributes: it makes the core/adapter split auditable and prevents hidden coupling from reducing the value of the reusable completion core.

## Current gap

`boundary_check.py` checks required files and forbidden strings in `lib/jpcmp/core/*.go`, but it does not parse the actual Go import graph.

## Required work

- Add a check that reads Go packages/imports under `packages/auto-complete`.
- Fail if any package under `lib/jpcmp/core` imports `adapters/*`, `app/*`, `cmd/*`, `adapters/transport/lsp`, Vim, Helix, JSONL source adapter packages, or OS/file parsing packages not explicitly allowed.
- Fail if `lib/jpcmp/ports` imports concrete source/transport/editor adapters.
- Keep source adapters allowed to import `lib/jpcmp/core` and `lib/jpcmp/ports`.

## False-positive prevention

The rule must be package-path based, not substring based. It should allow standard library imports that are intentionally part of core.

## False-negative prevention

Add a fixture or test mode that would fail if a forbidden import is introduced.

## Done when

- CI runs the import graph check.
- `core -> adapters/app/cmd` imports are mechanically rejected.
- `ports -> concrete adapters` imports are mechanically rejected.

Decide whether it contains at least one statement presented as a specification or operative contract: a rule, expected or acceptable condition, responsibility, functional capability, input/output mapping, interface purpose, or condition or limitation of use. A stated expected-outcome caption or interface text declaring an action's purpose can qualify. No formal specification label, generality, adoption, implementation, must-word or future tense is required. Distinguish the role of the relationship being stated. Declaring what a function does or what condition applies counts; merely describing what happened, is happening, used to happen or regularly happens in observed execution does not by itself declare a specification. A performed configuration, measured value, comparison or causal explanation does not supply an unstated applicable contract. These are role distinctions, not rules excluding particular headings, formats, tenses or words: a report may also contain a genuine specification, and an ordinary capability statement can declare one without requesting a change. Read each statement in context; one qualifying declaration anywhere is sufficient and observations elsewhere do not cancel it. Quoted or hypothetical text counts when used to declare the specification, but not when displayed only as an illustration. Synthetic contrast: 'This dial sets the sampling interval' declares a function; 'I turned the dial and the reading changed' alone reports an observation. A request or a subject's goal alone does not establish this specification role. Do not consult external content.

options.yes: The complete body contains at least one statement presented as a specification or operative contract of the kind defined in the instruction. It declares the relationship itself; merely reporting a performed action, observed configuration or value, observed result, or a causal explanation of an observed event does not by itself establish that role. A genuine declaration still counts inside a report, quotation or template when the body uses it to declare that relationship.
options.no: The complete body contains no statement presented as a specification or operative contract of the kind defined in the instruction. Answer no only for absence throughout the body; observations elsewhere do not cancel a genuine declaration.

request.instruction: Read only the complete literal body, including HTML comments, tables, formulas and templates. Decide whether it contains at least one genuine request for an action, answer, submission, improvement or remedy, or explicitly presents an action or state as a subject's intended goal or need. Count indirect requests and actual conditional reporting or submission directions, including directions carried by a template or HTML comment whether or not the requested information has been supplied. No addressee, stated reason, fully identified final goal, solution, adoption or implementation is required. Distinguish a relationship presented as a target or request from wording that only locates the circumstances of a reported event or explains a necessary response to it. An incident, inability, missing feature, risk, complaint, category or recipient mention alone does not declare the desired opposite or request its correction. Merely explaining what was necessary to obtain an observed result or work around it does not by itself declare an intended goal. Do not exclude a genuine goal or request merely because it appears within a report or a subordinate clause; do not infer one solely from modality, tense, a heading, mention, imperative form or question mark. A specification or expected caption alone does not establish this request or subject-goal role. One qualifying statement anywhere is sufficient and observations elsewhere do not cancel it. Quoted or hypothetical text counts when the body uses it to make an actual request or goal declaration, but not when shown only as an illustration. Synthetic contrast: 'I need a cost estimate before ordering the materials' declares a goal or need; 'The estimate arrived late, so I postponed the order' alone reports an event and response. Do not consult external content.

options.yes: The complete body contains at least one genuine request or declaration of a subject's intended goal or need of the kind defined in the instruction. This includes actual reporting or submission directions before the requested information is supplied. Merely naming a category or recipient, reporting an incident or inability, or explaining a necessary workaround does not itself establish this role.
options.no: The complete body contains no genuine request or declaration of a subject's intended goal or need of the kind defined in the instruction. Answer no only for absence throughout the body; a report or subordinate clause does not cancel an actual request or goal.

{"body":"## 背景 手元の約10年前のVersaPro（Core i5 / RAM 8GB / SSD 256GB）はOS消去可。LLM推論は外部APIに任せ、開発・内部エージェントの常設ホストをVPSから自宅機へ移せるか検討する。固定費を減らし、既存Nix/package・Cloudflare接続・envsの責務を再利用する。VersaProは物理NixOSのown′で、#8が扱う別rent端末と独立する。 ## 合意した完成状態（2026-10-08） 1. **対象・導入**：VersaProは#8の別rent端末と独立した物理NixOS常設own′。USBから初回導入する。2026-10-09のUser追加指定により、内蔵SSDへNixOSを常設インストールし、Windowsは消去して起動OSをNixOSのみとする。導入後はUSBを外した状態でBIOSから内蔵SSDのNixOSが起動し、手元での対話ログオン・コマンド入力なしにネットワークと認可SSH管理が復帰することを確認する。USB live環境の起動・SSH成功だけを常設インストール完了とは扱わない。常設OSと初回・復旧installerは、GitHubで管理する非秘密の宣言と固定pin/lockから別outputとして再生成できることを求める。flakeまたは同等に再現可能なsourceを使い、既存own/rentのpinやoutputsを変更しない。以後は同じ非秘密の宣言によるrebuildを通常更新とする。 2. **接続**：Userの追加指定により、USB boot後の確認・インストール・設定・以後の管理はG6I3からのSSHを前提とする。VersaPro側でのコマンド入力・対話パスワード設定・GUI操作に依存せず、USB boot後にネットワーク・sshd・指定管理者の公開鍵認証が成立する状態を準備する。初回のネットワーク・SSH管理到達を確保し、導入後は意図したCloudflare Mesh内の既存クライアントからown′を認可SSHで管理できることを目標にする。NixOSでその到達性を満たす接続・登録方式は未確認。未登録経路に初回bootstrapを依存させず、別経路のSSH成功をMesh要望の達成と読み替えない。 3. **状態・復旧**：宣言と必要なwork/auth/session・端末状態を分け、有効な認証と必要状態をrebuild/再起動で保持する。期限切れ・失効・鍵/状態喪失は別の復旧で、主体・必要な保管物または正規再登録/再認証先・復旧後の実利用を明確にする。LAN/USBでOSへ入れたことだけを認証復旧としない。鍵方式は未採択。 4. **常設利用**：電源投入・通常再起動・設定/有効認証を保持した回線再接続後、対話ログオンなしに管理経路が復帰し、外部SSHと必要な代表エージェント一件を実利用できることを確認する。全agentの自動常駐や全session自動再開は求めない。停電後の自動power-onは別の実機能力で未確認。 Codex / Pi / OpenCode等の必要なエージェントとGitHub認証を初回設定後に保持・復旧できることを目標とする。非秘密の宣言・配布用起動ISO・Git・ログへ秘密を混入させない。2026-10-09のUser明示許可により、初回接続用Wi-Fi設定とUSB起動専用SSHホスト秘密鍵は、配布用ISOと分けた私用USB設定領域へ保存する。この例外を管理者SSH秘密鍵・provider資格情報・常設ホストのage鍵へ広げない。8GBでの必要workload、電力、故障・停電・回線障害の影響を評価し、VPS代替の可否を判断する。全エージェントの同時常駐や全障害の故意再現を追加条件にしない。 ```mermaid flowchart TB U["USB boot・自動ネットワーク・公開鍵SSH"] --> I["G6I3からSSHで内蔵SSDへNixOS導入
Windows消去・初回登録"] I --> SBOOT["USBなしでBIOSからSSDのNixOSのみ起動"] SBOOT --> H["ログイン不要の管理経路"] C["意図したMesh内の既存クライアント"] --> H H --> V["認可SSH・必要な代表agent実利用"] D["同じ非秘密の宣言"] --> R["rebuild"] --> H S["必要状態・有効な認証"] --> H B["電源投入・通常再起動・通常再接続"] --> H X["失効・鍵/状態喪失"] --> F["復旧主体・保管物/正規再登録"] F --> Q["認証と状態を復旧・実利用で確認"] --> S ``` ## host / repoの関係 以下は導入・運用の役割図。破線はこれから成立させる関係であり、実接続や配備成功を表さない。G6I3は現在USBを準備するWindows host、NixOSのインストール先はVersaPro。USBをG6I3に挿しただけではVersaProへの導入は始まらない。初回ネットワークはUSB boot後のLinuxがG6I3からのSSHと必要な取得先へ接続できることを指す。有線LANそのものは必須ではないが、手元コマンドに依存せず接続できる方式を準備する。SSHは初回から必須で、VersaProの手元画面・キーボードでインストールする経路は完成形に含めない。envsは#14が定める既存の接続・secret配置責務を指し、現在のrepository locatorは実装前に再確認する。 ```mermaid flowchart TB subgraph REPO["リポジトリの責務"] A["adrs
採択済み規約・責任境界"] W["windows
OS・package定義 / CI
VersaPro定義はこれから"] E["envsの既存責務
接続登録・secret配置"] A --> W A --> E end subgraph HOST["物理ホスト"] G["G6I3 / このWindows host
USB準備・遠隔管理"] V["VersaPro / own′
NixOS常設の導入対象"] T["PC7337 / 別rent
Windows + 既存OCI"] end O["NixOS標準installerを基に
公開鍵SSH・初回接続を準備"] U["I-O DATA 8GB USB
修正版1.59GB全量一致
正常ポートcold boot / 自動SSH PASS"] M["Cloudflare Mesh内の
既存クライアント"] O -. 取得して準備 .-> G G -->|修正USB準備・全量一致| U U -->|正常ポートで修正版cold boot PASS| V W -. 必要な定義・package / rebuild .-> V W -->|既存OCIの配布| T E -. 採用経路を確認して登録・配置 .-> V E -->|既存接続・配置の責務| T G -->|修正版自動Wi-Fi / strict SSH PASS| V M -. 要求する認可SSH / 接続方式未確認 .-> V ``` ## 小ささと未確認 要件の4点補完は構成部品を増やさず会話依存を減らす、という3者の設計合意。実装の小ささ・美しさは未証明で、宣言・保存物・権限・起動依存・手作業・初回/通常/復旧の運用分岐の総量と実利用で評価する。専用ISO、disko/nixos-anywhere、OCI追加、二重connector、追加helper、恒久台帳、固定ファイル数を先に必須化しない。現行の共通package profileは再利用候補であり、物理NixOSの完成定義が既にあるとは扱わない。 実機でBIOSによるUSB起動、USB Wi-Fi認識・接続、G6I3からのホスト鍵固定・公開鍵認証SSHを確認済み。未確認は常設SSDへの導入・通常起動、蓋/suspend・停電後自動power-on、NixOSで必要なMesh到達性を満たす接続/登録方式、必要状態と復旧用保管、8GBの実負荷。端末age鍵を使うか・どこへ復旧用保管するかも未採択。 ## 次の段階と作用境界 I-O DATA製8GB（作成hostでF:「UBUNTU」だった媒体）は、User許可後にWindowsから直接書込みし、1,589,706,752 bytesの全量読み戻し一致を確認済み。D:「EXTERNAL」500GBは対象外。当初はF7起動一覧で全USBポートを試してもUSBが表示されなかったが、その後、Userの実機写真で `versapro-installer` のUSB起動を確認した。設定領域 `NIXOSCONF` の通常mountは `/dev/sdb3: Can't open blockdev` で失敗し、Userの手元で読み取り専用loop mountを実行して `/run/bootstrap` へのmountに成功した。続けて初回Wi-Fi profileを生成・接続し、LANアドレス `192.168.0.104` を取得した。その後G6I3から、準備したホスト鍵を固定したstrict SSHと既存管理鍵による公開鍵認証でrootログインに成功した。実機はBIOS boot、RAM 7.7GiB、内蔵SSDは223.6GiBで既存NTFS領域が残っている。実機SSHから、設定領域のby-label deviceへ `ro,loop,nosuid,nodev,noexec,umask=0077` を指定する標準mountを一時的な別mountpointで検証し、成功・ファイル存在を確認して解除した。元のSSH用mountと接続は維持した。ローカルinstaller宣言へ `loop` optionを追加し、Nix構文検査が通過した。2026-10-09に同じUSBがG6I3へ戻された。`loop`と`noCheck=true`を実宣言へ反映した新ISOの生成は正常完了し、P/R/Wが実生成物・起動構造・設定分離・書込用イメージを確認した。識別済みUSBへ1,589,706,752 bytesを書込み、全量読み戻ししたが比較は不一致となった。独立した読み取り照合で360 bytes/15か所の差分を確認し、USB私用設定領域は全量一致、差分は公開起動領域と末尾領域に限定された。2026-10-11に実adapterの64KiB転送上限とGUID一覧に出ないUSB領域の対応を確認し、既存writerへ上限内direct I/Oと実partition binding・2領域lock/dismountを組み込んだ。修正宣言・ISO・私用イメージは再生成せず、Rが実sourceを独立評価した後、同じUSBへ1,589,706,752 bytesを書込み・全量照合し、差分0/処理exit 0を確認、Rも媒体checkpoint PASSとした（[実結果と修正ループ](https://github.com/roccho-dev/resources/issues/58#issuecomment-6249432717)）。UserがWi-Fiアダプタを正常な本体ポートへ、電源OFF状態で差し替えて電源ONした後、192.168.0.103へP/Rが既存管理鍵と固定USBホスト鍵によるstrict SSHで独立接続した。修正版pg1、設定領域の自動ro/loop mount、Wi-Fi/NM/sshd、設定生成成功を実確認し、RはUSB修正jobをMissing=[]で受入した。手元Linux入力は不要だった。正常なポート配置での起動を使用条件として記録し、追加再起動・再build・kernel変更は不要。これはUSB live/bootstrapの完成であり、常設SSDの導入・GitHub常設flake・Mesh等の完成へ広げない。SSD消去・インストールは未実施。USB HDDは既に起動順位1位で、順位の再変更や書込方法の再質問を次工程にしない。標準installerの起動後に手元で鍵配置/password設定を要求する構成では今回のSSH前提を満たさないため、標準NixOS installerの機能を使い、公開鍵認証・sshd・初回自動ネットワークを必要最小限で準備する。管理者SSH秘密鍵・provider資格情報はUSB起動環境へ混入させない。USB起動専用SSHホスト秘密鍵の私用設定領域への保存は2026-10-09にUserが明示許可した。その後、対象を特定したUSB書込み、VersaProでのUSB boot、G6I3からのstrict SSH到達、SSH経由の実disk/NIC/boot確認、最小NixOS定義の実装・評価、インストールと初回登録/認証、rebuild/再起動/遠隔実利用の確認へ進む。各作用の許可と実証を分け、今回の図の保存をUSB消去、実機初期化、秘密移送、設定変更、VPS停止のGOにしない。 ## 次工程の設計協議（2026-10-09） Pと継続中のVersaPro設計担当A/Bが相互反証し、[工程・組成・復旧の結論とMermaid](https://github.com/roccho-dev/resources/issues/58#issuecomment-6249432642)に収束した。現SSHで宣言/最小systemを準備し、SSD消去前にだけ修正USBの実cold boot→手元Linux操作0のstrict SSHを確認する。対象SSD・BIOS boot・必要保全・対象作用許可を確認後、標準install→恒久公開host鍵pin→USBなしSSD単独boot→同source rebuild/再起動と必要状態/認証/代表agentの継続を実証する。Meshは別受入とする。 PR #612](https://github.com/roccho-dev/adrs/pull/612)のexact complete commit `9d77544a2ad45b12bc2bd2b30da83ee1e643bc96`へ保存した。同版をP/R/Wが全graph・entry state.body:
## 背景 手元の約10年前のVersaPro（Core i5 / RAM 8GB / SSD 256GB）はOS消去可。LLM推論は外部APIに任せ、開発・内部エージェントの常設ホストをVPSから自宅機へ移せるか検討する。固定費を減らし、既存Nix/package・Cloudflare接続・envsの責務を再利用する。VersaProは物理NixOSのown′で、#8が扱う別rent端末と独立する。 ## 合意した完成状態（2026-10-08） 1. **対象・導入**：VersaProは#8の別rent端末と独立した物理NixOS常設own′。USBから初回導入する。2026-10-09のUser追加指定により、内蔵SSDへNixOSを常設インストールし、Windowsは消去して起動OSをNixOSのみとする。導入後はUSBを外した状態でBIOSから内蔵SSDのNixOSが起動し、手元での対話ログオン・コマンド入力なしにネットワークと認可SSH管理が復帰することを確認する。USB live環境の起動・SSH成功だけを常設インストール完了とは扱わない。常設OSと初回・復旧installerは、GitHubで管理する非秘密の宣言と固定pin/lockから別outputとして再生成できることを求める。flakeまたは同等に再現可能なsourceを使い、既存own/rentのpinやoutputsを変更しない。以後は同じ非秘密の宣言によるrebuildを通常更新とする。 2. **接続**：Userの追加指定により、USB boot後の確認・インストール・設定・以後の管理はG6I3からのSSHを前提とする。VersaPro側でのコマンド入力・対話パスワード設定・GUI操作に依存せず、USB boot後にネットワーク・sshd・指定管理者の公開鍵認証が成立する状態を準備する。初回のネットワーク・SSH管理到達を確保し、導入後は意図したCloudflare Mesh内の既存クライアントからown′を認可SSHで管理できることを目標にする。NixOSでその到達性を満たす接続・登録方式は未確認。未登録経路に初回bootstrapを依存させず、別経路のSSH成功をMesh要望の達成と読み替えない。 3. **状態・復旧**：宣言と必要なwork/auth/session・端末状態を分け、有効な認証と必要状態をrebuild/再起動で保持する。期限切れ・失効・鍵/状態喪失は別の復旧で、主体・必要な保管物または正規再登録/再認証先・復旧後の実利用を明確にする。LAN/USBでOSへ入れたことだけを認証復旧としない。鍵方式は未採択。 4. **常設利用**：電源投入・通常再起動・設定/有効認証を保持した回線再接続後、対話ログオンなしに管理経路が復帰し、外部SSHと必要な代表エージェント一件を実利用できることを確認する。全agentの自動常駐や全session自動再開は求めない。停電後の自動power-onは別の実機能力で未確認。 Codex / Pi / OpenCode等の必要なエージェントとGitHub認証を初回設定後に保持・復旧できることを目標とする。非秘密の宣言・配布用起動ISO・Git・ログへ秘密を混入させない。2026-10-09のUser明示許可により、初回接続用Wi-Fi設定とUSB起動専用SSHホスト秘密鍵は、配布用ISOと分けた私用USB設定領域へ保存する。この例外を管理者SSH秘密鍵・provider資格情報・常設ホストのage鍵へ広げない。8GBでの必要workload、電力、故障・停電・回線障害の影響を評価し、VPS代替の可否を判断する。全エージェントの同時常駐や全障害の故意再現を追加条件にしない。 ```mermaid flowchart TB U["USB boot・自動ネットワーク・公開鍵SSH"] --> I["G6I3からSSHで内蔵SSDへNixOS導入
Windows消去・初回登録"] I --> SBOOT["USBなしでBIOSからSSDのNixOSのみ起動"] SBOOT --> H["ログイン不要の管理経路"] C["意図したMesh内の既存クライアント"] --> H H --> V["認可SSH・必要な代表agent実利用"] D["同じ非秘密の宣言"] --> R["rebuild"] --> H S["必要状態・有効な認証"] --> H B["電源投入・通常再起動・通常再接続"] --> H X["失効・鍵/状態喪失"] --> F["復旧主体・保管物/正規再登録"] F --> Q["認証と状態を復旧・実利用で確認"] --> S ``` ## host / repoの関係 以下は導入・運用の役割図。破線はこれから成立させる関係であり、実接続や配備成功を表さない。G6I3は現在USBを準備するWindows host、NixOSのインストール先はVersaPro。USBをG6I3に挿しただけではVersaProへの導入は始まらない。初回ネットワークはUSB boot後のLinuxがG6I3からのSSHと必要な取得先へ接続できることを指す。有線LANそのものは必須ではないが、手元コマンドに依存せず接続できる方式を準備する。SSHは初回から必須で、VersaProの手元画面・キーボードでインストールする経路は完成形に含めない。envsは#14が定める既存の接続・secret配置責務を指し、現在のrepository locatorは実装前に再確認する。 ```mermaid flowchart TB subgraph REPO["リポジトリの責務"] A["adrs
採択済み規約・責任境界"] W["windows
OS・package定義 / CI
VersaPro定義はこれから"] E["envsの既存責務
接続登録・secret配置"] A --> W A --> E end subgraph HOST["物理ホスト"] G["G6I3 / このWindows host
USB準備・遠隔管理"] V["VersaPro / own′
NixOS常設の導入対象"] T["PC7337 / 別rent
Windows + 既存OCI"] end O["NixOS標準installerを基に
公開鍵SSH・初回接続を準備"] U["I-O DATA 8GB USB
修正版1.59GB全量一致
正常ポートcold boot / 自動SSH PASS"] M["Cloudflare Mesh内の
既存クライアント"] O -. 取得して準備 .-> G G -->|修正USB準備・全量一致| U U -->|正常ポートで修正版cold boot PASS| V W -. 必要な定義・package / rebuild .-> V W -->|既存OCIの配布| T E -. 採用経路を確認して登録・配置 .-> V E -->|既存接続・配置の責務| T G -->|修正版自動Wi-Fi / strict SSH PASS| V M -. 要求する認可SSH / 接続方式未確認 .-> V ``` ## 小ささと未確認 要件の4点補完は構成部品を増やさず会話依存を減らす、という3者の設計合意。実装の小ささ・美しさは未証明で、宣言・保存物・権限・起動依存・手作業・初回/通常/復旧の運用分岐の総量と実利用で評価する。専用ISO、disko/nixos-anywhere、OCI追加、二重connector、追加helper、恒久台帳、固定ファイル数を先に必須化しない。現行の共通package profileは再利用候補であり、物理NixOSの完成定義が既にあるとは扱わない。 実機でBIOSによるUSB起動、USB Wi-Fi認識・接続、G6I3からのホスト鍵固定・公開鍵認証SSHを確認済み。未確認は常設SSDへの導入・通常起動、蓋/suspend・停電後自動power-on、NixOSで必要なMesh到達性を満たす接続/登録方式、必要状態と復旧用保管、8GBの実負荷。端末age鍵を使うか・どこへ復旧用保管するかも未採択。 ## 次の段階と作用境界 I-O DATA製8GB（作成hostでF:「UBUNTU」だった媒体）は、User許可後にWindowsから直接書込みし、1,589,706,752 bytesの全量読み戻し一致を確認済み。D:「EXTERNAL」500GBは対象外。当初はF7起動一覧で全USBポートを試してもUSBが表示されなかったが、その後、Userの実機写真で `versapro-installer` のUSB起動を確認した。設定領域 `NIXOSCONF` の通常mountは `/dev/sdb3: Can't open blockdev` で失敗し、Userの手元で読み取り専用loop mountを実行して `/run/bootstrap` へのmountに成功した。続けて初回Wi-Fi profileを生成・接続し、LANアドレス `192.168.0.104` を取得した。その後G6I3から、準備したホスト鍵を固定したstrict SSHと既存管理鍵による公開鍵認証でrootログインに成功した。実機はBIOS boot、RAM 7.7GiB、内蔵SSDは223.6GiBで既存NTFS領域が残っている。実機SSHから、設定領域のby-label deviceへ `ro,loop,nosuid,nodev,noexec,umask=0077` を指定する標準mountを一時的な別mountpointで検証し、成功・ファイル存在を確認して解除した。元のSSH用mountと接続は維持した。ローカルinstaller宣言へ `loop` optionを追加し、Nix構文検査が通過した。2026-10-09に同じUSBがG6I3へ戻された。`loop`と`noCheck=true`を実宣言へ反映した新ISOの生成は正常完了し、P/R/Wが実生成物・起動構造・設定分離・書込用イメージを確認した。識別済みUSBへ1,589,706,752 bytesを書込み、全量読み戻ししたが比較は不一致となった。独立した読み取り照合で360 bytes/15か所の差分を確認し、USB私用設定領域は全量一致、差分は公開起動領域と末尾領域に限定された。2026-10-11に実adapterの64KiB転送上限とGUID一覧に出ないUSB領域の対応を確認し、既存writerへ上限内direct I/Oと実partition binding・2領域lock/dismountを組み込んだ。修正宣言・ISO・私用イメージは再生成せず、Rが実sourceを独立評価した後、同じUSBへ1,589,706,752 bytesを書込み・全量照合し、差分0/処理exit 0を確認、Rも媒体checkpoint PASSとした（[実結果と修正ループ](https://github.com/roccho-dev/resources/issues/58#issuecomment-6249432717)）。UserがWi-Fiアダプタを正常な本体ポートへ、電源OFF状態で差し替えて電源ONした後、192.168.0.103へP/Rが既存管理鍵と固定USBホスト鍵によるstrict SSHで独立接続した。修正版pg1、設定領域の自動ro/loop mount、Wi-Fi/NM/sshd、設定生成成功を実確認し、RはUSB修正jobをMissing=[]で受入した。手元Linux入力は不要だった。正常なポート配置での起動を使用条件として記録し、追加再起動・再build・kernel変更は不要。これはUSB live/bootstrapの完成であり、常設SSDの導入・GitHub常設flake・Mesh等の完成へ広げない。SSD消去・インストールは未実施。USB HDDは既に起動順位1位で、順位の再変更や書込方法の再質問を次工程にしない。標準installerの起動後に手元で鍵配置/password設定を要求する構成では今回のSSH前提を満たさないため、標準NixOS installerの機能を使い、公開鍵認証・sshd・初回自動ネットワークを必要最小限で準備する。管理者SSH秘密鍵・provider資格情報はUSB起動環境へ混入させない。USB起動専用SSHホスト秘密鍵の私用設定領域への保存は2026-10-09にUserが明示許可した。その後、対象を特定したUSB書込み、VersaProでのUSB boot、G6I3からのstrict SSH到達、SSH経由の実disk/NIC/boot確認、最小NixOS定義の実装・評価、インストールと初回登録/認証、rebuild/再起動/遠隔実利用の確認へ進む。各作用の許可と実証を分け、今回の図の保存をUSB消去、実機初期化、秘密移送、設定変更、VPS停止のGOにしない。 ## 次工程の設計協議（2026-10-09） Pと継続中のVersaPro設計担当A/Bが相互反証し、[工程・組成・復旧の結論とMermaid](https://github.com/roccho-dev/resources/issues/58#issuecomment-6249432642)に収束した。現SSHで宣言/最小systemを準備し、SSD消去前にだけ修正USBの実cold boot→手元Linux操作0のstrict SSHを確認する。対象SSD・BIOS boot・必要保全・対象作用許可を確認後、標準install→恒久公開host鍵pin→USBなしSSD単独boot→同source rebuild/再起動と必要状態/認証/代表agentの継続を実証する。Meshは別受入とする。 Windows消去・初回登録"] I --> SBOOT["USBなしでBIOSからSSDのNixOSのみ起動"] SBOOT --> H["ログイン不要の管理経路"] C["意図したMesh内の既存クライアント"] --> H H --> V["認可SSH・必要な代表agent実利用"] D["同じ非秘密の宣言"] --> R["rebuild"] --> H S["必要状態・有効な認証"] --> H B["電源投入・通常再起動・通常再接続"] --> H X["失効・鍵/状態喪失"] --> F["復旧主体・保管物/正規再登録"] F --> Q["認証と状態を復旧・実利用で確認"] --> S ``` ## host / repoの関係 以下は導入・運用の役割図。破線はこれから成立させる関係であり、実接続や配備成功を表さない。G6I3は現在USBを準備するWindows host、NixOSのインストール先はVersaPro。USBをG6I3に挿しただけではVersaProへの導入は始まらない。初回ネットワークはUSB boot後のLinuxがG6I3からのSSHと必要な取得先へ接続できることを指す。有線LANそのものは必須ではないが、手元コマンドに依存せず接続できる方式を準備する。SSHは初回から必須で、VersaProの手元画面・キーボードでインストールする経路は完成形に含めない。envsは#14が定める既存の接続・secret配置責務を指し、現在のrepository locatorは実装前に再確認する。 ```mermaid flowchart TB subgraph REPO["リポジトリの責務"] A["adrs

要件の4点補完は構成部品を増やさず会話依存を減らす、という3者の設計合意。実装の小ささ・美しさは未証明で、宣言・保存物・権限・起動依存・手作業・初回/通常/復旧の運用分岐の総量と実利用で評価する。専用ISO、disko/nixos-anywhere、OCI追加、二重connector、追加helper、恒久台帳、固定ファイル数を先に必須化しない。現行の共通package profileは再利用候補であり、物理NixOSの完成定義が既にあるとは扱わない。 実機でBIOSによるUSB起動、USB Wi-Fi認識・接続、G6I3からのホスト鍵固定・公開鍵認証SSHを確認済み。未確認は常設SSDへの導入・通常起動、蓋/suspend・停電後自動power-on、NixOSで必要なMesh到達性を満たす接続/登録方式、必要状態と復旧用保管、8GBの実負荷。端末age鍵を使うか・どこへ復旧用保管するかも未採択。 ## 次の段階と作用境界 I-O DATA製8GB（作成hostでF:「UBUNTU」だった媒体）は、User許可後にWindowsから直接書込みし、1,589,706,752 bytesの全量読み戻し一致を確認済み。D:「EXTERNAL」500GBは対象外。当初はF7起動一覧で全USBポートを試してもUSBが表示されなかったが、その後、Userの実機写真で `versapro-installer` のUSB起動を確認した。設定領域 `NIXOSCONF` の通常mountは `/dev/sdb3: Can't open blockdev` で失敗し、Userの手元で読み取り専用loop mountを実行して `/run/bootstrap` へのmountに成功した。続けて初回Wi-Fi profileを生成・接続し、LANアドレス `192.168.0.104` を取得した。その後G6I3から、準備したホスト鍵を固定したstrict SSHと既存管理鍵による公開鍵認証でrootログインに成功した。実機はBIOS boot、RAM 7.7GiB、内蔵SSDは223.6GiBで既存NTFS領域が残っている。実機SSHから、設定領域のby-label deviceへ `ro,loop,nosuid,nodev,noexec,umask=0077` を指定する標準mountを一時的な別mountpointで検証し、成功・ファイル存在を確認して解除した。元のSSH用mountと接続は維持した。ローカルinstaller宣言へ `loop` optionを追加し、Nix構文検査が通過した。2026-10-09に同じUSBがG6I3へ戻された。`loop`と`noCheck=true`を実宣言へ反映した新ISOの生成は正常完了し、P/R/Wが実生成物・起動構造・設定分離・書込用イメージを確認した。識別済みUSBへ1,589,706,752 bytesを書込み、全量読み戻ししたが比較は不一致となった。独立した読み取り照合で360 bytes/15か所の差分を確認し、USB私用設定領域は全量一致、差分は公開起動領域と末尾領域に限定された。2026-10-11に実adapterの64KiB転送上限とGUID一覧に出ないUSB領域の対応を確認し、既存writerへ上限内direct I/Oと実partition binding・2領域lock/dismountを組み込んだ。修正宣言・ISO・私用イメージは再生成せず、Rが実sourceを独立評価した後、同じUSBへ1,589,706,752 bytesを書込み・全量照合し、差分0/処理exit 0を確認、Rも媒体checkpoint PASSとした（[実結果と修正ループ](https://github.com/roccho-dev/resources/issues/58#issuecomment-6249432717)）。UserがWi-Fiアダプタを正常な本体ポートへ、電源OFF状態で差し替えて電源ONした後、192.168.0.103へP/Rが既存管理鍵と固定USBホスト鍵によるstrict SSHで独立接続した。修正版pg1、設定領域の自動ro/loop mount、Wi-Fi/NM/sshd、設定生成成功を実確認し、RはUSB修正jobをMissing=[]で受入した。手元Linux入力は不要だった。正常なポート配置での起動を使用条件として記録し、追加再起動・再build・kernel変更は不要。これはUSB live/bootstrapの完成であり、常設SSDの導入・GitHub常設flake・Mesh等の完成へ広げない。SSD消去・インストールは未実施。USB HDDは既に起動順位1位で、順位の再変更や書込方法の再質問を次工程にしない。標準installerの起動後に手元で鍵配置/password設定を要求する構成では今回のSSH前提を満たさないため、標準NixOS installerの機能を使い、公開鍵認証・sshd・初回自動ネットワークを必要最小限で準備する。管理者SSH秘密鍵・provider資格情報はUSB起動環境へ混入させない。USB起動専用SSHホスト秘密鍵の私用設定領域への保存は2026-10-09にUserが明示許可した。その後、対象を特定したUSB書込み、VersaProでのUSB boot、G6I3からのstrict SSH到達、SSH経由の実disk/NIC/boot確認、最小NixOS定義の実装・評価、インストールと初回登録/認証、rebuild/再起動/遠隔実利用の確認へ進む。各作用の許可と実証を分け、今回の図の保存をUSB消去、実機初期化、秘密移送、設定変更、VPS停止のGOにしない。 ## 次工程の設計協議（2026-10-09） Pと継続中のVersaPro設計担当A/Bが相互反証し、[工程・組成・復旧の結論とMermaid](https://github.com/roccho-dev/resources/issues/58#issuecomment-6249432642)に収束した。現SSHで宣言/最小systemを準備し、SSD消去前にだけ修正USBの実cold boot→手元Linux操作0のstrict SSHを確認する。対象SSD・BIOS boot・必要保全・対象作用許可を確認後、標準install→恒久公開host鍵pin→USBなしSSD単独boot→同source rebuild/再起動と必要状態/認証/代表agentの継続を実証する。Meshは別受入とする。 組織の役割契約は存在する。2026-10-09のUser明示許可により、既存A=/root/versapro_minimal_designを継続W、B=/root/versapro_operabilityを独立Rへそのまま割り当てた。当該scopeのCodex代替はUser許可済みで、P=/rootが調整Dを兼務する。W/Rの直接反証とPの最終補正を経て、[完成tree・数式・有限検証一覧・復旧表・閉包プロセス](https://github.com/roccho-dev/resources/issues/58#issuecomment-6249432678)の全節に3者合意した。未解消の設計反証は0。USB修正の限定scopeについて、必要なsource/admission・controlの実在担当/限定job登録を[adrs PR #612](https://github.com/roccho-dev/adrs/pull/612)のexact complete commit `9d77544a2ad45b12bc2bd2b30da83ee1e643bc96`へ保存した。同版をP/R/Wが全graph・entry SQL・原文readbackで独立確認し、Pが同版GOを出した。これは当該USBの生成・識別付き更新・読み戻し・実cold boot確認の作用に限定し、SSD消去/install・merge・VPS停止や全完成状態の採択/実機受入へ広げない。小ささは一組の宣言・標準機能・最小状態/分岐で評価し、実装の美しさは実source・実機証拠まで未判定。 ## 合意根拠 [3者の最終結論](https://github.com/roccho-dev/resources/issues/58#issuecomment-6249432484) / [Aの最終結論](https://github.com/roccho-dev/resources/issues/58#issuecomment-6249432438) / [Bの最終結論](https://github.com/roccho-dev/resources/issues/58#issuecomment-6249432388)。 本文は合意済み完成状態の参照先、コメントは主張・反証の根拠として残す。3者議論後のUser追加指定「SSH前提・手元端末に依存しない」は上の接続と次段階へ反映した。実装・実機受入・VPS代替の最終採否は未完了。 関連: roccho-dev/resources#52（別rentを含むNix開発環境・認証）、#14（Cloudflare接続）。 SSH起動条件の根拠：[NixOS公式manual](https://nixos.org/manual/nixos/stable/)はinstallerのsshdが有効でも、loginには公開鍵配置またはpassword設定が必要と説明する。今回の手元操作不要条件では、その公開鍵と初回接続をUSB準備段階で成立させる。 "}

body内の各文を、望ましい状態の宣言と、実際に起きたことの報告に分けて読んでください。EとOは同時にyesでも構いません。Eは文書の主題や多数決ではなく存在判定です。具体的な要求文・完成条件・目標文が一文でもあれば、残りが全部作業報告でもE=yesです。例えば「利用者に完了を通知すること」は期待ですが、「利用者に通知した」は実施報告であり期待ではありません。Goal・Acceptanceという見出しそのものは期待文ではなく、その下に過去の実施報告しかなければE=noです。表・数式・役割が完成状態の対応を定義する場合も期待です。Oでは実測の引用・確認状況一覧・本文内HTMLコメントの作業メモも数えますが、架空の試験入力・条件付きの例は数えません。許容を表す「〜でもよい」や仮定・可能性だけを述べる文は、現状の報告ではありません。例えば「点検は後日でもよい」は許容条件ですが、「点検はまだしていない」は現在の状態の報告です。O=yesにするには、本文が現実にそうだと主張している箇所が必要です。与えられたbody全体だけを対象に判断し、そこにない現状を推測しないでください。
本問はEだけ：本文が実現すべき状態を一つでも宣言しているか。完成状態の表・責務・式も宣言である。Goal等の見出しだけでYesにしない。本文にそのような期待がなければNo。実施済みと書いてあるだけなら期待ではない。
