request.text:
{"body":"Parent architecture: `roccho-dev/adrs#260`

Related authority and transition boundaries: `roccho-dev/adrs#223`, `roccho-dev/adrs#238`

Provider evidence owner: future `roccho-dev/ops` GitHub approval-evidence Issue

Consumer boundary: future `roccho-dev/diagrams` waiver-receipt Issue

## Status and authority

Implementation Issue. It creates no accepted authority and may not start a mergeable implementation PR until `adrs#260` is Accepted with exact schemas and claim ceiling.

Until acceptance, this Issue may only refine fixtures, destructive cases, package ownership, and fail-closed interfaces.

## Purpose

Implement one provider-neutral pure verifier:

```text
accepted authority grant
+ provider evidence envelope
+ exact candidate revision
+ exact subject/finding digest
+ exact policy digest
+ explicit as_of
+ exact engine
  -> approvalReceipt.v1
  -> VALID | INVALID | ERROR
```

The verifier determines whether an observed provider approval action is covered by one accepted authority grant. It does not call GitHub, mutate authority, approve a waiver, or identify a physical human.

## Repository ownership

Governance owns:

- closed schema validation;
- exact joins;
- authority-scope and validity evaluation;
- provider-neutral failure codes;
- deterministic receipt generation;
- positive and destructive fixtures;
- proof and Nix packaging.

Governance must not own:

- accepted authority grants or actor bindings;
- GitHub API calls or provider credentials;
- repository permission mutation;
- diagram waiver application;
- UI review state;
- physical-human identity claims.

## Inputs

### Accepted authority grant

Must be the exact accepted ADRS record/release projection and identify:

```text
grant_id
subject_id
action_kinds[]
resource_scope
provider_bindings[]
valid_from
valid_until
status
grant_digest
accepted_decision_id
accepted_release_digest
```

### Provider evidence envelope

Provider-neutral outer requirements:

```text
provider
provider_object_ids
repository_identity
candidate_revision
action_kind
action_state
action_time
actor_provider_account_id
actor_provider_login
observed_at
provider_response_digest
evidence_schema
```

The initial adapter may emit `githubApprovalEvidence.v1`, but the verifier must not import GitHub clients or infer GitHub semantics outside the accepted envelope contract.

### Subject identity

```text
repository
candidate_revision
finding_digest or subject_digest
policy_digest
```

### Evaluation identity

```text
as_of
engine_version
engine_digest
schema_digests
```

No implicit wall clock is permitted.

## Exact joins

The verifier requires exactly one matching:

- accepted authority grant;
- provider account binding;
- action kind;
- closed resource scope;
- candidate revision;
- subject/finding digest;
- policy digest;
- action time inside grant interval;
- provider evidence digest;
- engine and schema set.

Missing, duplicate, conflicting, stale, superseded, or substituted inputs are not VALID.

## Output

Minimum deterministic `approvalReceipt.v1`:

```json
{
  "kind": "approvalReceipt.v1",
  "approval_id": "A-...",
  "subject": {
    "repository": "roccho-dev/diagrams",
    "candidate_revision": "...",
    "finding_digest": "sha256:...",
    "policy_digest": "sha256:..."
  },
  "actor": {
    "subject_id": "person-or-role:...",
    "provider": "github",
    "provider_account_id": 0,
    "provider_login": "..."
  },
  "action": {
    "kind": "pull_request_review.approve",
    "provider_review_id": 0,
    "state": "APPROVED",
    "submitted_at": "..."
  },
  "authority": {
    "grant_id": "G-...",
    "scope_digest": "sha256:...",
    "valid_from": "...",
    "valid_until": "..."
  },
  "provider_evidence_digest": "sha256:...",
  "engine_digest": "sha256:...",
  "as_of": "...",
  "status": "VALID",
  "findings": []
}
```

Terminal statuses:

```text
VALID
INVALID
ERROR
```

- `VALID`: all complete exact joins succeed.
- `INVALID`: complete deterministic evidence proves a contract violation.
- `ERROR`: validation cannot establish validity because input, schema, provenance, or engine is incomplete/ambiguous/unsupported.

`ERROR` must never be downgraded to INVALID warning or VALID.

## Failure codes

At minimum:

```text
ACTOR_BINDING_MISSING
ACTOR_PROVIDER_ID_MISMATCH
ACTOR_LOGIN_MISMATCH
AUTHORITY_GRANT_MISSING
AUTHORITY_GRANT_DUPLICATE
AUTHORITY_GRANT_INACTIVE
AUTHORITY_GRANT_EXPIRED
AUTHORITY_SCOPE_MISMATCH
ACTION_KIND_NOT_GRANTED
CANDIDATE_REVISION_MISMATCH
REVIEW_COMMIT_MISMATCH
SUBJECT_DIGEST_MISMATCH
POLICY_DIGEST_MISMATCH
REVIEW_STATE_NOT_APPROVED
REVIEW_DISMISSED
PROVIDER_EVIDENCE_MALFORMED
PROVIDER_EVIDENCE_DIGEST_MISMATCH
PROVIDER_OBJECT_ID_MISMATCH
ACTION_TIME_OUTSIDE_GRANT
AS_OF_MISSING
ENGINE_UNKNOWN
VALIDATION_EXCEPTION
```

Every finding must expose expected, actual, stable subject identifiers, owner, and next action where deterministically known.

## Package design

Prefer one bounded package within the existing governance package graph, for example:

```text
approval-receipt-verifier
```

Internal modules may separate:

```text
schema validation
exact joins
authority evaluation
receipt construction
fixtures / proof
```

Do not create provider-specific verifier packages in governance.

## Public API

One pure entry point is sufficient:

```text
validate_approval(
  authority_grants,
  provider_evidence,
  subject,
  as_of,
  engine_identity
) -> approvalReceipt.v1
```

Inputs and output must be serializable closed-schema values. No network, filesystem discovery, implicit environment variables, or current-time reads inside the evaluator.

## Acceptance gates

| Gate | Requirement |
|---|---|
| G1 Accepted input | exact Accepted ADRS #260 release is required |
| G2 Provider neutrality | no GitHub API/client/provider permission logic in verifier |
| G3 Exact actor | numeric provider account binding joins exactly once |
| G4 Exact revision | action binds the exact candidate revision |
| G5 Exact subject | finding/subject and policy digests match |
| G6 Historical authority | action time is inside accepted grant interval |
| G7 Closed scope | repository/resource/action are inside a closed grant scope |
| G8 Fail closed | incomplete, duplicate, conflicting, stale, or unknown input is not VALID |
| G9 Determinism | identical inputs produce byte-equivalent deterministic receipt fields |
| G10 Diagnostics | every INVALID/ERROR has an exact code and bounded evidence |
| G11 Nix | package build and `nix flake check` pass |
| G12 Exact head | all proof and existing repository checks pass on exact candidate/merge ref |
| G13 No authority drift | governance output remains evidence, not accepted meaning |
| G14 Claim ceiling | physical-human identity and account non-compromise remain false |

## Mandatory destructive cases

1. Login matches but numeric actor ID differs.
2. Numeric actor ID matches but accepted binding is absent.
3. Candidate revision differs.
4. Review/action state is not approved.
5. Review is dismissed.
6. Grant is not yet valid.
7. Grant expired before action.
8. Grant is inactive, revoked, or superseded.
9. Repository is outside scope.
10. Action kind is outside scope.
11. Finding/subject digest differs.
12. Policy digest differs.
13. Duplicate grants match ambiguously.
14. Provider evidence digest is substituted.
15. Provider object ID is substituted.
16. Current permission is used instead of accepted historical grant.
17. `as_of` is missing or implicit.
18. Engine or schema digest is unknown.
19. Verifier imports or calls a GitHub provider client.
20. Receipt claims physical-human identity, account non-compromise, or provider-independent non-repudiation.
21. Identical inputs produce different deterministic receipt bytes.
22. Validation exception is converted to VALID.

## PR design

Suggested PR title after ADRS acceptance:

```text
feat(approval): add pure exact-revision approval receipt verifier
```

The PR must:

- bind the exact ADRS Decision/release digest;
- add the package and closed schemas;
- include positive and destructive fixtures;
- emit deterministic proof artifacts;
- add Nix and exact-head CI;
- avoid provider/network implementation;
- use `Refs`, not `Closes`, until merged readback and consumer integration exist.

## Claim ceiling

The implementation may prove:

```text
providerNeutralVerifierImplemented=true
exactAuthorityGrantJoinProven=true
exactRevisionJoinProven=true
```

It must retain:

```text
githubEvidenceAdapterImplemented=false until ops merge
physicalHumanIdentityProven=false
accountNonCompromiseProven=false
allRepositoriesEnforced=false
businessOutcomeAchieved=false
corporateSaleOutcomeAchieved=false
```

## Closure

Close only after the exact Accepted ADRS #260 release is read, one valid GitHub-shaped fixture passes, all destructive cases fail with exact codes, Nix/exact-head CI pass, and merged governance readback preserves the receipt contract and claim ceiling."}

request.text:
{"body":"Parent architecture: `roccho-dev/adrs#260`

Related authority and transition boundaries: `roccho-dev/adrs#223`, `roccho-dev/adrs#238`

Provider evidence owner: future `roccho-dev/ops` GitHub approval-evidence Issue

Consumer boundary: future `roccho-dev/diagrams` waiver-receipt Issue

## Status and authority

Implementation Issue. It creates no accepted authority and may not start a mergeable implementation PR until `adrs#260` is Accepted with exact schemas and claim ceiling.

Until acceptance, this Issue may only refine fixtures, destructive cases, package ownership, and fail-closed interfaces.

## Purpose

Implement one provider-neutral pure verifier:

```text
accepted authority grant
+ provider evidence envelope
+ exact candidate revision
+ exact subject/finding digest
+ exact policy digest
+ explicit as_of
+ exact engine
  -> approvalReceipt.v1
  -> VALID | INVALID | ERROR
```

The verifier determines whether an observed provider approval action is covered by one accepted authority grant. It does not call GitHub, mutate authority, approve a waiver, or identify a physical human.

## Repository ownership

Governance owns:

- closed schema validation;
- exact joins;
- authority-scope and validity evaluation;
- provider-neutral failure codes;
- deterministic receipt generation;
- positive and destructive fixtures;
- proof and Nix packaging.

Governance must not own:

- accepted authority grants or actor bindings;
- GitHub API calls or provider credentials;
- repository permission mutation;
- diagram waiver application;
- UI review state;
- physical-human identity claims.

## Inputs

### Accepted authority grant

Must be the exact accepted ADRS record/release projection and identify:

```text
grant_id
subject_id
action_kinds[]
resource_scope
provider_bindings[]
valid_from
valid_until
status
grant_digest
accepted_decision_id
accepted_release_digest
```

### Provider evidence envelope

Provider-neutral outer requirements:

```text
provider
provider_object_ids
repository_identity
candidate_revision
action_kind
action_state
action_time
actor_provider_account_id
actor_provider_login
observed_at
provider_response_digest
evidence_schema
```

The initial adapter may emit `githubApprovalEvidence.v1`, but the verifier must not import GitHub clients or infer GitHub semantics outside the accepted envelope contract.

### Subject identity

```text
repository
candidate_revision
finding_digest or subject_digest
policy_digest
```

### Evaluation identity

```text
as_of
engine_version
engine_digest
schema_digests
```

No implicit wall clock is permitted.

## Exact joins

The verifier requires exactly one matching:

- accepted authority grant;
- provider account binding;
- action kind;
- closed resource scope;
- candidate revision;
- subject/finding digest;
- policy digest;
- action time inside grant interval;
- provider evidence digest;
- engine and schema set.

Missing, duplicate, conflicting, stale, superseded, or substituted inputs are not VALID.

## Output

Minimum deterministic `approvalReceipt.v1`:

```json
{
  "kind": "approvalReceipt.v1",
  "approval_id": "A-...",
  "subject": {
    "repository": "roccho-dev/diagrams",
    "candidate_revision": "...",
    "finding_digest": "sha256:...",
    "policy_digest": "sha256:..."
  },
  "actor": {
    "subject_id": "person-or-role:...",
    "provider": "github",
    "provider_account_id": 0,
    "provider_login": "..."
  },
  "action": {
    "kind": "pull_request_review.approve",
    "provider_review_id": 0,
    "state": "APPROVED",
    "submitted_at": "..."
  },
  "authority": {
    "grant_id": "G-...",
    "scope_digest": "sha256:...",
    "valid_from": "...",
    "valid_until": "..."
  },
  "provider_evidence_digest": "sha256:...",
  "engine_digest": "sha256:...",
  "as_of": "...",
  "status": "VALID",
  "findings": []
}
```

Terminal statuses:

```text
VALID
INVALID
ERROR
```

- `VALID`: all complete exact joins succeed.
- `INVALID`: complete deterministic evidence proves a contract violation.
- `ERROR`: validation cannot establish validity because input, schema, provenance, or engine is incomplete/ambiguous/unsupported.

`ERROR` must never be downgraded to INVALID warning or VALID.

## Failure codes

At minimum:

```text
ACTOR_BINDING_MISSING
ACTOR_PROVIDER_ID_MISMATCH
ACTOR_LOGIN_MISMATCH
AUTHORITY_GRANT_MISSING
AUTHORITY_GRANT_DUPLICATE
AUTHORITY_GRANT_INACTIVE
AUTHORITY_GRANT_EXPIRED
AUTHORITY_SCOPE_MISMATCH
ACTION_KIND_NOT_GRANTED
CANDIDATE_REVISION_MISMATCH
REVIEW_COMMIT_MISMATCH
SUBJECT_DIGEST_MISMATCH
POLICY_DIGEST_MISMATCH
REVIEW_STATE_NOT_APPROVED
REVIEW_DISMISSED
PROVIDER_EVIDENCE_MALFORMED
PROVIDER_EVIDENCE_DIGEST_MISMATCH
PROVIDER_OBJECT_ID_MISMATCH
ACTION_TIME_OUTSIDE_GRANT
AS_OF_MISSING
ENGINE_UNKNOWN
VALIDATION_EXCEPTION
```

Every finding must expose expected, actual, stable subject identifiers, owner, and next action where deterministically known.

## Package design

Prefer one bounded package within the existing governance package graph, for example:

```text
approval-receipt-verifier
```

Internal modules may separate:

```text
schema validation
exact joins
authority evaluation
receipt construction
fixtures / proof
```

Do not create provider-specific verifier packages in governance.

## Public API

One pure entry point is sufficient:

```text
validate_approval(
  authority_grants,
  provider_evidence,
  subject,
  as_of,
  engine_identity
) -> approvalReceipt.v1
```

Inputs and output must be serializable closed-schema values. No network, filesystem discovery, implicit environment variables, or current-time reads inside the evaluator.

## Acceptance gates

| Gate | Requirement |
|---|---|
| G1 Accepted input | exact Accepted ADRS #260 release is required |
| G2 Provider neutrality | no GitHub API/client/provider permission logic in verifier |
| G3 Exact actor | numeric provider account binding joins exactly once |
| G4 Exact revision | action binds the exact candidate revision |
| G5 Exact subject | finding/subject and policy digests match |
| G6 Historical authority | action time is inside accepted grant interval |
| G7 Closed scope | repository/resource/action are inside a closed grant scope |
| G8 Fail closed | incomplete, duplicate, conflicting, stale, or unknown input is not VALID |
| G9 Determinism | identical inputs produce byte-equivalent deterministic receipt fields |
| G10 Diagnostics | every INVALID/ERROR has an exact code and bounded evidence |
| G11 Nix | package build and `nix flake check` pass |
| G12 Exact head | all proof and existing repository checks pass on exact candidate/merge ref |
| G13 No authority drift | governance output remains evidence, not accepted meaning |
| G14 Claim ceiling | physical-human identity and account non-compromise remain false |

## Mandatory destructive cases

1. Login matches but numeric actor ID differs.
2. Numeric actor ID matches but accepted binding is absent.
3. Candidate revision differs.
4. Review/action state is not approved.
5. Review is dismissed.
6. Grant is not yet valid.
7. Grant expired before action.
8. Grant is inactive, revoked, or superseded.
9. Repository is outside scope.
10. Action kind is outside scope.
11. Finding/subject digest differs.
12. Policy digest differs.
13. Duplicate grants match ambiguously.
14. Provider evidence digest is substituted.
15. Provider object ID is substituted.
16. Current permission is used instead of accepted historical grant.
17. `as_of` is missing or implicit.
18. Engine or schema digest is unknown.
19. Verifier imports or calls a GitHub provider client.
20. Receipt claims physical-human identity, account non-compromise, or provider-independent non-repudiation.
21. Identical inputs produce different deterministic receipt bytes.
22. Validation exception is converted to VALID.

## PR design

Suggested PR title after ADRS acceptance:

```text
feat(approval): add pure exact-revision approval receipt verifier
```

The PR must:

- bind the exact ADRS Decision/release digest;
- add the package and closed schemas;
- include positive and destructive fixtures;
- emit deterministic proof artifacts;
- add Nix and exact-head CI;
- avoid provider/network implementation;
- use `Refs`, not `Closes`, until merged readback and consumer integration exist.

## Claim ceiling

The implementation may prove:

```text
providerNeutralVerifierImplemented=true
exactAuthorityGrantJoinProven=true
exactRevisionJoinProven=true
```

It must retain:

```text
githubEvidenceAdapterImplemented=false until ops merge
physicalHumanIdentityProven=false
accountNonCompromiseProven=false
allRepositoriesEnforced=false
businessOutcomeAchieved=false
corporateSaleOutcomeAchieved=false
```

## Closure

Close only after the exact Accepted ADRS #260 release is read, one valid GitHub-shaped fixture passes, all destructive cases fail with exact codes, Nix/exact-head CI pass, and merged governance readback preserves the receipt contract and claim ceiling."}

子の詳細を表示"] end subgraph CROSS["包含ではない関係"] R["関係・相手・根拠を表示"] T["相手を開く"] R -->|"明示操作"| T end subgraph NEXT["別次元の図"] F["相手を中心に表示"] B["元の図・位置へ戻る"] F --> B end Q -->|"親子・内側"| Z Q -->|"依存・参照・担当など"| R T --> F B --> N ``` ## 読み方と境界 - request.instructions:
body内の各文を、望ましい状態の宣言と、実際に起きたことの報告に分けて読んでください。EとOは同時にyesでも構いません。Eは文書の主題や多数決ではなく存在判定です。具体的な要求文・完成条件・目標文が一文でもあれば、残りが全部作業報告でもE=yesです。例えば「利用者に完了を通知すること」は期待ですが、「利用者に通知した」は実施報告であり期待ではありません。Goal・Acceptanceという見出しそのものは期待文ではなく、その下に過去の実施報告しかなければE=noです。表・数式・役割が完成状態の対応を定義する場合も期待です。Oでは実測の引用・確認状況一覧・本文内HTMLコメントの作業メモも数えますが、架空の試験入力・条件付きの例は数えません。許容を表す「〜でもよい」や仮定・可能性だけを述べる文は、現状の報告ではありません。例えば「点検は後日でもよい」は許容条件ですが、「点検はまだしていない」は現在の状態の報告です。O=yesにするには、本文が現実にそうだと主張している箇所が必要です。与えられたbody全体だけを対象に判断し、そこにない現状を推測しないでください。
本問はEだけ：本文が実現すべき状態を一つでも宣言しているか。完成状態の表・責務・式も宣言である。Goal等の見出しだけでYesにしない。本文にそのような期待がなければNo。実施済みと書いてあるだけなら期待ではない。

{"body":" ## 目的・位置付け **OPEN / UX完成条件の提案・未採択・未実装・未実証。** 複数のMMD／表示次元を行き来するときに、**包含はその場で深掘り、非包含は関係を確認して別の視点へ渡り、元の視点へ戻れる**ようにする。前後の文脈を失う「クリックして別ページへ飛ぶだけ」の体験を避ける。 本Issueが所有するのは**これらの既存UI機能をつなぐ横断ナビゲーションのUX完成条件だけ**。新しい意味正本・relation schema・renderer・DB・ナビゲーション基盤・URL基盤・アプリ固有の業務意味は所有しない。 ## User指定のメタMMD（そのまま保持） ```mermaid flowchart TB subgraph CURRENT["現在の図"] N["対象を選択"] Q{"関係の種類"} N --> Q end subgraph INSIDE["包含関係"] Z["その場でズーム
子の詳細を表示"] end subgraph CROSS["包含ではない関係"] R["関係・相手・根拠を表示"] T["相手を開く"] R -->|"明示操作"| T end subgraph NEXT["別次元の図"] F["相手を中心に表示"] B["元の図・位置へ戻る"] F --> B end Q -->|"親子・内側"| Z Q -->|"依存・参照・担当など"| R T --> F B --> N ``` ## 読み方と境界 - **包含**：根拠ある親子・詳細化の関係。その場でzoom / LOD / 既存module mountを優先する。単なる`depends_on`や参照リンクを包含に変換しない。 - **非包含**：依存・参照・担当などの明示的な関係。相手の識別子・関係種別・根拠・状態を表示し、利用者の明示操作で移動する。同じ図に相手がいれば既存Focusでもよく、別図が必要なら既存URL／view入口を使う。 - **戻る**：元の表示対象・図の種類・選択・focus・camera／zoomを復帰できること。途中で元情報が更新された／権限を失った場合は、無理に古い意味を復元せずUNKNOWN／差分を明示する。 - **意味・権限**：MMD、描画、座標、URLは意味や採択の正本ではない。状態・証拠がない線は推測して補わない。UIの選択／編集は正式なadmissionや実行許可にしない。 ## 既存議論を再利用（Ref / Rel） | Ref | 関係と、本Issueが再実装しないもの | |---|---| | [ADRS #439：8次元MMD索引](https://github.com/roccho-dev/adrs/issues/439#issuecomment-6161373864) | **uses**：どの次元のMMDか／出典の索引。このIssueに元の意味を複製しない | | [ui #112](https://github.com/roccho-dev/ui/issues/112) / [#116](https://github.com/roccho-dev/ui/issues/116) | **reuses**：包含ナビゲーション、semantic LOD、全体の文脈維持 | | [ui #278](https://github.com/roccho-dev/ui/issues/278) | **reuses**：選択した関係と両端を読めるrelation focus | | [ui #311](https://github.com/roccho-dev/ui/issues/311) / [#312](https://github.com/roccho-dev/ui/issues/312) | **depends on / preserves**：view/focus/depthと再現可能なURL、projectionとrendererの分離 | | [ui #320](https://github.com/roccho-dev/ui/issues/320) / [#342](https://github.com/roccho-dev/ui/issues/342) / [PR #343](https://github.com/roccho-dev/ui/pull/343) | **reuses / distinguishes**：Atlasの同じWorld内での跨領域関係・選択。別MMDへの往復は完成扱いしない | | [ui #207](https://github.com/roccho-dev/ui/issues/207) | **preserves**：semanticとlayout／camera／selectionの所有分離 | ## 最小の受入観点（案） | 観点 | 必要な観測 | |---|---| | 包含 | 明示親子の詳細化は元の図の中で行え、zoom-outで全体へ戻れる | | 非包含 | 選択した関係から、種別・相手ID・根拠・状態が分かる。相手を無断で推定しない | | 移動 | 明示操作で正しい相手のViewへ移り、相手をfocusできる。移動先不明なら拒否／UNKNOWN | | 戻る | 元のView・選択・カメラ・zoomを復元する。ブラウザ戻る／進むと矛盾しない | | 安全 | 版違い、出典欠落、循環、他次元でのID衝突、無権限、入力なしを成功扱いしない | | 再利用 | 既存zoom・relation overlay・Inspector・URL・Historyを再利用し、第二正本や新rendererを増やさない | ## 次の議論（別コメント） **「包含関係でない関係のUXをどうするか」**。関係を選ぶ→その場で周辺を確認→必要に応じて別図へ移る→戻る、などの候補を外部UXの先行例と既存実装で比較する。比較案は本Issueのコメントに残す。採択・実装GOは別判定。 **今回の起票は要件保存のみ。** 元Issue/PR、採択済みJSONL、既存コード・CI・merge・配備・外部作用は変更しない。"}

## Parent

- Integration tracker: roccho-dev/adrs#318
- Existing GitHub-as-adapter proof: #148 and merged PR #149
- Existing lifecycle/current shadow proof: PR #203 (proof-only; recover semantics, do not assume cutover)

## Goal

Provide one provider-neutral decision pipeline that turns ADRS Issue/comment events into deterministic, authorized, current decision projections suitable for downstream governance checks and read-only UI rendering.

```text
saved/live GitHub pages
  -> provider payload + transport evidence
  -> canonical raw.jsonl
  -> authority.results.jsonl
  -> lifecycle reduce
  -> decisions.current.jsonl
  -> views/<decision_type>/<status>.jsonl
  -> routes.logical.json
  -> receipt.json
```

This issue owns decision meaning. It does not own hosting, authentication, deployed URLs, or rendering.

## Required boundaries

- GitHub is an adapter, not decision authority.
- Provider metadata and transport evidence remain separate from semantic decision events.
- Authority verification is explicit and fail-closed.
- Current state is a deterministic projection, never a second source of truth.
- Decision type and lifecycle status are semantic fields; physical URLs are not.
- `ops-decision-closure` Fact/Condition/Claim semantics must not be reused as ADR lifecycle semantics.
- No accepted-authority change, cutover, or legacy retirement is authorized by this work.

## Proposed single-bin surface

A single distributable command may expose subcommands, but must preserve distinct artifacts:

```text
decisionctl materialize
decisionctl verify-authority
decisionctl reduce
decisionctl project-views
decisionctl verify
```

Equivalent smaller bins are acceptable only when the public artifact contracts remain identical and duplicated reducer/schema logic is avoided.

## Canonical outputs

### `canonical/raw.jsonl`

## Purpose
Define stable paths for queue, event log, session ledger, final outputs, and proofs so all projects use the same local layout.

## Scope-to-meta contribution
| generation | contribution |
|---|---|
| scope | Stabilizes where `hq` and worker exchange durable data. |
| product | Reduces setup and integration complexity. |
| system/org | Makes logs and sessions easy to find. |
| business/meta | Improves reproducibility and handoff. |

## Scope
- Define `.hq/`, `.agent-runs/`, or equivalent convention.
- Define default paths for instruction queue, events, sessions, outputs, and proof artifacts.

## Non-scope
- Cloud storage.
- External deployment.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Default layout is documented.

- 責務の領域（actor ごと）を voronoi 状の面で塗り分けた（`responsibilityData`）。目的が変わると距離の基準が変わり、同じ node が組み直される。

## いまの3ペインとの違い
- いまは Purpose・Scope・Agent の3列で、目的に向かう**方向**は位置で表していない。
- 線は Current・Target から各 Scope へ扇状に出るので、並べ替えだけでは交差が減らない（V で数値として確認：モックは 10→10、HQ は 15→15）。

## 検討すること
1. 方向の意味：左上を目的（G）にし、右・下を現状と実現の側に置く。Gap は「左上へ向かう距離」として読める形にできるか。

5. 予定：plan のノード（未来）を、左上へ向かう破線の経路として重ねて描けるか。

- [ ] v6 の `applyMetaLayout`・`supportDistances`・`responsibilityData` を読み、再利用できる考え方と捨てるものを一覧にする。
- [ ] 宣言された入力だけから決まる、配置の純関数の仕様（入力・出力・決定性）を起案する。
- [ ] モック（D の fixture、7 frame）で、左上に向かう配置の試作を作り、User の実画面確認に出す。
- [ ] 交差数と、目的までの距離の単調性を、数値の検査として定義する。
- [ ] 3ペインとの関係（切り替えか取り込みか）を決める。
- [ ] P・R・W で主張反復を行い、閉包グラフ（adrs#647）に版を上げて組み込むかどうかを決める。
"}

## Purpose

Make the UX visual evidence artifact auditable as a canonical snapshot, not only generated and uploaded.

Why this contributes: it avoids a false-green path where an artifact exists but no longer represents the intended UX state.

The CI generates and checks `ux-golden.svg/json/md`, but the refactor no-degrade issue does not yet require a stable snapshot audit of those artifacts.

- Keep `ux-golden.json` deterministic.
- Store or compare the canonical UX evidence payload.
- Ensure SVG/Markdown contents are generated from the same canonical JSON.
- Verify the artifact still shows raw buffer, preedit, and expected candidates.

## False-positive prevention

Artifact upload alone is insufficient; its semantic content must match the expected UX state.

## False-negative prevention

Avoid pixel-level comparisons. Compare semantic JSON and key SVG text instead.

## Done when

- CI validates `ux-golden.json` against a canonical snapshot.
- CI checks SVG includes raw buffer, preedit, and candidate labels.
- Artifact mismatch fails with a readable diff.
"}

state.body:
背景: 現状はJEV専用で、secret追加時にEnvironment Secret・workflow参照・SOPS出力定義の複数更新が必要。

完成形: Gitのauthoring contractに対象secret名だけを列挙し、Environmentは実値のみ保持。generic workflowが宣言対象だけをSOPS化する。Environment内secretの全列挙・自動暗号化はしない。

specification.instruction: Read only the complete literal body, including HTML comments, tables, formulas and templates. Decide whether it contains at least one statement presented as a specification or operative contract: a rule, expected or acceptable condition, responsibility, functional capability, input/output mapping, interface purpose, or condition or limitation of use. A stated expected-outcome caption or interface text declaring an action's purpose can qualify. No formal specification label, generality, adoption, implementation, must-word or future tense is required. Distinguish the role of the relationship being stated. Declaring what a function does or what condition applies counts; merely describing what happened, is happening, used to happen or regularly happens in observed execution does not by itself declare a specification. A performed configuration, measured value, comparison or causal explanation does not supply an unstated applicable contract. These are role distinctions, not rules excluding particular headings, formats, tenses or words: a report may also contain a genuine specification, and an ordinary capability statement can declare one without requesting a change. Read each statement in context; one qualifying declaration anywhere is sufficient and observations elsewhere do not cancel it. Quoted or hypothetical text counts when used to declare the specification, but not when displayed only as an illustration. Synthetic contrast: 'This dial sets the sampling interval' declares a function; 'I turned the dial and the reading changed' alone reports an observation. A request or a subject's goal alone does not establish this specification role. Do not consult external content.

options.yes: The complete body contains at least one statement presented as a specification or operative contract of the kind defined in the instruction. It declares the relationship itself; merely reporting a performed action, observed configuration or value, observed result, or a causal explanation of an observed event does not by itself establish that role. A genuine declaration still counts inside a report, quotation or template when the body uses it to declare that relationship.
options.no: The complete body contains no statement presented as a specification or operative contract of the kind defined in the instruction. Answer no only for absence throughout the body; observations elsewhere do not cancel a genuine declaration.

request.instruction: Read only the complete literal body, including HTML comments, tables, formulas and templates. Decide whether it contains at least one genuine request for an action, answer, submission, improvement or remedy, or explicitly presents an action or state as a subject's intended goal or need. Count indirect requests and actual conditional reporting or submission directions, including directions carried by a template or HTML comment whether or not the requested information has been supplied. No addressee, stated reason, fully identified final goal, solution, adoption or implementation is required. Distinguish a relationship presented as a target or request from wording that only locates the circumstances of a reported event or explains a necessary response to it. An incident, inability, missing feature, risk, complaint, category or recipient mention alone does not declare the desired opposite or request its correction. Merely explaining what was necessary to obtain an observed result or work around it does not by itself declare an intended goal. Do not exclude a genuine goal or request merely because it appears within a report or a subordinate clause; do not infer one solely from modality, tense, a heading, mention, imperative form or question mark. A specification or expected caption alone does not establish this request or subject-goal role. One qualifying statement anywhere is sufficient and observations elsewhere do not cancel it. Quoted or hypothetical text counts when the body uses it to make an actual request or goal declaration, but not when shown only as an illustration. Synthetic contrast: 'I need a cost estimate before ordering the materials' declares a goal or need; 'The estimate arrived late, so I postponed the order' alone reports an event and response. Do not consult external content.

options.yes: The complete body contains at least one genuine request or declaration of a subject's intended goal or need of the kind defined in the instruction. This includes actual reporting or submission directions before the requested information is supplied. Merely naming a category or recipient, reporting an incident or inability, or explaining a necessary workaround does not itself establish this role.
options.no: The complete body contains no genuine request or declaration of a subject's intended goal or need of the kind defined in the instruction. Answer no only for absence throughout the body; a report or subordinate clause does not cancel an actual request or goal.

state.body:
Parent: #99

Related: #46, #67-#70, #98, #101, #102

## Purpose

Define retry, replay, resume, and reconciliation as separate safe operations before any user-facing retry implementation is allowed to merge.

## Core decision

| operation | instruction identity | run identity | purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| resume | same | same | continue only when durable evidence proves no duplicate external effect |
| retry | new id with `reply_to` | new | create a new governed attempt |
| replay | same immutable instruction | new | explicit diagnostic reproduction, never silent recovery |
| reconciliation | prior evidence plus typed resolution | no execution until resolved | handle an ambiguous post-effect crash |

A terminal run never rewinds. `error.retryable=true` is advisory evidence, not dispatch permission.

## Purpose lineage

| generation | purpose | contribution | relation |
|---:|---|---|---|
| G0 scope | Define safe recovery semantics. | Separates four operations and their identities. | direct |
| G1 correctness | Prevent duplicate side effects and false completed results. | Ambiguous provider-effect crashes fail closed. | direct |
| G2 contract | Preserve canonical instruction/result/session history. | New attempts are new rows/runs; prior evidence never changes. | direct |
| G3 product | Give operators predictable recovery behavior. | Each action states what may execute and what approval is required. | direct |
| G4 system | Align one-shot and managed worker recovery. | #98 claim/lease/crash rules constrain every path. | direct |
| G5 organization | Eliminate hand-copied failed rows and hidden operator rules. | Recovery becomes typed and reviewable. | direct |
| G6 business | Lower incident and support cost across adapters. | Provider idempotency is explicit capability evidence. | direct |
| G7 transfer | Let a new owner recover failures safely. | Decision tables and examples replace tribal knowledge. | indirect |
| G8 due diligence | Avoid unsupported exactly-once claims. | The unavoidable ambiguity window is explicit. | indirect |
| G9 asset value | Keep recovery small without a scheduler/database. | Existing append-only evidence and policy/claim boundaries are reused. | indirect |
| G10 meta | Increase company value and saleability. | Lower operational ambiguity and buyer risk improves transferability. | indirect |

## Scope

- Define retryable versus non-retryable conditions by lifecycle and provider-effect boundary.
- Define new instruction/run identities and `reply_to` lineage for retry.
- Define explicit same-instruction/new-run diagnostic replay.
- Define safe same-run resume constraints.
- Define `reconcile_required` or equivalent non-green handling for ambiguous post-effect crashes.
- Define approval, redaction, single-writer claim, idempotency, and ledger interactions.
- Provide example lineage and implementation gates.

## Non-scope

- Implementing a retry command.
- Selecting a new durable status/version before #98 and canonical contract review.
- Adapter-specific retry logic.
- Unconditional exactly-once external effects.
- Automatic repair of missing terminal evidence.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Retry, replay, resume, and reconciliation have non-overlapping definitions.
- [ ] Retry always means new instruction id, new run id, and `reply_to` lineage.
- [ ] Replay is explicit diagnostic execution and cannot be reached by normal crash recovery.
- [ ] Resume preserves one run only when durable/provider evidence proves continuation cannot duplicate an effect.
- [ ] Ambiguous post-effect crash causes zero automatic dispatch and typed non-green reconciliation.
- [ ] Completed/terminal runs never rewind.
- [ ] Destructive retry/replay requires fresh validation, policy, digest-bound approval, claim, and provider-effect safety.
- [ ] Provider idempotency is verified adapter capability evidence, not an input boolean.
- [ ] `error.retryable` cannot bypass lifecycle, policy, approval, claim, or reconciliation.
- [ ] Ledger/readback preserves each attempt independently.
- [ ] The design is compatible with #98, #101, #102, and canonical instruction/result/session contracts.

## Destructive cases

The issue is not complete if any is allowed:

1. failed JSONL is copied by hand with no lineage;
2. retry reuses the prior instruction id;
3. a terminal run rewinds to queued/running;
4. replay occurs implicitly after restart;
5. stale approval is reused for a new attempt;
6. `retryable=true` alone causes dispatch;
7. a stale claim is treated as proof that no provider effect occurred;
8. ambiguous post-effect crash automatically re-executes;
9. provider idempotency is accepted without a verified adapter contract;
10. observation commands select or execute recovery;
11. prior terminal evidence is edited or deleted;
12. retry/replay attempts are collapsed into one ledger row;
13. a repair procedure fabricates completed evidence without external confirmation;
14. unconditional exactly-once is claimed for providers without deduplication.

## Required design evidence

- `docs/worker-retry.md` with purpose lineage, definitions, state matrix, lineage graph, destructive-operation gate, and future implementation gate.
- Example instruction/run lineage using `reply_to`.
- Explicit mapping to #98 crash matrix.
- Explicit mapping to #101 policy/redaction and #102 single-writer claim.
- Review proof that no new runtime retry path is added by this issue.

## Future implementation gate

No retry command may merge until tests prove:

1. new instruction/run identity and exact `reply_to`;
2. unchanged prior evidence;
3. fresh digest-bound policy/approval;
4. zero calls on stale approval or unresolved reconciliation;
5. explicit-only replay;
6. provider idempotency capability verification;
7. separate ledger rows for all attempts;
8. Linux and Windows binary proof using canonical rows.

## Merge condition

Merge this design only when future recovery cannot bypass identity, policy, claim, idempotency, or the ambiguous external-effect boundary, and the current implementation gains no implicit retry path.

Related: #46, #67-#70, #98, #101, #102

## Purpose

Define retry, replay, resume, and reconciliation as separate safe operations before any user-facing retry implementation is allowed to merge.

## Core decision

| operation | instruction identity | run identity | purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| resume | same | same | continue only when durable evidence proves no duplicate external effect |
| retry | new id with `reply_to` | new | create a new governed attempt |
| replay | same immutable instruction | new | explicit diagnostic reproduction, never silent recovery |
| reconciliation | prior evidence plus typed resolution | no execution until resolved | handle an ambiguous post-effect crash |

A terminal run never rewinds. `error.retryable=true` is advisory evidence, not dispatch permission.

## Purpose lineage

| generation | purpose | contribution | relation |
|---:|---|---|---|
| G0 scope | Define safe recovery semantics. | Separates four operations and their identities. | direct |
| G1 correctness | Prevent duplicate side effects and false completed results. | Ambiguous provider-effect crashes fail closed. | direct |
| G2 contract | Preserve canonical instruction/result/session history. | New attempts are new rows/runs; prior evidence never changes. | direct |
| G3 product | Give operators predictable recovery behavior. | Each action states what may execute and what approval is required. | direct |
| G4 system | Align one-shot and managed worker recovery. | #98 claim/lease/crash rules constrain every path. | direct |
| G5 organization | Eliminate hand-copied failed rows and hidden operator rules. | Recovery becomes typed and reviewable. | direct |
| G6 business | Lower incident and support cost across adapters. | Provider idempotency is explicit capability evidence. | direct |
| G7 transfer | Let a new owner recover failures safely. | Decision tables and examples replace tribal knowledge. | indirect |
| G8 due diligence | Avoid unsupported exactly-once claims. | The unavoidable ambiguity window is explicit. | indirect |
| G9 asset value | Keep recovery small without a scheduler/database. | Existing append-only evidence and policy/claim boundaries are reused. | indirect |
| G10 meta | Increase company value and saleability. | Lower operational ambiguity and buyer risk improves transferability. | indirect |

## Scope

- Define retryable versus non-retryable conditions by lifecycle and provider-effect boundary.
- Define new instruction/run identities and `reply_to` lineage for retry.
- Define explicit same-instruction/new-run diagnostic replay.
- Define safe same-run resume constraints.
- Define `reconcile_required` or equivalent non-green handling for ambiguous post-effect crashes.
- Define approval, redaction, single-writer claim, idempotency, and ledger interactions.
- Provide example lineage and implementation gates.

## Non-scope

- Implementing a retry command.
- Selecting a new durable status/version before #98 and canonical contract review.
- Adapter-specific retry logic.
- Unconditional exactly-once external effects.
- Automatic repair of missing terminal evidence.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Retry, replay, resume, and reconciliation have non-overlapping definitions.
- [ ] Retry always means new instruction id, new run id, and `reply_to` lineage.
- [ ] Replay is explicit diagnostic execution and cannot be reached by normal crash recovery.
- [ ] Resume preserves one run only when durable/provider evidence proves continuation cannot duplicate an effect.
- [ ] Ambiguous post-effect crash causes zero automatic dispatch and typed non-green reconciliation.
- [ ] Completed/terminal runs never rewind.
- [ ] Destructive retry/replay requires fresh validation, policy, digest-bound approval, claim, and provider-effect safety.
- [ ] Provider idempotency is verified adapter capability evidence, not an input boolean.
- [ ] `error.retryable` cannot bypass lifecycle, policy, approval, claim, or reconciliation.
- [ ] Ledger/readback preserves each attempt independently.
- [ ] The design is compatible with #98, #101, #102, and canonical instruction/result/session contracts.

## Destructive cases

The issue is not complete if any is allowed:

1. failed JSONL is copied by hand with no lineage;
2. retry reuses the prior instruction id;
3. a terminal run rewinds to queued/running;
4. replay occurs implicitly after restart;
5. stale approval is reused for a new attempt;
6. `retryable=true` alone causes dispatch;
7. a stale claim is treated as proof that no provider effect occurred;
8. ambiguous post-effect crash automatically re-executes;
9. provider idempotency is accepted without a verified adapter contract;
10. observation commands select or execute recovery;
11. prior terminal evidence is edited or deleted;
12. retry/replay attempts are collapsed into one ledger row;
13. a repair procedure fabricates completed evidence without external confirmation;
14. unconditional exactly-once is claimed for providers without deduplication.

## Required design evidence

- `docs/worker-retry.md` with purpose lineage, definitions, state matrix, lineage graph, destructive-operation gate, and future implementation gate.
- Example instruction/run lineage using `reply_to`.
- Explicit mapping to #98 crash matrix.
- Explicit mapping to #101 policy/redaction and #102 single-writer claim.
- Review proof that no new runtime retry path is added by this issue.

## Future implementation gate

No retry command may merge until tests prove:

1. new instruction/run identity and exact `reply_to`;
2. unchanged prior evidence;
3. fresh digest-bound policy/approval;
4. zero calls on stale approval or unresolved reconciliation;
5. explicit-only replay;
6. provider idempotency capability verification;
7. separate ledger rows for all attempts;
8. Linux and Windows binary proof using canonical rows.

## Merge condition

Merge this design only when future recovery cannot bypass identity, policy, claim, idempotency, or the ambiguous external-effect boundary, and the current implementation gains no implicit retry path."}

{"body":"## Purpose

Allow the repo-map artifact to render external projection input from local/dev tooling instead of only the built-in fixture.

## Completion state

This is complete when the repo-map artifact builder can accept an external JSONL/projection input path, record its digest, and still fall back to the existing fixture when no input is supplied.

## Scope

- Add CLI/env input path for external repo-map input.
- Support external world JSONL or projection JSON, with backward compatibility for the current fixture.
- Record input path and digest in artifact manifest.
- Bundle source input under artifact `source/` evidence.
- Preserve `generatedArtifactsAreAuthority:false`.
- Keep existing CI artifact behavior green.

## Inputs

| input | Role |
|---|---|
| repoMap world JSONL | Source read model |
| repoMap projection JSON | Renderer-ready read model |
| legacy `map.*` JSONL | Compatibility input |

## Done checklist

- [ ] External input path can be specified by CLI or env.
- [ ] No input path keeps existing fixture behavior.
- [ ] Artifact manifest includes input path and digest.
- [ ] Artifact includes a source copy of the input.
- [ ] Generated HTML remains evidence only.
- [ ] CI covers fixture mode and external input mode.

## Purpose

## Completion state

- Add CLI/env input path for external repo-map input.
- Support external world JSONL or projection JSON, with backward compatibility for the current fixture.
- Record input path and digest in artifact manifest.
- Bundle source input under artifact `source/` evidence.
- Preserve `generatedArtifactsAreAuthority:false`.
- Keep existing CI artifact behavior green.

## Inputs

| input | Role |
|---|---|
| repoMap world JSONL | Source read model |
| repoMap projection JSON | Renderer-ready read model |
| legacy `map.*` JSONL | Compatibility input |

- [ ] No input path keeps existing fixture behavior.
- [ ] Artifact manifest includes input path and digest.
- [ ] Artifact includes a source copy of the input.
- [ ] Generated HTML remains evidence only.
- [ ] CI covers fixture mode and external input mode.
- [ ] Invalid input fails clearly.

- Making ui.git a state store.
- Placing local queues in ui.git.
- Large renderer rewrite.

## Purpose

Let Vim/hq append modeling queue rows into one local JSONL file and let tools read them back deterministically.

## Completion state

This is complete when `.local/queue.jsonl` supports append, readback, parse, tail, and dedupe for local/dev operation.

## Scope

- Define local queue and receipt paths.
- Add append command.
- Add readback command.
- Add tail command for unprocessed rows.
- Detect broken JSONL rows.
- Keep committed samples separate from local files.

## Local files

| path | Role |
|---|---|
| `.local/queue.jsonl` | Local queue body |
| `.local/receipt.jsonl` | Local processing receipts |
| `examples/queue.sample.jsonl` | Committed sample |
| `examples/receipt.sample.jsonl` | Committed sample receipt |

## Done checklist

- [ ] One row can be appended to the local queue.
- [ ] Appended rows can be read back.
- [ ] Tail mode returns unprocessed rows.
- [ ] Broken JSONL produces an error receipt.
- [ ] Duplicate `id` or `idempotencyKey` is detected.
- [ ] Local queue files are gitignored.
- [ ] Sample queue files are committed and tested.
- [ ] Empty queue files are valid.

## Non-scope

- Database or event bus.
- GitHub issue comment persistence.
- Accepted ledger promotion.

{"body":"## Purpose

Apply the adrs #196 pattern across the selected repo universe so each selected repo can prove that its committed root `README.md` matches its generated README artifact, or explicitly records why it is not yet in generated/materialized mode.

This closes the local README materialization gap. It does not replace governance final-join README projection drift enforcement.

## Context

Current state after adrs #196:

- `roccho-dev/adrs` has a generated README artifact.
- `roccho-dev/adrs` root `README.md` is materialized from that generated artifact.
- `roccho-dev/adrs` has a `readme-materialized` flake check that fails when generated README and committed README drift.

Observed selected repo state:

| repo | README artifact producer | committed README materialization check | current status |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| `roccho-dev/adrs` | yes | yes | complete for local materialization |
| `roccho-dev/governance` | yes | no explicit `readme-materialized` check observed | needs rollout |
| `roccho-dev/ui` | yes | no explicit `readme-materialized` check observed | needs rollout |
| `roccho-dev/ops` | unclear / no matching flake readme artifact observed in quick readback | needs inventory first |

Existing broader issues:

- governance #81 covers README projection drift integration in the final report/final join.
- governance #131 covers the wider ADRS-owned output plane and governance final-monitor cutover.

This issue is narrower: repo-local materialization drift checks for selected repos.

## Required work

### R1. Inventory selected repo README artifact mode

For each selected repo, record:

- whether it has a `readme-artifact` package/check;
- whether generated `README.md` exists in the artifact;
- whether committed root `README.md` is expected to be generated, partially managed, or handwritten;
- whether local flake/CI compares generated README with committed README;
- whether the repo emits a `readmeProjectionReceipt.v1` row consumable by governance.

### R2. Add materialization check where generated mode is active

For every selected repo with generated README mode:

- add a deterministic check analogous to adrs `readme-materialized`;
- compare generated artifact `README.md` with committed root `README.md`;
- fail with an actionable diff on mismatch;
- ensure the check is part of `nix flake check` or the repo's stable local CI entrypoint;
- keep README non-authority.

### R3. Materialize committed README where needed

For every selected repo where generated mode is active but committed README differs:

- update root `README.md` to match generated artifact output;
- keep authority boundary text;
- do not use CI auto-commit as the write path.

### R4. Residualize non-generated repos explicitly

If a selected repo is not ready for generated/materialized README mode:

- record a residual row or issue comment;
- state owner, reason, next action, and expiry/return condition;
- make clear that final README projection enforcement remains in governance #81 / #131.

### R5. Attach final readback to governance #131

After rollout PRs merge, comment on governance #131 with:

- per-repo materialization status;
- check names;
- merge commits;
- default branch README readback evidence;
- remaining residuals, if any.

## Acceptance criteria

Close only when:

1. The selected repo universe for this rollout is listed.
2. `adrs` remains complete after readback.
3. `governance` either has generated README materialization check or an explicit residual.
4. `ui` either has generated README materialization check or an explicit residual.
5. `ops` either has generated README artifact + materialization check or an explicit residual explaining why not.
6. Generated README drift cannot silently pass in any selected repo that claims generated README mode.
7. No repo claims README authority.
8. The work is linked back to governance #131 and distinguished from final join enforcement under governance #81.

## Non-goals

- Do not claim all-repo README final compliance from this issue alone.
- Do not replace governance #81 README projection drift integration.
- Do not mutate branch protection or provider required checks here.
- Do not make README, generated artifacts, or CI logs authority.
- Do not auto-commit generated README from CI.

## Completion note template

| repo | readme artifact | materialized check | committed README matches generated | status | evidence |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|---|
| adrs | yes | yes | yes | complete | adrs #196 |
| governance |  |  |  |  |  |
| ui |  |  |  |  |  |
| ops |  |  |  |  |  |"}

## Purpose

Build the package-level closure and final report/join machinery that proves README/ADRS expectations are met by package assertions, receipts, admission, README projection, and provider CI evidence.

This phase prevents repo-level packet presence from hiding package-level omissions.

## Child PRs to attach

| Work | Repo | PR status |
|---|---|---|
| F1: observed package inventory detector | governance | new PR |
| F2: missing/orphan package findings | governance | new PR |
| F3: canonical receipt producer | governance | new PR |
| F4: package contract receipt fixtures | governance | new PR |
| G1: final report schema | governance | new PR |
| G2: ADRS × packet × assertion × receipt join | governance | new PR |
| G3: admission compiler | governance | new PR |
| G4: README projection drift integration | governance | new PR |
| G5: provider CI drift integration | governance | new PR |
| G6: final report DX hardening | governance | new PR |

## Requirements

### F1 observed package inventory

- Detect package-like surfaces from repo reality, not only packet claims.
- Compare observed package surfaces to packet `packages.jsonl`.
- Include root/tool/module/package README surfaces when required by ADRS projection contract.
- Deterministic output with stable ordering.

### F2 package findings

Emit findings for:

- required package missing from packet;
- observed package without assertion;
- package row without observed surface;
- duplicate package id;
- missing package README where required;
- package README with forbidden authority claim.

### F3 canonical receipts

Receipt rows must include:

- `repoId`
- `packageId`
- `contractId`
- `assertionDigest`
- `decisionDigest`
- `checkId`
- `status`
- `evidenceDigest`
- `sourcePath` or evidence locator

`nix flake check` green must remain evidence producer, not final pass.

### F4 receipt fixtures

Fixtures must cover:

- clean receipt;
- missing receipt;
- stale decisionDigest;
- mismatched assertionDigest;
- wrong packageId;
- raw human log without structured receipt.

### G1 final report schema

`govFinalScopePurposeJoin.report.v1` must include:

- inventory section;
- expectation section;
- assertion section;
- receipt section;
- admission section;
- providerCi section;
- readmeProjection section;
- provenance section;
- waivers section;
- findings section.

### G2 final join compiler

- Join accepted ADRS grants with required repo universe, packet registry, package assertions, and receipts.
- Do not pass on README text alone.
- Do not pass on packet existence alone.
- Treat feature/package wishes as non-authority challenge/proposal unless accepted by ADRS.

### G3 admission compiler

- Only `organization-active` is pass.
- `unclaimed-grant`, `orphan-assertion`, `asserted-but-unproven`, `stale-assertion`, `conflict`, `revoked-grant`, missing package, missing packet, and stale packet block unless narrowly waived.

### G4 README projection drift

- Consume `readmeProjectionReceipt.v1` and `readmeProjectionFinding.v1` rows.
- README and package README are non-authority projection surfaces.
- Required README drift blocks only when accepted ADRS projection contract marks that surface required.
- Findings must not treat README as authority.

### G5 provider CI drift

- Consume CI intent and workflow reality.
- Block on manual/stale/undeclared provider CI surfaces when in scope.
- Preserve provider CI YAML checks as final join input or receipt producer.

### G6 DX hardening

Every blocking finding must include:

- `repoId`, `packageId` when applicable, `contractId`, `adrsRef`;
- `expected`, `actual`, `delta`;
- `diagnosticClass`, `likelyOwner`, `nextAction`;
- `decisionDigest`, `assertionDigest`, `receiptDigest` when applicable.

## Done when

- Package inventory cannot be hidden by omitting packet rows.
- Canonical receipts are structured and joinable.
- Final report schema is fixed before strict gate work.
- Final join consumes org packets, package assertions, receipts, admission, README drift, provider CI drift, and waivers.
- All blocking findings are actionable without reading ADRS prose by hand.

## Not done when

- Packet exists but package omissions can pass.
- Receipt is only human-readable CI output.
- Report only says pass/fail.
- README drift is outside final report.
- Provider CI drift is outside final report.
- Partial join green is presented as final green.

## Evidence required

- Schema files and fixture rows.
- Clean and dirty fixture outputs.
- Nonzero exit on blocking dirty fixtures.
- Comment links to child PRs.

## Child PR comment template

```text
Child PR: <repo#number>
Phase issue: Phase F/G
Requirement: <F1/F2/F3/F4/G1/G2/G3/G4/G5/G6>
Delta removed: <which package/final-report escape hatch is removed>
Evidence: <schema/fixture/check/report>
Boundary: no branch protection cutover in this phase
```

| G2: ADRS × packet × assertion × receipt join | governance | new PR |
| G3: admission compiler | governance | new PR |
| G4: README projection drift integration | governance | new PR |
| G5: provider CI drift integration | governance | new PR |
| G6: final report DX hardening | governance | new PR |

## Requirements

### F1 observed package inventory

- Detect package-like surfaces from repo reality, not only packet claims.
- Compare observed package surfaces to packet `packages.jsonl`.
- Include root/tool/module/package README surfaces when required by ADRS projection contract.
- Deterministic output with stable ordering.

### F2 package findings

Emit findings for:

- required package missing from packet;
- observed package without assertion;
- package row without observed surface;
- duplicate package id;
- missing package README where required;
- package README with forbidden authority claim.

### F3 canonical receipts

Receipt rows must include:

- `repoId`
- `packageId`
- `contractId`
- `assertionDigest`
- `decisionDigest`
- `checkId`
- `status`
- `evidenceDigest`
- `sourcePath` or evidence locator

`nix flake check` green must remain evidence producer, not final pass.

### F4 receipt fixtures

Fixtures must cover:

- clean receipt;
- missing receipt;
- stale decisionDigest;
- mismatched assertionDigest;
- wrong packageId;
- raw human log without structured receipt.

### G1 final report schema

`govFinalScopePurposeJoin.report.v1` must include:

- inventory section;
- expectation section;
- assertion section;
- receipt section;
- admission section;
- providerCi section;
- readmeProjection section;
- provenance section;
- waivers section;
- findings section.

### G2 final join compiler

- Join accepted ADRS grants with required repo universe, packet registry, package assertions, and receipts.
- Do not pass on README text alone.
- Do not pass on packet existence alone.
- Treat feature/package wishes as non-authority challenge/proposal unless accepted by ADRS.

### G3 admission compiler

- Only `organization-active` is pass.
- `unclaimed-grant`, `orphan-assertion`, `asserted-but-unproven`, `stale-assertion`, `conflict`, `revoked-grant`, missing package, missing packet, and stale packet block unless narrowly waived.

### G4 README projection drift

- Consume `readmeProjectionReceipt.v1` and `readmeProjectionFinding.v1` rows.
- README and package README are non-authority projection surfaces.
- Required README drift blocks only when accepted ADRS projection contract marks that surface required.
- Findings must not treat README as authority.

### G5 provider CI drift

- Consume CI intent and workflow reality.
- Block on manual/stale/undeclared provider CI surfaces when in scope.
- Preserve provider CI YAML checks as final join input or receipt producer.

### G6 DX hardening

Every blocking finding must include:

- `repoId`, `packageId` when applicable, `contractId`, `adrsRef`;
- `expected`, `actual`, `delta`;
- `diagnosticClass`, `likelyOwner`, `nextAction`;
- `decisionDigest`, `assertionDigest`, `receiptDigest` when applicable.

## Done when

- Package inventory cannot be hidden by omitting packet rows.
- Canonical receipts are structured and joinable.
- Final report schema is fixed before strict gate work.
- Final join consumes org packets, package assertions, receipts, admission, README drift, provider CI drift, and waivers.
- All blocking findings are actionable without reading ADRS prose by hand.

## Not done when

- Packet exists but package omissions can pass.
- Receipt is only human-readable CI output.
- Report only says pass/fail.
- README drift is outside final report.
- Provider CI drift is outside final report.
- Partial join green is presented as final green.

## Evidence required

- Schema files and fixture rows.
- Clean and dirty fixture outputs.
- Nonzero exit on blocking dirty fixtures.
- Comment links to child PRs.

## Child PR comment template

```text
Child PR: <repo#number>
Phase issue: Phase F/G
Requirement: <F1/F2/F3/F4/G1/G2/G3/G4/G5/G6>
Delta removed: <which package/final-report escape hatch is removed>
Evidence: <schema/fixture/check/report>
Boundary: no branch protection cutover in this phase
```
"}

## Scope

This Issue is a **non-authority physical GitHub Environment readback ledger**.

It records only non-secret observable/reported facts about GitHub Environments. It never becomes the logical contract and never promotes input presence to provider or consumer PASS.

## Authority

```text
accepted architecture    = roccho-dev/adrs#443
canonical branch         = proposals
logical contract         = contracts/environments.jsonl
provider physical state  = #2
repo-owned effect entry  = #18
this Issue               = physical readback only
```

## Expected Environment set

```text
dev-authoring
dev-projection
stg-projection
prd-projection
```

Do not create `stg-authoring` or `prd-authoring`.

| Environment | Secrets | Variables | Logical desired state |

Keep these states separate:

```text
NAME_PRESENT / BOOTSTRAP_REPORTED
!= INPUT_VALIDATED
!= CONFIGURED
!= ACTIVE
!= PROVIDER_EFFECT_PASS
!= HANDOFF_PASS
!= CONSUMER_PASS

NOT_OBSERVED       no current readback/report

- no unresolved state is absorbed into PASS.

| dev-projection | yes/no | ... | ... | STATE | ... | non-secret ref |
| stg-projection | yes/no | ... | ... | STATE | NOT_CONFIGURED | non-secret ref |
| prd-projection | yes/no | ... | ... | STATE | NOT_CONFIGURED | non-secret ref |
```

## Non-goals

- storing or revealing values;
- becoming the logical contract;
- declaring provider projection PASS;

!= CONFIGURED
!= ACTIVE
!= PROVIDER_EFFECT_PASS
!= HANDOFF_PASS
!= CONSUMER_PASS

PR #17 records a separately performed owner bootstrap with no secret/private value included in the PR:

### YYYY-MM-DD

canonical SHA: <exact proposals SHA>

| Environment | Exists | Required names | Protection | Evidence level | Logical state | Evidence |
|---|---:|---|---|---|---|---|

## Purpose

Implement the target-owned half of roccho-dev/adrs#460: start the exact voice-ui dev server in WSLC OCI with the target-bound `jev-api` ciphertext, while keeping plaintext out of Git, Nix, artifacts, files and logs.

Refs: roccho-dev/resources#52 only for the existing OCI dev runtime; roccho-dev/resources#53 is explicitly out of scope. Provider counterpart: roccho-dev/envs#24. Observed canonical `proposals` at issue creation: `4712d1eb8959de4e24775dc3c33ca7d614637177`.

## Scope and concurrency

Use a new PR limited to `oci/dev/**`. Current open PRs roccho-dev/windows#19/#20/#21 touch `flake.nix` and `hosts/**`, not `oci/dev/**`. Do not absorb or modify their own/rent/Cloudflare work. If a `flake.nix` change becomes necessary, stop, wait for that series, rebase and escalate instead of editing it concurrently.

The target identity must not be generated until the preceding ADRS policy PR fixes its exact credential-root path and residual boundary.

## Target contract

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  C["envs exact-SHA\nsingle-recipient ciphertext"]
  I["OCI target age identity\noutside Git/Nix"]
  X["bounded pinned launcher\nin-memory decrypt"]
  A["exact apps dev server\nJEV_API_KEY child env only"]
  T["secretless acceptance runner"]
  C --> X
  I --> X
  X --> A --> T
```

- Identity path: `/work/repos/.auth/roccho-dev/age/oci-dev.key`, mode 0600, generated inside OCI. Only its public recipient may leave the target. The path becomes policy-bound only after the ADRS policy PR lands.
- Use Nix-pinned sops/age only as absolute store-path dependencies inside bounded tool closures. Raw `sops`, `age` and `age-keygen` must not appear in the shared `profile/bin` or ambient PATH.
- Decrypt anew for each fresh server process. Do not write a plaintext env file.
- `jev-age-init` is the only key-generation entry: fixed destination, umask 077/atomic create, refuses overwrite, prints only the public recipient, no rotate/export flags.
- `voice-ui-jev-dev` is bounded to voice-ui local development: it accepts only exact envs SHA, exact apps SHA and loopback port; it accepts no arbitrary argv, shell or decrypt/export mode.
- Verify exact clean source identities and resolve/build the apps runtime before decrypting.

## Minimal source shape

```text
oci/dev/
├── nix.nix       # two bounded tools; raw crypto binaries closure-internal only
└── proof.sh      # existing proof extended with secret-free failure/fixture cases
```

Prefer these existing files. Add another file only if it materially reduces coupling. No classes, redundant adapters or generic framework.

## Required guards

- missing/empty/wrong-mode identity, wrong recipient, tamper, dirty/mismatched exact SHA or absent ciphertext starts no child;
- nonselected/multi-recipient ciphertext is rejected;
- child receives `JEV_API_KEY`, but no `SOPS_AGE_*`, identity path, GitHub credential or unrelated secret;
- fixture secret appears in no stdout, stderr, receipt or log;
- key presence/child start is not a REAL PASS;
- a secret-free fixture proves good identity PASS and wrong identity/tamper RED;
- raw sops/age binaries are absent from `profile/bin`, and neither bounded tool can print/export decrypted material;
- source checks use only fixtures. Real Jev is a separately authorized effect and the User has authorized fresh repeated runs.

## Explicit residual

This is a trusted single-operator/root OCI, not a hostile-root isolation boundary. Root or another same-uid session can read the identity and `/proc/<pid>/environ`; mode 0600 does not prevent that. The controls are policy, bounded commands, non-disclosure and no ambient raw decrypt tool—not a claim of kernel/process isolation.

Adopting the change produces a new dev image identity. Keep the old image for rollback and record the new image identity with the exact envs/apps SHAs in run evidence.

## Handoff and evidence ceiling

After envs#24 source is merged and its authorized ciphertext PR is merged, start apps PR roccho-dev/windows#34's then-current exact head through this launcher and run its secretless acceptance runtime. A live success proves only local-OCI, exact source-head, dev-server `REAL_JEV_DEPENDENT_SCENARIO`. It does not prove Cloudflare, deploy, ops admission, credentialed CI or real microphone/audio.

## Non-goals

Cloudflare, Tailscale, own/rent image changes, deployment, apps auth code, envctl/envs-old restoration, plaintext at rest, arbitrary child execution, flake changes while the active windows series overlaps, and merge authority.

request.text:
{"body":"## Purpose

Implement the target-owned half of roccho-dev/adrs#460: start the exact voice-ui dev server in WSLC OCI with the target-bound `jev-api` ciphertext, while keeping plaintext out of Git, Nix, artifacts, files and logs.

Refs: roccho-dev/resources#52 only for the existing OCI dev runtime; roccho-dev/resources#53 is explicitly out of scope. Provider counterpart: roccho-dev/envs#24. Observed canonical `proposals` at issue creation: `4712d1eb8959de4e24775dc3c33ca7d614637177`.

## Scope and concurrency

Use a new PR limited to `oci/dev/**`. Current open PRs roccho-dev/windows#19/#20/#21 touch `flake.nix` and `hosts/**`, not `oci/dev/**`. Do not absorb or modify their own/rent/Cloudflare work. If a `flake.nix` change becomes necessary, stop, wait for that series, rebase and escalate instead of editing it concurrently.

The target identity must not be generated until the preceding ADRS policy PR fixes its exact credential-root path and residual boundary.

## Target contract

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  C["envs exact-SHA\nsingle-recipient ciphertext"]
  I["OCI target age identity\noutside Git/Nix"]
  X["bounded pinned launcher\nin-memory decrypt"]
  A["exact apps dev server\nJEV_API_KEY child env only"]
  T["secretless acceptance runner"]
  C --> X
  I --> X
  X --> A --> T
```

- Identity path: `/work/repos/.auth/roccho-dev/age/oci-dev.key`, mode 0600, generated inside OCI. Only its public recipient may leave the target. The path becomes policy-bound only after the ADRS policy PR lands.
- Use Nix-pinned sops/age only as absolute store-path dependencies inside bounded tool closures. Raw `sops`, `age` and `age-keygen` must not appear in the shared `profile/bin` or ambient PATH.
- Decrypt anew for each fresh server process. Do not write a plaintext env file.
- `jev-age-init` is the only key-generation entry: fixed destination, umask 077/atomic create, refuses overwrite, prints only the public recipient, no rotate/export flags.
- `voice-ui-jev-dev` is bounded to voice-ui local development: it accepts only exact envs SHA, exact apps SHA and loopback port; it accepts no arbitrary argv, shell or decrypt/export mode.
- Verify exact clean source identities and resolve/build the apps runtime before decrypting.

## Minimal source shape

```text
oci/dev/
├── nix.nix       # two bounded tools; raw crypto binaries closure-internal only
└── proof.sh      # existing proof extended with secret-free failure/fixture cases
```

Prefer these existing files. Add another file only if it materially reduces coupling. No classes, redundant adapters or generic framework.

## Required guards

- missing/empty/wrong-mode identity, wrong recipient, tamper, dirty/mismatched exact SHA or absent ciphertext starts no child;
- nonselected/multi-recipient ciphertext is rejected;
- child receives `JEV_API_KEY`, but no `SOPS_AGE_*`, identity path, GitHub credential or unrelated secret;
- fixture secret appears in no stdout, stderr, receipt or log;
- key presence/child start is not a REAL PASS;
- a secret-free fixture proves good identity PASS and wrong identity/tamper RED;
- raw sops/age binaries are absent from `profile/bin`, and neither bounded tool can print/export decrypted material;
- source checks use only fixtures. Real Jev is a separately authorized effect and the User has authorized fresh repeated runs.

## Explicit residual

This is a trusted single-operator/root OCI, not a hostile-root isolation boundary. Root or another same-uid session can read the identity and `/proc/<pid>/environ`; mode 0600 does not prevent that. The controls are policy, bounded commands, non-disclosure and no ambient raw decrypt tool—not a claim of kernel/process isolation.

Adopting the change produces a new dev image identity. Keep the old image for rollback and record the new image identity with the exact envs/apps SHAs in run evidence.

## Handoff and evidence ceiling

After envs#24 source is merged and its authorized ciphertext PR is merged, start apps PR roccho-dev/windows#34's then-current exact head through this launcher and run its secretless acceptance runtime. A live success proves only local-OCI, exact source-head, dev-server `REAL_JEV_DEPENDENT_SCENARIO`. It does not prove Cloudflare, deploy, ops admission, credentialed CI or real microphone/audio.

## Non-goals

Cloudflare, Tailscale, own/rent image changes, deployment, apps auth code, envctl/envs-old restoration, plaintext at rest, arbitrary child execution, flake changes while the active windows series overlaps, and merge authority."}

- selected universe digest/source.

- PR comment stating shadow is observation only.

This issue closes observation only. It does not close strict failure, required checks, or branch protection.

{"body":"## Goal

Make `graph/1`, `seq/1`, and `map/1` three projection profiles over one semantic JSONL, not three separate input models.

User mental model:

```text
same JSONL
  ├─ graph/1  : relation/topology-led projection
  ├─ seq/1    : order/time/actor-led projection
  └─ map/1    : bounds/spatial-led projection
        ↓
     maxGraph
```

## Current state

- `graph` and `seq` already read the same `examples/shared/business-model.jsonl` through the same business-model feature path.
- `map` still reads `examples/map/example.jsonl` through `packages/semantic-map/feature.mjs`.
- Low-level state is already converged on `semantic-map-state/1` (`meta / region / relation`).
- `semantic-map/feature-runtime.mjs` already selects `graph/1`, `seq/1`, or `map/1` as projection patterns.

So the architecture is close, but the public/runtime contract is not yet truly **one data, three views**.

## Desired state

- One semantic source can be passed unchanged to `graph`, `seq`, or `map`.
- `graph / seq / map` differ only by projection policy.
- No fourth generic canvas DSL.
- No duplicated business semantics per view.
- maxGraph remains the shared rendering/authoring engine, not the semantic source of truth.

## Minimal implementation direction

1. Let the business-model feature support `map` in addition to `graph` / `seq`.
2. Point the map adapter at the same shared semantic source used by graph/seq.
3. Keep view-specific requirements as projection validation/policy:
   - graph: relations/topology
   - seq: temporal/order/actor
   - map: bounds/spatial
4. Preserve one `semantic-map-state/1`-compatible projected state rather than introducing another DSL.

## Acceptance

- The same JSONL payload renders successfully through `graph/1`, `seq/1`, and `map/1`.
- Switching the projection does not require rewriting or translating the source payload at the adapter boundary.
- Existing graph/seq behavior remains green.
- Map uses the same source and preserves spatial/bounds semantics.
- Tests prove `same input hash -> three valid projections`.
- No new renderer and no new top-level DSL are introduced.

Refs #271"}

state.body:
## Purpose

Integrate Contract Model Atlas into `ui.git` without turning `ui.git` into a source authority or state store.

The intended shape is:

> Contract Model Atlas is not a new meaning system inside `ui.git`.
> Upstream contract meaning is folded once into `ui.contractModelAtlas.view.v1`.
> A2UI reads that view from `/atlas` and emits preview/evidence only.

## Context

Current `ui.git` already owns the A2UI / SDUI component registry, renderer-neutral projection package, adapter artifact producer, and non-authority evidence surfaces.

The current repo boundary says:

- runtime input is produced outside this repo
- A2UI is build input
- JSONL in this repo is attached data
- fixtures are stateless and non-authoritative
- `ui.git` is not a state store
- generated HTML, manifests, previews, and receipts are build evidence only

The uploaded Contract Model Atlas preview demonstrates a useful target shape:

- A2UI registry + shell + data JSONL
- data is supplied as `updateDataModel` under `/atlas`
- atlas view has `containers[]`, `elements[]`, `edges[]`, `treeText`, `edgeList`, and `diagnostics`
- rendering is ERD-like: nested boxes plus edges
- generated artifacts are not authority
- adapter does not own state

## Decision

Add only the thin read model and artifact pipeline required to render this safely.

| Area | Decision |
|---|---|
| New UI model | Add `ui.contractModelAtlas.view.v1` |
| Independent IRs | Do not create separate `Container`, `Element`, or `Edge` IR families |
| Upstream contract schemas | Do not redefine them in `ui.git` |
| A2UI data path | Use `/atlas` only |
| Renderer | Stateless artifact host only |
| Authority | No approval, no admission, no merge/fire authorization |
| CI proof | Check boundary, digest, fixture, and artifact reproducibility |

## Scope

- Add `packages/core-port/src/contract-model-atlas-view.mjs` for validation, normalization, and digesting of `ui.contractModelAtlas.view.v1`.
- Export the new helper surface from `packages/core-port/src/index.mjs`.
- Add the smallest needed registry/catalog alignment:
  - add `ForEach` as a layout component if still absent
  - align `List` props with `rows` if required by the shell contract
- Add checked-in fixtures under `tests/fixtures/contract-model-atlas/**`:
  - `contract.json`
  - `registry.json`
  - `shell.v0.9.jsonl`
  - `data.contract-model-atlas.v1.jsonl`
- Add tests that prove:
  - the view model shape is valid
  - the shell contains no data messages
  - data cartridge contains only `updateDataModel`
  - data updates only the declared `/atlas` path
  - root data update is rejected
  - unknown data path is rejected
  - raw HTML is rejected in data
  - authority fields are rejected
  - generated artifacts are evidence only
- Add `scripts/build-contract-model-atlas-artifact.mjs` to produce a replayable preview artifact.
- Add a Nix package/check in `flake.nix`.
- Add CI intent only if an exported artifact is required beyond `nix flake check`.

## Non-scope

- No upstream contract schema ownership inside `ui.git`.
- No accepted decision authority.
- No state store.
- No final governance admission.
- No branch protection mutation.
- No replacement of the existing purpose visualization pipeline.
- No broad generic renderer rewrite.
- No attempt to make generated HTML a source of truth.

## Acceptance criteria

- `nix flake check --print-build-logs` passes.
- `tests/run-all.mjs` includes the Contract Model Atlas checks.
- The artifact contains replayable source inputs and a machine-readable receipt.
- The receipt states `generatedArtifactsAreAuthority: false`.
- The adapter/renderer declares or proves `ownsState: false`.
- The A2UI shell can be compiled without data.
- Changing only the `/atlas` data changes the preview digest but not the shell digest.
- The rendered view uses existing primitive SVG components where possible.
- No new authority language appears in README, package claims, proof reports, or receipts.

## Preferred minimal file map

| Path | Role |
|---|---|
| `packages/core-port/src/contract-model-atlas-view.mjs` | read model validation / normalization |
| `packages/core-port/src/catalog.mjs` | minimal component catalog alignment |
| `packages/core-port/src/index.mjs` | export surface |
| `tests/fixtures/contract-model-atlas/**` | checked-in sample input |
| `tests/check-contract-model-atlas-view.mjs` | read model and boundary test |
| `tests/check-contract-model-atlas-artifact.mjs` | artifact replay / digest test |
| `scripts/build-contract-model-atlas-artifact.mjs` | generated artifact producer |
| `flake.nix` | package/check exposure |

## Merge-blocking conditions

- `ui.git` redefines upstream contract meaning instead of reading a view model.
- `ui.git` stores or mutates live state.
- Shell JSONL contains `updateDataModel` rows.
- Data JSONL updates any path other than `/atlas`.
- Generated HTML or manifest is described as authority.
- Artifact builder embeds unbounded display data where external JSONL should be replayable.
- Tests do not include negative controls for authority fields and raw HTML.

## Closing statement

This issue is complete when Contract Model Atlas is integrated as a small, replayable, non-authority A2UI read-model artifact, and not as a new UI meaning system.
