{"body":"## Problem

Model selection is configured through a growing set of independent, flat settings. Each has its own ID format, its own meaning for "empty", and its own picker UX. Three recent developments make this worse:

1. **The runtime prompt advertises `/subagents`, which VS Code doesn't expose.** In the Copilot runtime's `task` tool schema, the `model`, `reasoning_effort`, and `context_tier` descriptions all say: *"The runtime resolves `/subagents` preferences when these fields are omitted; do not copy them merely because they appear in `<subagent_model_preferences>`."* `/subagents` is a CLI command, and VS Code intentionally hides it (it is in `HIDDEN_RUNTIME_COMMANDS` in `copilotSlashCommandCompletionProvider.ts`). So the model is told about a preference surface that VS Code users can't reach, while VS Code has its own unrelated per-subagent settings (below). The same schema also injects a flat `model` enum containing every available model (22 in the e2e snapshots, and 50+ in a real session with BYOK and OpenRouter models), plus prose lists of which models support each reasoning effort and long context.
2. **Many settings use very long flat lists.** Several settings build a dynamic enum of every user-selectable chat model (`DefaultModelContribution`). With BYOK, OpenRouter, and on-device models, each of these becomes a long, flat, unsearchable dropdown (#317420). The Settings editor repeats it once per setting, and each copy has to be repopulated whenever models change. Other settings are free-form strings with no discovery or validation (#319191).
3. **Non-chat models are arriving.** Image generation is a boolean (`chat.copilot.imageGeneration.enabled`) with the model hard-coded to GPT Image 2.5 Sunburst, so users can't choose an image model. Speech, voice, embeddings, completions, NES, and on-device models each have separate settings too. `ILanguageModelsService` is centered on chat models, and nothing shared describes "the model for capability X".

We need one unified way to configure all of these.

## Inventory of current cases

### Main conversation

| Setting | Owner | Shape | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `chat.defaultModel` | workbench | free string (`auto`, family alias such as `opus`, or full id) | Policy-backed (`ChatDefaultModel`, managed `model` / `permissions.model`) |
| `inlineChat.defaultModel` | workbench | dynamic enum of all tool-calling models | `Name (vendor)` format |
| Per-session model picker | workbench | state, not a setting | |

### Agents and subagents

| Setting / surface | Owner | Shape | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `chat.planAgent.defaultModel` | workbench | dynamic enum | `Name (vendor)` format |
| `chat.exploreAgent.defaultModel` | workbench | dynamic enum | `Name (vendor)` format |
| `github.copilot.chat.exploreAgent.model` | Copilot extension | free string | Duplicates the workbench setting above |
| `github.copilot.chat.askAgent.model` | Copilot extension | free string | |
| `github.copilot.chat.implementAgent.model` | Copilot extension | free string | |
| `github.copilot.chat.searchSubagent.model` | Copilot extension | free string | Extension harness |
| `chat.copilot.searchSubagent.model` | agent host | free string (CAPI model id) | Agent host harness; restarts the SDK client |
| `github.copilot.chat.executionSubagent.model` | Copilot extension | free string, default `gpt-5.6-luna` | Description and defaults are inconsistent (#341517) |
| `chat.agentHost.copilot.executionSubagent.model` | agent host | free string (runtime model id), default `gpt-5.6-luna` | Empty means "inherit parent"; restarts the runtime |
| `.agent.md` `model:` frontmatter | prompt files | `Name (vendor)` | Doesn't map to `task` tool ids (#340844) |
| `task` tool `model` / `reasoning_effort` / `context_tier` | Copilot runtime | chosen by the model; flat enum | Points to `/subagents` and `<subagent_model_preferences>` |
| CLI `/subagents` preferences | Copilot runtime | CLI config | Not reachable from VS Code |

### Utility and background flows

| Setting | Shape | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `chat.utilityModel` | dynamic enum | `vendor/id` format |
| `chat.utilitySmallModel` | dynamic enum | `vendor/id` format; synced to the agent host |
| `chat.byokUtilityModelDefault` | enum `none` / `mainAgent` / `copilot` | Only applies when the main model is BYOK |
| `chat.tools.riskAssessment.model` | free string, default `copilot-utility-small` | |
| `dictation.experimental.llmCleanupModel` | fixed enum (`auto`, `copilot-utility-small`, `gpt-5.6-luna`) | |
| Commit message generation | n/a | Requested in #328619 |

### Auto, routing, and per-model behavior

| Setting | Shape |
|---|---|
| `github.copilot.chat.autoModeTierOverride` | string / null |
| `chat.copilot.ensemble.enabled`, `chat.copilot.ensemble.intelligenceUsesHydraFusion`, `chat.copilot.hydraFusion.enabled`, `chat.modelPicker.fusionInlineTiers` | booleans / variants |
| `chat.agentHost.copilot.modelCapabilityOverrides` and `github.copilot.chat.modelCapabilityOverrides` | per-model object maps, duplicated across harnesses |

### On-device and BYOK

| Setting | Shape |
|---|---|
| `chat.copilot.localModel.enabled`, `chat.copilot.localModel.useInAuto`, `chat.copilot.localModel.llamaServerPath` | boolean / boolean / path |
| `chat.agentHost.byokModels.enabled` | boolean |

### Non-chat modalities

| Capability | Setting | Shape | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Image generation and editing | `chat.copilot.imageGeneration.enabled` | boolean | Model hard-coded to GPT Image 2.5 Sunburst; pricing lives in the description |
| Dictation (speech to text) | `dictation.model` | fixed enum (on-device Nemotron / MAI cloud) | Policy-backed |
| Voice Mode (realtime) | `agents.voice.useBYOKVoiceModel` | free string (OpenAI live model id) | |
| Code completions | `github.copilot.selectedCompletionModel` | free string, set through a command | |
| Next edit suggestions | `github.copilot.nextEditSuggestions.preferredModel`, `github.copilot.chat.inlineEdits.xtabProvider.modelConfiguration` | string / object | |
| Embeddings | `github.copilot.chat.workspace.preferredEmbeddingsModel` | free string | |
| Instant apply | `github.copilot.chat.instantApply.shortContextModelName` | free string | |

### Other places models are chosen

| Surface | Shape | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `.prompt.md` `model:` | string or ordered list | The first available model wins |
| `.agent.md` `model:` and `reasoningEffort:` | string or ordered list / enum | `model` only applies in the Copilot harness |
| `chatLanguageModels.json` (per profile) | JSON file | BYOK providers and per-model configuration (`configurationSchema`), kept outside `settings.json` |
| Model picker visibility (hide/show models) | profile storage | Not a setting, so users can't edit it directly and admins can't manage it |
| Agents window **Compare Models** | attempts, judge, synthesizer | Three more role-like model choices |
| Codex harness `codex.modelReasoningEffort` | session config | Harness-specific effort control |
| Agent handoffs `model:` in `.agent.md` | string | Uses the `Name (vendor)` format, for example `"GPT-5 (copilot)"`, so it has the same ID mismatch as #340844 |
| MCP server sampling: `chat.mcp.serverSampling` → `allowedModels` | list for each server | Chosen through a separate quick pick |
| Completions status-bar picker ("Change Completions Model...") | Copilot extension UI | A separate picker that writes `github.copilot.selectedCompletionModel` |

## Inconsistencies

- **ID formats.** Settings use `Name (vendor)` qualified names (plan, explore, inline chat, `.agent.md`), `vendor/id` (utility models), CAPI ids (search subagent), runtime ids (execution subagent, `task` tool), family aliases (`chat.defaultModel`), and `provider/Provider/model` for BYOK models in the `task` tool enum. #340844 is a direct result of this.
- **Empty values mean different things.** Depending on the setting, an empty value means "Auto (Vendor Default)", "runtime default", "inherit the parent session model", "use configured default behavior", or "use the hosted model".
- **Picker UX.** Settings use dynamic enums (unsearchable, repeated per setting, rebuilt on model changes), free-form strings (no discovery or validation), or fixed enums.
- **Duplication across harnesses.** The same concept has both a `github.copilot.chat.*` setting and a `chat.*` / `chat.agentHost.*` setting with different semantics. Examples include the explore, search, and execution subagent models and the capability overrides (#341517).
- **Apply semantics.** Some settings apply immediately. Others restart the SDK client or runtime after active turns finish.
- **Policy.** Only `chat.defaultModel` and `dictation.model` can be managed by policy.
- **Prompt cost.** The full model list, plus per-model reasoning-effort and long-context lists, is injected into every `task` tool schema.

## Proposal (strawman)

- **Capability-aware model registry.** Describe models by capability (chat, image generation and editing, speech to text, realtime voice, embeddings, completions), so that image and other non-chat models can be listed, gated, priced, and picked like chat models.
- **One home for each model choice.** Choices made while chatting stay in the input's model picker (chat, inline chat), with one order for which model a new conversation starts with. Agent models belong to the agent: built-in and custom agents, including subagents, get a model in the Agents list. Everything with no picker at the point of use (utility, image, dictation, voice, embeddings, completions) goes on one Feature models page. Use explicit `auto` / "same as conversation" / inherit values instead of empty strings, and allow optional reasoning effort and context tier. See the proposal comment below.
- **One canonical model reference format.** Accept it in settings, `.agent.md` frontmatter, the `task` tool, and policy. Normalize the legacy formats on read.
- **One searchable picker.** Group models by vendor and capability, and show pricing in AI credits. Use the same picker in the Settings editor, Models management, and the chat model picker, instead of injecting dynamic enums into the settings schema.
- **Bridge to runtime subagent preferences.** Feed VS Code role assignments into the runtime's subagent preferences so that `<subagent_model_preferences>` reflects what the user configured in VS Code. Otherwise, stop advertising `/subagents` in VS Code sessions. Also consider trimming the flat `model` enum from the `task` tool schema.
- **Policy.** Expose role assignments through managed settings so admins can control more than the default model, including image models.
- **Migration.** Deprecate the per-feature settings, migrate their values, and remove the duplicates between `github.copilot.chat.*` and `chat.agentHost.*`.

## Resolution order

The runtime already reports where a subagent's model came from (`AgentSubagentTaskModelSource`: `task_argument`, `subagent_configuration`, `custom_agent_definition`, `unset`). However, the order isn't documented, and users can't see which source won. A unified design should define one order across all roles, for example: an explicit request in the current turn, then the custom agent definition, then the role assignment, then inheriting the parent model, then `auto`. The UI (subagent pill, debug view) should show the resolved model and where it came from.

## When the configured model is unavailable

Behavior differs by surface:

- `chat.copilot.searchSubagent.model`: an unavailable model makes the search tool unavailable.
- `chat.agentHost.copilot.executionSubagent.model`: an unavailable model disables the runtime execution subagent.
- `.prompt.md` / `.agent.md`: the file can list models in order, and the first available one is used.
- `chat.defaultModel`: a family alias resolves to the latest available model in that family.

We should pick one behavior (for example, an ordered fallback list plus a visible notice) and apply it to every role.

## Experiments, sync, and scope

- Many of these settings are experiment-controlled (`experiment: { mode: 'auto' | 'startup' }`), and some track whether the value is still controlled by its default (`executionSubagentModelDefaultControlled`). A unified setting must tell experiment-provided defaults apart from explicit user choices. #341517 shows the reset / "modified" confusion this causes today.
- Settings Sync can carry a model ID to another machine, account, or org where that model isn't available or is blocked by policy.
- Scopes are inconsistent: some of these settings are `APPLICATION`, some `APPLICATION_MACHINE`, some `MACHINE`, and some use the default window scope. We need to decide whether workspace-level overrides are allowed. Repos can already pin models through `.agent.md`.

## Extension API

The `speech`, `embeddings`, `languageModelCapabilities`, and `languageModelPricing` APIs are proposed, but there is nothing for image models. Models that extensions contribute, of any modality, should be able to appear in the same registry and be assigned to roles.

## Cost visibility

Pricing is no longer one number. Each model has AI credit rates per 1M tokens for input, cached input, cache writes, and output, sometimes with separate long-context rates, and image models add separate image-token rates. Today, image generation pricing appears only in the setting's description, and subagent and utility model choices don't show pricing at all, so picking a more expensive subagent model silently increases cost. Every role should show a relative price indicator (`priceCategory`), with the full AI credit breakdown on hover or in the picker's details.

## Requirements

- Hide the unified surface when AI features are disabled (`ChatContextKeys.enabled` / `chat.disableAIFeatures`).
- Make the picker keyboard- and screen-reader-accessible: searchable, grouped, and with proper ARIA labels.
- Allow admins to manage role assignments, including restricting or disabling image generation.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every model choice in the inventory has exactly one home: the picker, the agent, or the Feature models page.
- [ ] Settings, prompt and agent files, the `task` tool, and policy all accept one model reference format, and legacy formats are migrated.
- [ ] Image models and other non-chat models can be selected, with their AI credit pricing shown.
- [ ] The resolution order and unavailable-model behavior are documented, and each subagent shows its resolved model and where it came from.
- [ ] The runtime prompt only references preferences that VS Code users can actually set.
- [ ] The per-feature settings are deprecated, with automatic migration.

## Open questions

- Where does the unified configuration live: `settings.json`, `chatLanguageModels.json`, or a dedicated Models editor backed by one of them?
- Are roles shared across harnesses (Copilot, Claude, Codex), with harness-specific overrides, or defined per harness?
- Are reasoning effort and context tier part of the role assignment, or per-model settings (as in `modelCapabilityOverrides`)?
- Are workspace-level role overrides allowed?
- How do org policies restrict which models are available for each role?

## Related

#319191, #317420, #341517, #340844, #328619, #325069




"}

- **Policy.** Expose role assignments through managed settings so admins can control more than the default model, including image models.
- **Migration.** Deprecate the per-feature settings, migrate their values, and remove the duplicates between `github.copilot.chat.*` and `chat.agentHost.*`.

## Resolution order

The runtime already reports where a subagent's model came from (`AgentSubagentTaskModelSource`: `task_argument`, `subagent_configuration`, `custom_agent_definition`, `unset`). However, the order isn't documented, and users can't see which source won. A unified design should define one order across all roles, for example: an explicit request in the current turn, then the custom agent definition, then the role assignment, then inheriting the parent model, then `auto`. The UI (subagent pill, debug view) should show the resolved model and where it came from.

## When the configured model is unavailable

Behavior differs by surface:

- `chat.copilot.searchSubagent.model`: an unavailable model makes the search tool unavailable.
- `chat.agentHost.copilot.executionSubagent.model`: an unavailable model disables the runtime execution subagent.
- `.prompt.md` / `.agent.md`: the file can list models in order, and the first available one is used.
- `chat.defaultModel`: a family alias resolves to the latest available model in that family.

We should pick one behavior (for example, an ordered fallback list plus a visible notice) and apply it to every role.

## Experiments, sync, and scope

- Many of these settings are experiment-controlled (`experiment: { mode: 'auto' | 'startup' }`), and some track whether the value is still controlled by its default (`executionSubagentModelDefaultControlled`). A unified setting must tell experiment-provided defaults apart from explicit user choices. #341517 shows the reset / "modified" confusion this causes today.
- Settings Sync can carry a model ID to another machine, account, or org where that model isn't available or is blocked by policy.
- Scopes are inconsistent: some of these settings are `APPLICATION`, some `APPLICATION_MACHINE`, some `MACHINE`, and some use the default window scope. We need to decide whether workspace-level overrides are allowed. Repos can already pin models through `.agent.md`.

## Extension API

The `speech`, `embeddings`, `languageModelCapabilities`, and `languageModelPricing` APIs are proposed, but there is nothing for image models. Models that extensions contribute, of any modality, should be able to appear in the same registry and be assigned to roles.

## Cost visibility

Pricing is no longer one number. Each model has AI credit rates per 1M tokens for input, cached input, cache writes, and output, sometimes with separate long-context rates, and image models add separate image-token rates. Today, image generation pricing appears only in the setting's description, and subagent and utility model choices don't show pricing at all, so picking a more expensive subagent model silently increases cost. Every role should show a relative price indicator (`priceCategory`), with the full AI credit breakdown on hover or in the picker's details.

## Requirements

- Hide the unified surface when AI features are disabled (`ChatContextKeys.enabled` / `chat.disableAIFeatures`).
- Make the picker keyboard- and screen-reader-accessible: searchable, grouped, and with proper ARIA labels.
- Allow admins to manage role assignments, including restricting or disabling image generation.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every model choice in the inventory has exactly one home: the picker, the agent, or the Feature models page.
- [ ] Settings, prompt and agent files, the `task` tool, and policy all accept one model reference format, and legacy formats are migrated.
- [ ] Image models and other non-chat models can be selected, with their AI credit pricing shown.
- [ ] The resolution order and unavailable-model behavior are documented, and each subagent shows its resolved model and where it came from.
- [ ] The runtime prompt only references preferences that VS Code users can actually set.
- [ ] The per-feature settings are deprecated, with automatic migration.

## Open questions

- Where does the unified configuration live: `settings.json`, `chatLanguageModels.json`, or a dedicated Models editor backed by one of them?
- Are roles shared across harnesses (Copilot, Claude, Codex), with harness-specific overrides, or defined per harness?
- Are reasoning effort and context tier part of the role assignment, or per-model settings (as in `modelCapabilityOverrides`)?
- Are workspace-level role overrides allowed?
- How do org policies restrict which models are available for each role?

## Related

#319191, #317420, #341517, #340844, #328619, #325069

### Nixpkgs version

- Unstable (26.11)

### Describe the bug

Since a43236f0859d `kernel.dev` ships `System.map`. The kernel's `scripts/depmod.sh` only skips depmod when `System.map` is missing, so out-of-tree modules that install through `make modules_install INSTALL_MOD_PATH=$out` now run depmod and write `modules.dep`, `modules.symbols.bin`, `modules.alias` and so on into their own output.

`aggregateModules` then fails because those files collide with the kernel's:

```
pkgs.buildEnv error: two given paths contain a conflicting subpath:
  `/nix/store/93n5879v79ljfdhaglr8p4kxndrgmq0d-v4l2loopback-0.15.4/lib/modules/7.2.11/modules.symbols.bin' and
  `/nix/store/36c6ybh6gv1mbnfq5n5sbqy2ghbdcgsa-linux-7.2.11-modules/lib/modules/7.2.11/modules.symbols.bin'
```

v4l2loopback runs `sed -i '/depmod/d' Makefile`, but that only removes its own depmod call. The kernel's `Makefile.modinst` still runs `DEPMOD`:

```
  INSTALL /nix/store/...-v4l2loopback-0.15.4/lib/modules/7.2.11/updates/v4l2loopback.ko
  DEPMOD  /nix/store/...-v4l2loopback-0.15.4/lib/modules/7.2.11
depmod: WARNING: could not open modules.order at ...
```

Any other external module that installs through `modules_install` probably hits the same thing.

### Steps to reproduce

```nix
boot.kernelPackages = pkgs.linuxPackages_latest; # 7.2.11
boot.extraModulePackages = [ config.boot.kernelPackages.v4l2loopback ];
```

### Minimal reproducer

```nix

```

### Expected behaviour

External module outputs contain only the modules, and `aggregateModules` regenerates the depmod files itself, as it did before.

```console

```

{"body":"### Nixpkgs version

- Unstable (26.11)

### Describe the bug

Since a43236f0859d `kernel.dev` ships `System.map`. The kernel's `scripts/depmod.sh` only skips depmod when `System.map` is missing, so out-of-tree modules that install through `make modules_install INSTALL_MOD_PATH=$out` now run depmod and write `modules.dep`, `modules.symbols.bin`, `modules.alias` and so on into their own output.

`aggregateModules` then fails because those files collide with the kernel's:

```
pkgs.buildEnv error: two given paths contain a conflicting subpath:
  `/nix/store/93n5879v79ljfdhaglr8p4kxndrgmq0d-v4l2loopback-0.15.4/lib/modules/7.2.11/modules.symbols.bin' and
  `/nix/store/36c6ybh6gv1mbnfq5n5sbqy2ghbdcgsa-linux-7.2.11-modules/lib/modules/7.2.11/modules.symbols.bin'
```

v4l2loopback runs `sed -i '/depmod/d' Makefile`, but that only removes its own depmod call. The kernel's `Makefile.modinst` still runs `DEPMOD`:

```
  INSTALL /nix/store/...-v4l2loopback-0.15.4/lib/modules/7.2.11/updates/v4l2loopback.ko
  DEPMOD  /nix/store/...-v4l2loopback-0.15.4/lib/modules/7.2.11
depmod: WARNING: could not open modules.order at ...
```

Any other external module that installs through `modules_install` probably hits the same thing.

### Steps to reproduce

```nix
boot.kernelPackages = pkgs.linuxPackages_latest; # 7.2.11
boot.extraModulePackages = [ config.boot.kernelPackages.v4l2loopback ];
```

### Minimal reproducer

```nix

```

### Expected behaviour

External module outputs contain only the modules, and `aggregateModules` regenerates the depmod files itself, as it did before.

```

{"body":"### Request

Please consider packaging [xonedo](https://github.com/OpenGamingCollective/xonedo) and providing NixOS integration as an alternative to the current `xone` + `xpad-noone` setup, with a view to replacing that combination where feature coverage allows.

### Motivation

Currently, `hardware.xone.enable` blacklists `xpad` and enables `hardware.xpad-noone.enable` by default. This requires an additional out-of-tree driver to retain support for devices otherwise handled by xpad.

xonedo is a fork of dlundqvist/xone focused on Xbox One and Xbox Series X|S accessories connected through the Xbox Wireless Dongle. Upstream explicitly states that it does not disable the kernel's xpad driver.

Using xonedo alongside the in-tree xpad driver could therefore eliminate the need for xpad-noone in this configuration.

### Suggested approach

- Package xonedo for the supported kernel package sets.
- Provide a NixOS option to enable it, including the required dongle firmware.
- Keep xpad available instead of enabling xpad-noone.
- Evaluate migration from the existing options and document any differences.

### Compatibility considerations

This should not be treated as an unconditional drop-in replacement: upstream directs wired-device users to xone and Bluetooth users to xpadneo.

Before changing defaults or removing existing packages, please assess whether xpad covers the wired devices and features currently supported by xone, including accessories beyond standard gamepads.

### References

- https://github.com/OpenGamingCollective/xonedo
- https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/master/nixos/modules/hardware/xone.nix
- https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/master/nixos/modules/hardware/xpad-noone.nix
"}

state.body:
We support a large enterprise organization transitioning from the VS Code Local harness to the Copilot harness.

Could the active harness be exposed as authoritative runtime context to the agent and skills?

This is important because Local and Copilot harnesses currently require different configuration in areas such as MCP. Our existing internal MCP guidance is largely based on the Local harness, while we need to help users migrate safely to the Copilot harness.

We would like to build a skill that detects the user's current harness, validates their MCP configuration against internal documentation, and provides harness-specific migration and troubleshooting guidance.

However, the Local harness does not appear to provide the model with reliable knowledge that it is running under the Local harness. The model therefore has to infer or guess.

Even under the Copilot harness I received:

> My best answer is the Copilot harness. I’m an AI assistant using Copilot SDK in VS Code...
> 
> That said, I don’t have an independently verified runtime indicator exposing the active harness.

For a troubleshooting skill, inference is not sufficient.

Please expose something equivalent to `harness: local` or `harness: copilot` to the model/skills, and ideally through the SDK/runtime API as well.

This would enable deterministic harness-aware skills and make migration from Local to Copilot harness significantly easier to support in enterprise environments.


### Additional info

We require supporting our users with special migrations as Copilot harness has poor support for securely handling PAT tokens that some of our internally hosted MCP's still require. E.g. JIRA and Confluence MCP's do not support OAuth authentication if not hosted in the (atlassian) cloud and the migration while being planned will take time.

request.text:
{"body":"We support a large enterprise organization transitioning from the VS Code Local harness to the Copilot harness.

Could the active harness be exposed as authoritative runtime context to the agent and skills?

This is important because Local and Copilot harnesses currently require different configuration in areas such as MCP. Our existing internal MCP guidance is largely based on the Local harness, while we need to help users migrate safely to the Copilot harness.

We would like to build a skill that detects the user's current harness, validates their MCP configuration against internal documentation, and provides harness-specific migration and troubleshooting guidance.

However, the Local harness does not appear to provide the model with reliable knowledge that it is running under the Local harness. The model therefore has to infer or guess.

Even under the Copilot harness I received:

> My best answer is the Copilot harness. I’m an AI assistant using Copilot SDK in VS Code...
> 
> That said, I don’t have an independently verified runtime indicator exposing the active harness.

For a troubleshooting skill, inference is not sufficient.

Please expose something equivalent to `harness: local` or `harness: copilot` to the model/skills, and ideally through the SDK/runtime API as well.

This would enable deterministic harness-aware skills and make migration from Local to Copilot harness significantly easier to support in enterprise environments.


### Additional info

We require supporting our users with special migrations as Copilot harness has poor support for securely handling PAT tokens that some of our internally hosted MCP's still require. E.g. JIRA and Confluence MCP's do not support OAuth authentication if not hosted in the (atlassian) cloud and the migration while being planned will take time.

state.body:
### Nixpkgs version

- Unstable (26.11)

### Describe the bug

Since the nixos-unstable update that moved patchelf from 0.15.2 to 0.19.2, `nvidia-smi` from `nvidia-x11` segfaults immediately on every invocation, before any library is loaded. The driver itself is unaffected (kernel module loads, desktop/GPU work); only the patched `bin/` executables are broken.

This looks like the upstream patchelf bug NixOS/patchelf#674: running `--interpreter` and `--set-rpath` in **one** patchelf invocation produces a broken binary. The nvidia-x11 builder does exactly that for `nvidia-smi`, `nvidia-cuda-mps-*`, `nvidia-debugdump` and `nvidia-powerd`:

https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/09063bd1f2b36fd9fd793c36dfade7bd40a93dfc/pkgs/os-specific/linux/nvidia-x11/builder.sh#L203-L204

```sh
patchelf --interpreter "$(cat $NIX_CC/nix-support/dynamic-linker)" \
    --set-rpath $out/lib:$libPath $bin/bin/$i
```

In the resulting ELF the read-only `LOAD` segment overlaps the writable one and `.dynamic` ends up mapped read-only, so `ld.so` crashes with `SEGV_ACCERR` in `dl_main` (presumably when it writes `DT_DEBUG`).

Program headers of the old (working) and new (broken) build of the same driver:

```
old (patchelf 0.15.2)
  LOAD     0x000000 0x3ff000 ... 0x001000 RW
  DYNAMIC  0x000318 0x3ff318 ... 0x0001f0 RW
  LOAD     0x001000 0x400000 ... 0x003418 R
  Segment 03: .dynamic                                    <- inside the RW LOAD

new (patchelf 0.19.2)
  LOAD     0x000000 0x3ff000 ... 0x002670 RW              <- covers up to 0x401670
  LOAD     0x0012c4 0x4002c4 ... 0x003154 R               <- starts at 0x4002c4, overlaps
  DYNAMIC  0x002480 0x401480 ... 0x0001f0 RW
  Segment 06: .dynstr .dynamic .gnu.version ... .rela.plt <- .dynamic inside the R LOAD
```

Things ruled out:
- **glibc** (2.44-25 -> 2.44-57 changed in the same update): the old binary runs fine with the new `ld.so`, and the new binary crashes with the old `ld.so`.
- **Libraries**: `LD_DEBUG=libs` prints nothing before the crash, so no library has been loaded yet; forcing the previous openssl also still crashes.
- **Driver version**: unchanged (615.78.08) between the working and broken builds.

### Steps to reproduce

1. On nixos-unstable (09063bd) with `hardware.nvidia` enabled (proprietary driver 615.78.08, RTX 4070 SUPER), run `nvidia-smi`.
2. It segfaults (exit 139).

Standalone reproducer, re-patching the unmodified binary nixpkgs ships in `origBin/` with patchelf 0.19.2 from nixpkgs:

```sh
BIN=$(dirname $(dirname $(readlink -f $(command -v nvidia-smi))))   # nvidia-x11-*-bin output
RP=$(patchelf --print-rpath $BIN/bin/nvidia-smi)
INT=$(patchelf --print-interpreter $BIN/bin/nvidia-smi)

# single invocation, as builder.sh does
cp $BIN/origBin/nvidia-smi single && chmod +w single
patchelf --interpreter $INT --set-rpath "$RP" single
cmp single $BIN/bin/nvidia-smi && echo identical   # -> identical to the nixpkgs binary
./single -L                                        # -> Segmentation fault (exit 139)

# two invocations, rpath first
cp $BIN/origBin/nvidia-smi split && chmod +w split
patchelf --set-rpath "$RP" split
patchelf --interpreter $INT split
./split -L                                         # -> GPU 0: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4070 SUPER ... (exit 0)
```


### Minimal reproducer

```nix
Re-patching the unmodified binary nixpkgs ships in `origBin/`, with patchelf 0.19.2 from nixpkgs:

{"body":"### Nixpkgs version

- Unstable (26.11)

### Describe the bug

Since the nixos-unstable update that moved patchelf from 0.15.2 to 0.19.2, `nvidia-smi` from `nvidia-x11` segfaults immediately on every invocation, before any library is loaded. The driver itself is unaffected (kernel module loads, desktop/GPU work); only the patched `bin/` executables are broken.

This looks like the upstream patchelf bug NixOS/patchelf#674: running `--interpreter` and `--set-rpath` in **one** patchelf invocation produces a broken binary. The nvidia-x11 builder does exactly that for `nvidia-smi`, `nvidia-cuda-mps-*`, `nvidia-debugdump` and `nvidia-powerd`:

https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/blob/09063bd1f2b36fd9fd793c36dfade7bd40a93dfc/pkgs/os-specific/linux/nvidia-x11/builder.sh#L203-L204

```sh
patchelf --interpreter "$(cat $NIX_CC/nix-support/dynamic-linker)" \
    --set-rpath $out/lib:$libPath $bin/bin/$i
```

In the resulting ELF the read-only `LOAD` segment overlaps the writable one and `.dynamic` ends up mapped read-only, so `ld.so` crashes with `SEGV_ACCERR` in `dl_main` (presumably when it writes `DT_DEBUG`).

Program headers of the old (working) and new (broken) build of the same driver:

```
old (patchelf 0.15.2)
  LOAD     0x000000 0x3ff000 ... 0x001000 RW
  DYNAMIC  0x000318 0x3ff318 ... 0x0001f0 RW
  LOAD     0x001000 0x400000 ... 0x003418 R
  Segment 03: .dynamic                                    <- inside the RW LOAD

new (patchelf 0.19.2)
  LOAD     0x000000 0x3ff000 ... 0x002670 RW              <- covers up to 0x401670
  LOAD     0x0012c4 0x4002c4 ... 0x003154 R               <- starts at 0x4002c4, overlaps
  DYNAMIC  0x002480 0x401480 ... 0x0001f0 RW
  Segment 06: .dynstr .dynamic .gnu.version ... .rela.plt <- .dynamic inside the R LOAD
```

Things ruled out:
- **glibc** (2.44-25 -> 2.44-57 changed in the same update): the old binary runs fine with the new `ld.so`, and the new binary crashes with the old `ld.so`.
- **Libraries**: `LD_DEBUG=libs` prints nothing before the crash, so no library has been loaded yet; forcing the previous openssl also still crashes.
- **Driver version**: unchanged (615.78.08) between the working and broken builds.

### Steps to reproduce

1. On nixos-unstable (09063bd) with `hardware.nvidia` enabled (proprietary driver 615.78.08, RTX 4070 SUPER), run `nvidia-smi`.
2. It segfaults (exit 139).

Standalone reproducer, re-patching the unmodified binary nixpkgs ships in `origBin/` with patchelf 0.19.2 from nixpkgs:

```sh
BIN=$(dirname $(dirname $(readlink -f $(command -v nvidia-smi))))   # nvidia-x11-*-bin output
RP=$(patchelf --print-rpath $BIN/bin/nvidia-smi)
INT=$(patchelf --print-interpreter $BIN/bin/nvidia-smi)

# single invocation, as builder.sh does
cp $BIN/origBin/nvidia-smi single && chmod +w single
patchelf --interpreter $INT --set-rpath "$RP" single
cmp single $BIN/bin/nvidia-smi && echo identical   # -> identical to the nixpkgs binary
./single -L                                        # -> Segmentation fault (exit 139)

# two invocations, rpath first
cp $BIN/origBin/nvidia-smi split && chmod +w split
patchelf --set-rpath "$RP" split
patchelf --interpreter $INT split
./split -L                                         # -> GPU 0: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4070 SUPER ... (exit 0)
```


### Minimal reproducer

```nix
Re-patching the unmodified binary nixpkgs ships in `origBin/`, with patchelf 0.19.2 from nixpkgs:


BIN=$(dirname $(dirname $(readlink -f $(command -v nvidia-smi))))   # nvidia-x11-*-bin output
RP=$(patchelf --print-rpath $BIN/bin/nvidia-smi)
INT=$(patchelf --print-interpreter $BIN/bin/nvidia-smi)

# single invocation, as builder.sh does
cp $BIN/origBin/nvidia-smi single && chmod +w single
patchelf --interpreter $INT --set-rpath "$RP" single
cmp single $BIN/bin/nvidia-smi && echo identical   # -> identical to the nixpkgs binary
./single -L                                        # -> Segmentation fault (exit 139)

# two invocations, rpath first
cp $BIN/origBin/nvidia-smi split && chmod +w split
patchelf --set-rpath "$RP" split
patchelf --interpreter $INT split
./split -L                                         # -> GPU 0: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4070 SUPER ... (exit 0)
```

### Expected behaviour

`nvidia-smi` runs, as it did with the previous build of the same driver (patched with patchelf 0.15.2).

### Screenshots

_No response_

### Relevant log output

```console
$ nvidia-smi
Segmentation fault (core dumped)

systemd-coredump stack trace:
#0  dl_main (/nix/store/...-glibc-2.44-57/lib/ld-linux-x86-64.so.2 + 0x25a74)
#1  _dl_sysdep_start
#2  _dl_start
#3  _start
Signal: 11 (SEGV) si_code: SEGV_ACCERR
```

### Additional context

- Any systemd unit that calls `nvidia-smi` (e.g. one running `nvidia-smi -pm 1` at boot) now fails on every boot and every `nixos-rebuild switch`.
- Upstream patchelf bug: https://github.com/NixOS/patchelf/issues/674 (another NixOS user confirms it with driver 595.104.02 on an RTX 3080).
- Possible fix in nixpkgs until patchelf is fixed: split the call in `builder.sh` into `patchelf --set-rpath ...` followed by a separate `patchelf --interpreter ...`.

AI disclosure (per the Nixpkgs automation/AI policy): the investigation and this write-up were done with Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5). I ran the reproducer from "Steps to reproduce" on my machine and reviewed the report before submitting.

- host os: `Linux 7.2.11-zen1, NixOS, 26.11 (Zokor), 26.11.20261017.09063bd`
- multi-user?: `yes`
- sandbox: `yes`
- version: `nix-env (Nix) 2.34.9`
- nixpkgs: nixos-unstable at `09063bd1f2b36fd9fd793c36dfade7bd40a93dfc`
- NVIDIA driver: 615.78.08 (proprietary, `hardware.nvidia.open = false`)
- patchelf: 0.19.2 (previously 0.15.2)

body内の各文を、望ましい状態の宣言と、実際に起きたことの報告に分けて読んでください。EとOは同時にyesでも構いません。Eは文書の主題や多数決ではなく存在判定です。具体的な要求文・完成条件・目標文が一文でもあれば、残りが全部作業報告でもE=yesです。例えば「利用者に完了を通知すること」は期待ですが、「利用者に通知した」は実施報告であり期待ではありません。Goal・Acceptanceという見出しそのものは期待文ではなく、その下に過去の実施報告しかなければE=noです。表・数式・役割が完成状態の対応を定義する場合も期待です。Oでは実測の引用・確認状況一覧・本文内HTMLコメントの作業メモも数えますが、架空の試験入力・条件付きの例は数えません。許容を表す「〜でもよい」や仮定・可能性だけを述べる文は、現状の報告ではありません。例えば「点検は後日でもよい」は許容条件ですが、「点検はまだしていない」は現在の状態の報告です。O=yesにするには、本文が現実にそうだと主張している箇所が必要です。与えられたbody全体だけを対象に判断し、そこにない現状を推測しないでください。

{"body":"<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! feature_request_template ⚠️⚠️ -->
<!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/ -->
<!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. -->

<!-- Describe the feature you'd like. -->

## Problem

The harness-aware `*.agent.md` schema work in #342854 can validate static attribute names, YAML shapes, enums, nested MCP/GitHub structures, and Copilot hook actions. Several useful value checks cannot be correct from static tables alone because the accepted values depend on the active harness, session, model catalogue, installed customizations, or connected servers.

We should inventory these opportunities and add provider-backed completion, hover, and validation only where the source is authoritative. Until an inventory has settled, the editor must not mark a value unused or unknown.

## Dynamic value opportunities

### Models

- Complete and validate `model` against models available to the effective harness/session.
- Support both scalar models and ordered model preference arrays.
- Distinguish unavailable, policy-disabled, and unknown model identifiers where the provider exposes that distinction.
- Validate `model-policy: required` against the declared model list and current availability without treating transient catalogue loading as an error.
- Complete or validate `reasoning-effort` using the selected model's advertised capabilities, while preserving arbitrary strings when the runtime intentionally accepts and adapts them.

### Tools

- Complete and validate `tools` against the authoritative Copilot tool inventory for the active session.
- Include provider-native tools, client-provided tools, MCP tools/server namespaces, supported aliases, and wildcard forms.
- Do not suggest VS Code tool sets to Copilot; mark authored tool-set references unused with an explanation that Copilot requires individual tools.
- Differentiate an unknown tool from a known but unavailable/disabled tool when the provider can do so.
- Revalidate when tools, MCP server state, client tools, or enablement changes.

### Skills and customizations

- Complete and validate `skills` from the active harness's enabled skill inventory.
- Use `ICustomizationItemProvider`/`provideChatSessionCustomizations` rather than Local `IPromptsService` discovery for provider-backed harnesses.
- Consider descriptions and source information in completion details and hovers.
- Revalidate when customizations are installed, removed, enabled, disabled, or republished.

### GitHub MCP configuration

- Complete `github.toolsets` from an authoritative GitHub MCP toolset catalogue if one is available.
- Complete permission scopes and values only if the runtime/provider publishes a stable schema. The current runtime structurally accepts string maps, so the editor should not invent restrictions from stale documentation.
- Explain values that are recognized but unavailable because of authentication, policy, or server configuration.

### Agent-scoped MCP servers

- Where available, validate `mcp-servers.<name>.tools` against the server's advertised tools.
- Detect duplicate/conflicting server names and tool namespace collisions when the provider supplies enough information.
- Avoid starting or authenticating a server merely to provide editor validation.
- Treat unresolved or disconnected server inventories as pending, not as an empty authoritative set.

## Additional value checks that do not require live inventory

These can be implemented in code or static metadata when useful:

- Validate hook `matcher` values as regular expressions where the runtime does so.
- Apply event-specific hook constraints, including matcher support and authorization-affecting HTTP hook requirements.
- Validate command action `exec`/`args`, shell-vs-exec exclusivity, positive timeouts, HTTP URL schemes, and prompt actions being limited to `sessionStart`.

<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! feature_request_template ⚠️⚠️ -->
<!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/ -->
<!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. -->

<!-- Describe the feature you'd like. -->
Hey VS Code team! 👋

I think it would be fun to let the VS Code Pet help us understand GitHub Copilot’s summaries and suggested changes in a more interactive way.

When Copilot finishes a task, it can provide a long summary covering things like:

What changed
Where it deviated from the original plan
Known limitations
Questions or follow-up items for the user
These summaries are useful, but they can sometimes be long and boring to read, especially when working on larger tasks.

💡 The idea

What if the VS Code Pet could walk us through the summary, breaking it down into small, digestible pieces instead of presenting everything at once?

For example, the pet could:

🐾 Explain one change at a time.
💬 Highlight important details using short, friendly explanations.
🔍 Guide us through the different sections of the summary.
❓ Present Copilot’s questions and let us respond before moving on.

Hey VS Code team! 👋

I really like the new /vscode-pet feature. It’s a fun little addition that brings some personality to the coding experience.

I was thinking it would be awesome if we could take it a step further by adding small, playable mini-games that we can enjoy during breaks without leaving VS Code.

Some ideas that could be fun:

🐍 Snake — The classic game where you control a snake and collect food.
🧱 Tetris — A simple block-stacking puzzle game.
🏎️ Mini Racing Game — A small pixel-art car dodging obstacles or racing on a simple track.
🏓 Pong — A quick game of classic paddle and ball.
🐦 Flappy Bird-style Game — A simple side-scrolling game.
🐾 Take Care of Your Pet — Feed the pet, play with it, give it treats, and take care of its needs. Maybe the pet could have simple moods or reactions depending on how you interact with it.
The games could use the same playful, pixel-art style as the existing pet and run in a small, lightweight view or panel.

Maybe they could even be launched directly from the pet, with something like a small “Play” action.

The idea isn’t to turn VS Code into a gaming platform, but to add a few lightweight games for quick breaks while coding.

I think this could make the pet feature even more engaging and give developers another fun way to interact with VS Code.

What do you think? Would you enjoy having mini-games built into the VS Code pet feature? 🎮🐾"}

<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! feature_request_template ⚠️⚠️ -->
<!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/ -->
<!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. -->

<!-- Describe the feature you'd like. -->
Hey VS Code team! 👋

I really like the new /vscode-pet feature. It’s a fun little addition that brings some personality to the coding experience.

I was thinking it would be awesome if we could take it a step further by adding small, playable mini-games that we can enjoy during breaks without leaving VS Code.

Some ideas that could be fun:

🐍 Snake — The classic game where you control a snake and collect food.
🧱 Tetris — A simple block-stacking puzzle game.
🏎️ Mini Racing Game — A small pixel-art car dodging obstacles or racing on a simple track.
🏓 Pong — A quick game of classic paddle and ball.
🐦 Flappy Bird-style Game — A simple side-scrolling game.
🐾 Take Care of Your Pet — Feed the pet, play with it, give it treats, and take care of its needs. Maybe the pet could have simple moods or reactions depending on how you interact with it.
The games could use the same playful, pixel-art style as the existing pet and run in a small, lightweight view or panel.

Maybe they could even be launched directly from the pet, with something like a small “Play” action.

The idea isn’t to turn VS Code into a gaming platform, but to add a few lightweight games for quick breaks while coding.

I think this could make the pet feature even more engaging and give developers another fun way to interact with VS Code.

What do you think? Would you enjoy having mini-games built into the VS Code pet feature? 🎮🐾

{"body":" Type: Bug Environment: macOS, VS Code 1.142.0. Server: https://mcp.atlassian.com/v1/mcp Copilot session: reports “requires authentication”; clicking Authenticate does not open a browser. Local session: the same Atlassian MCP configuration works reliably. Log evidence: VS Code successfully authenticated and discovered 32 tools, but the agent continued reporting “still requires authentication.” ### Steps to reproduce 1. On macOS, open VS Code **1.142.0** with the Atlassian MCP server configured: ```json "com.atlassian/atlassian-mcp-server": { "type": "http", "url": "https://mcp.atlassian.com/v1/mcp" } ``` 2. In a **Copilot** session (Copilot SDK), attempt to use Atlassian MCP. 3. The chat displays: > The MCP server com.atlassian/atlassian-mcp-server requires authentication. Authenticate? 4. Click **Authenticate**. 5. **Nothing visibly happens:** no browser window opens, and Atlassian remains unavailable. ### Troubleshooting attempted — problem persists 6. Open the Command Palette using **Cmd+Shift+P**. 7. Run **MCP: List Servers**. 8. Select **com.atlassian/atlassian-mcp-server** and restart it, using **Restart Server** or **Stop Server → Start Server**. 9. Complete any authentication prompted through the MCP server controls rather than the chat card. 10. Start a **new Copilot chat** and retry Atlassian. 11. The authentication problem persists. The above restart/authentication/new-chat sequence was followed without resolving the issue. ### Expected result Clicking **Authenticate** should complete authentication—opening a browser if necessary—and make the Atlassian tools available to the Copilot session. ### Actual result and log evidence Clicking **Authenticate** does not open a browser, and the Copilot session continues to require authentication. Logs from the same VS Code run show: - **15:18:37:** Atlassian browser sign-in completed successfully. - **15:18:38:** VS Code connected to Atlassian and discovered **32 tools**. - **15:20:02:** The Copilot session still reported that authentication was required. - **15:22:04:** The agent reported: > MCP server "com.atlassian/atlassian-mcp-server" still requires authentication ### Working comparison / workaround 12. In the same VS Code installation, leave the Atlassian MCP configuration unchanged. 13. Open **New Chat (+)**. 14. Change **Session Target** from **Copilot** to **Local**, leaving the agent mode as **Agent**. 15. Attempt to use Atlassian MCP. **Result:** Atlassian works reliably in the **Local** session. This appears specific to the Copilot SDK session’s authentication path; the same server configuration works in Local sessions. Type: Bug Environment: macOS, VS Code 1.142.0. Server: https://mcp.atlassian.com/v1/mcp Copilot session: reports “requires authentication”; clicking Authenticate does not open a browser. Local session: the same Atlassian MCP configuration works reliably. Log evidence: VS Code successfully authenticated and discovered 32 tools, but the agent continued reporting “still requires authentication.” ### Steps to reproduce 1. On macOS, open VS Code **1.142.0** with the Atlassian MCP server configured: ```json "com.atlassian/atlassian-mcp-server": { "type": "http", "url": "https://mcp.atlassian.com/v1/mcp" } ``` 2. In a **Copilot** session (Copilot SDK), attempt to use Atlassian MCP. 3. The chat displays: > The MCP server com.atlassian/atlassian-mcp-server requires authentication. Authenticate? 4. Click **Authenticate**. 5. **Nothing visibly happens:** no browser window opens, and Atlassian remains unavailable. ### Troubleshooting attempted — problem persists 6. Open the Command Palette using **Cmd+Shift+P**. 7. Run **MCP: List Servers**. 8. Select **com.atlassian/atlassian-mcp-server** and restart it, using **Restart Server** or **Stop Server → Start Server**. 9. Complete any authentication prompted through the MCP server controls rather than the chat card. 10. Start a **new Copilot chat** and retry Atlassian. 11. The authentication problem persists. The above restart/authentication/new-chat sequence was followed without resolving the issue. ### Expected result Clicking **Authenticate** should complete authentication—opening a browser if necessary—and make the Atlassian tools available to the Copilot session. ### Actual result and log evidence Clicking **Authenticate** does not open a browser, and the Copilot session continues to require authentication. Logs from the same VS Code run show: - **15:18:37:** Atlassian browser sign-in completed successfully. - **15:18:38:** VS Code connected to Atlassian and discovered **32 tools**. - **15:20:02:** The Copilot session still reported that authentication was required. - **15:22:04:** The agent reported: > MCP server "com.atlassian/atlassian-mcp-server" still requires authentication ### Working comparison / workaround 12. In the same VS Code installation, leave the Atlassian MCP configuration unchanged. 13. Open **New Chat (+)**. 14. Change **Session Target** from **Copilot** to **Local**, leaving the agent mode as **Agent**. 15. Attempt to use Atlassian MCP. **Result:** Atlassian works reliably in the **Local** session. This appears specific to the Copilot SDK session’s authentication path; the same server configuration works in Local sessions. Select **com.atlassian/atlassian-mcp-server** and restart it, using **Restart Server** or **Stop Server → Start Server**. 9. Complete any authentication prompted through the MCP server controls rather than the chat card. 10. Start a **new Copilot chat** and retry Atlassian. 11. The authentication problem persists. The repo's `launch` agent skill (`.agents/skills/launch`) starts isolated, debuggable Code OSS instances for agents. Today it is slow and fragile:

- Launch logic is duplicated between `launch.ps1` and `launch.sh`, with two different profile exclude rules.
- On Windows a launch takes ~10s or more (eager `fnm` scanning, robocopy of the whole profile, pre-launch run serially).
- Arguments are passed through `cmd.exe` (`code.bat`), so paths or titles with `&` or `%` break.
- A PowerShell caller that captures the output hangs until Code OSS exits, because Electron inherits the capture pipe.
- Run directories can collide, are never garbage collected, and cleanup matches processes by command line (8-14s).

## Expected

- One TypeScript launcher core with thin PowerShell/bash wrappers.
- Fast launches (~1-2s until CDP is ready), incremental profile copies, optional run-directory reuse.
- Robust argument passing, no hang when capturing output, unique run directories with automatic cleanup, and a cross-platform cleanup that stops the recorded process tree.

## Feature request

Chat's "Open With..." context-menu action on links should list every handler that can open the link, not only editor types, and should also be available for web (http/https) links.

- Web links in chat show "Open With...".

Part of #342050; builds on the link handler API from #342544.

{"body":"## Feature request

Track the experiment and rollout for `sessions.chat.compareAgents.showPickerHint`.

The optional picker footer improves discovery of Agent bake off by showing **Send Query to Multiple Models** at the bottom of the model picker. It gives users a second, explicit entry point in addition to the Compare Models tab-bar toggle.

## Expected behavior

- Keep the setting disabled by default and controlled through experimentation.
- When enabled, show the **Send Query to Multiple Models** footer action while model comparison is available.
- Include the user's resolved `sessions.compareModels` keybinding in the action label when configured.
- Open comparison setup without selecting a single model.
- Keep the Compare Models tab-bar toggle available regardless of whether the footer hint is enabled.
- Preserve the existing **Add Models...** action and single-model picker behavior.

## Tracking

Setting: `sessions.chat.compareAgents.showPickerHint`

Implemented by #342656.
"}

## Feature request

Track the experiment and rollout for `sessions.chat.compareAgents.showPickerHint`.

The optional picker footer improves discovery of Agent bake off by showing **Send Query to Multiple Models** at the bottom of the model picker. It gives users a second, explicit entry point in addition to the Compare Models tab-bar toggle.

## Expected behavior

- Keep the setting disabled by default and controlled through experimentation.
- When enabled, show the **Send Query to Multiple Models** footer action while model comparison is available.
- Include the user's resolved `sessions.compareModels` keybinding in the action label when configured.
- Open comparison setup without selecting a single model.
- Keep the Compare Models tab-bar toggle available regardless of whether the footer hint is enabled.
- Preserve the existing **Add Models...** action and single-model picker behavior.

## Tracking

Setting: `sessions.chat.compareAgents.showPickerHint`

Implemented by #342656.

No formal specification label, generality, adoption, implementation, must-word or future tense is required. Distinguish the role of the relationship being stated. Declaring what a function does or what condition applies counts; merely describing what happened, is happening, used to happen or regularly happens in observed execution does not by itself declare a specification. A performed configuration, measured value, comparison or causal explanation does not supply an unstated applicable contract. These are role distinctions, not rules excluding particular headings, formats, tenses or words: a report may also contain a genuine specification, and an ordinary capability statement can declare one without requesting a change. Read each statement in context; one qualifying declaration anywhere is sufficient and observations elsewhere do not cancel it. Quoted or hypothetical text counts when used to declare the specification, but not when displayed only as an illustration. Synthetic contrast: 'This dial sets the sampling interval' declares a function; 'I turned the dial and the reading changed' alone reports an observation. A request or a subject's goal alone does not establish this specification role. Do not consult external content.

A specification or expected caption alone does not establish this request or subject-goal role. One qualifying statement anywhere is sufficient and observations elsewhere do not cancel it. Synthetic contrast: 'I need a cost estimate before ordering the materials' declares a goal or need; 'The estimate arrived late, so I postponed the order' alone reports an event and response. {"body":"[Nixpkgs security tracker issue](https://tracker.security.nixos.org/issues/NIXPKGS-2026-3110) ## [CVE-2026-110672](https://tracker.security.nixos.org/suggestions/by-id/57419) ([NVD](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-110672))
Cpanel::JSON::XS versions before 4.80 for Perl leak the decoded key of an object rejected for a duplicate key or a missing colon in decode_hv Cpanel::JSON::XS versions before 4.80 for Perl leak the decoded key of an object rejected for a duplicate key or a missing colon in decode_hv. A quoted key of 24 or more bytes, or one containing a non-ASCII byte or an escape sequence, is decoded into a new scalar. Nothing frees that scalar when the object is rejected for a missing ':' after the key or, from 4.09, for a duplicate key. Duplicate keys are an error unless allow_dupkeys, dupkeys_as_arrayref or relaxed is set. A process that keeps running after a failed decode retains one key per rejected document, with its size chosen by the sender. Repeated requests exhaust process memory.
### References - https://github.com/rurban/Cpanel-JSON-XS/commit/532b53cf8d2ca5ab6bc24048325566d1f7132425.patch (`patch`) - https://metacpan.org/release/RURBAN/Cpanel-JSON-XS-4.80/changes (`release-notes`) ## [CVE-2026-110673](https://tracker.security.nixos.org/suggestions/by-id/56996) ([NVD](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-110673))
Cpanel::JSON::XS versions before 4.80 for Perl allow stack exhaustion via nested tagged values under allow_tags in decode_tag Cpanel::JSON::XS versions before 4.80 for Perl allow stack exhaustion via nested tagged values under allow_tags in decode_tag. With allow_tags, "(" starts a tagged value. Its tag and value are decoded recursively, and each can start another tagged value. Unlike arrays and objects, this nesting is not counted against max_depth. A run of "(" bytes exhausts the C stack and triggers an uncatchable segmentation fault regardless of max_depth.
### References - https://github.com/rurban/Cpanel-JSON-XS/commit/995eb484a9351753e2a8ec3317918b5b4a4e086a.patch (`patch`) - https://metacpan.org/release/RURBAN/Cpanel-JSON-XS-4.80/changes (`release-notes`) ## [CVE-2026-110687](https://tracker.security.nixos.org/suggestions/by-id/57046) ([NVD](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-110687))
Cpanel::JSON::XS versions from 4.43 before 4.80 for Perl misorder byte-string keys during canonical encoding in utf16_cmp Cpanel::JSON::XS versions from 4.43 before 4.80 for Perl misorder byte-string keys during canonical encoding in utf16_cmp. canonical sorts keys by UTF-16 code units. When any key in a hash is UTF-8 flagged, every key is decoded as UTF-8 for the comparison, including byte-string keys that the encoder writes out as Latin-1 characters. A byte-string key whose bytes are valid UTF-8 is sorted out of order, and two keys that encode differently can compare equal and are left in hash order. The same data can encode to different canonical documents across processes.
### References - https://github.com/rurban/Cpanel-JSON-XS/commit/bb9da30b67f637f4d57922f0e043376363f28f0c.patch (`patch`) - https://metacpan.org/release/RURBAN/Cpanel-JSON-XS-4.80/changes (`release-notes`) ## [CVE-2026-110682](https://tracker.security.nixos.org/suggestions/by-id/57081) ([NVD](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-110682))
Cpanel::JSON::XS versions from 4.42 before 4.80 for Perl let input chunking change the decoded value of top-level numbers in incr_parse Cpanel::JSON::XS versions from 4.42 before 4.80 for Perl let input chunking change the decoded value of top-level numbers in incr_parse. allow_nonref is enabled by default and incr_parse inherits it. A top-level number, true, false or null has no closing delimiter, so the incremental parser decodes whatever has arrived. The bytes 12 decode as one value when read together, but as 1 and then 2 when split across two reads. A peer that can influence read boundaries can change how many messages a stream consumer decodes and what values they carry.
### References - https://github.com/rurban/Cpanel-JSON-XS/commit/f632d6690d82c14cd2d76d648805325201c52b83.patch (`patch`) - https://metacpan.org/release/RURBAN/Cpanel-JSON-XS-4.80/changes (`release-notes`) ## [CVE-2026-110680](https://tracker.security.nixos.org/suggestions/by-id/57111) ([NVD](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-110680))
Cpanel::JSON::XS versions from 4.20 before 4.80 for Perl write out of bounds when a tied or shared hash grows during canonical encoding in encode_hv Cpanel::JSON::XS versions from 4.20 before 4.80 for Perl write out of bounds when a tied or shared hash grows during canonical encoding in encode_hv. With canonical, the keys of a tied or threads::shared hash are counted before a second pass collects them for sorting. The encoder uses a fixed 64-entry stack array or, for larger counts, a heap array sized from the first pass. If the second pass exceeds that capacity, entries are written out of bounds before the counts are compared. This corrupts stack or heap memory and can crash the process.
### References - https://github.com/rurban/Cpanel-JSON-XS/commit/44c4591cc62ea7f453a0ed931abf24394e1560a1.patch (`patch`) - https://metacpan.org/release/RURBAN/Cpanel-JSON-XS-4.80/changes (`release-notes`) ## [CVE-2026-110686](https://tracker.security.nixos.org/suggestions/by-id/57183) ([NVD](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-110686))
Cpanel::JSON::XS versions before 4.80 for Perl use freed filter callbacks when a filter removes itself during decoding in decode_hv Cpanel::JSON::XS versions before 4.80 for Perl use freed filter callbacks when a filter removes itself during decoding in decode_hv. A decode copies the parser's filter_json_object and filter_json_single_key_object callbacks without taking references to them. A filter callback that removes the last single-key filter frees the callback table while the decode in progress still uses it. The next object is dispatched through freed memory and can crash the process.
### References - https://github.com/rurban/Cpanel-JSON-XS/commit/c3e7e3c5b0b72d82b072c6a7cfb8c34cec4c7ea2.patch (`patch`) - https://metacpan.org/release/RURBAN/Cpanel-JSON-XS-4.80/changes (`release-notes`) ## [CVE-2026-110684](https://tracker.security.nixos.org/suggestions/by-id/57192) ([NVD](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-110684))
Cpanel::JSON::XS versions from 3.0202 before 4.80 for Perl leak memory and retain overloaded objects when encoding values as strings in encode_stringify Cpanel::JSON::XS versions from 3.0202 before 4.80 for Perl leak memory and retain overloaded objects when encoding values as strings in encode_stringify. encode_stringify writes a value in its string form under allow_stringify, under convert_blessed for objects without TO_JSON, and under allow_bignum. For an array or hash object with a "" overload, and from 4.20 a scalar object, it takes an extra reference that is never released, so the object and everything it references are never freed. From 4.10 it also never frees its copy of the string. Repeatedly encoding data that contains such values grows process memory without bound.
### References - https://github.com/rurban/Cpanel-JSON-XS/commit/5b15916b5e7841e447664ace51fb50c12d1e0f39.patch (`patch`) - https://metacpan.org/release/RURBAN/Cpanel-JSON-XS-4.80/changes (`release-notes`) ## [CVE-2026-110674](https://tracker.security.nixos.org/suggestions/by-id/57259) ([NVD](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-110674))
Cpanel::JSON::XS versions from 4.33 before 4.80 for Perl miss duplicate non-ASCII bare keys, allowing type confusion under dupkeys_as_arrayref in decode_hv Cpanel::JSON::XS versions from 4.33 before 4.80 for Perl miss duplicate non-ASCII bare keys, allowing type confusion under dupkeys_as_arrayref in decode_hv. With allow_barekey, which relaxed enables, a bare key containing a non-ASCII byte is stored as UTF-8 but looked up as raw bytes, so a repeated key escapes the duplicate-key check and replaces the earlier value. From 4.41, under dupkeys_as_arrayref, a bare repeat replaces the array that collects a key's values with a plain value, and the next quoted repeat pushes onto that value as if it were an array. A JSON integer there is dereferenced as a pointer. Untrusted JSON decoded with relaxed and dupkeys_as_arrayref can crash the process or dereference an address chosen by a JSON number.
### References - https://github.com/rurban/Cpanel-JSON-XS/commit/c52037857d6a99d96ebd1ce3e2fa769505f028cf.patch (`patch`) - https://metacpan.org/release/RURBAN/Cpanel-JSON-XS-4.80/changes (`release-notes`) - https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-9334 (`related`) ## [CVE-2026-110676](https://tracker.security.nixos.org/suggestions/by-id/57302) ([NVD](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-110676))
Cpanel::JSON::XS versions before 4.80 for Perl allow memory exhaustion by encoding exponent notation as full decimal digits under allow_bignum Cpanel::JSON::XS versions before 4.80 for Perl allow memory exhaustion by encoding exponent notation as full decimal digits under allow_bignum. With allow_bignum, a JSON number with a fraction or exponent decodes to a Math::BigFloat, which stores the exponent separately and so decodes cheaply. Encoding it untyped or as JSON_TYPE_FLOAT writes the plain decimal form with one digit per unit of exponent. Nothing bounds the exponent, so the 12-byte text [1e30000000] encodes to 30 MB. Untrusted JSON decoded with allow_bignum and encoded again can exhaust memory and CPU.
### References - https://github.com/rurban/Cpanel-JSON-XS/commit/996ab96972b967a917536d291947b5f3cf42e960.patch (`patch`) - https://metacpan.org/release/RURBAN/Cpanel-JSON-XS-4.80/changes (`release-notes`) ## [CVE-2026-110675](https://tracker.security.nixos.org/suggestions/by-id/57343) ([NVD](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-110675))
Cpanel::JSON::XS versions from 4.33 before 4.80 for Perl accept malformed UTF-8 in bare hash keys under allow_barekey in decode_hv Cpanel::JSON::XS versions from 4.33 before 4.80 for Perl accept malformed UTF-8 in bare hash keys under allow_barekey in decode_hv. With utf8 and allow_barekey, which relaxed enables, a quoted key is validated as UTF-8 but a bare key's bytes are stored as a UTF-8 flagged string without any check. Malformed UTF-8, control bytes and backslashes reach the decoded hash, while malformed UTF-8 and control bytes in a quoted key or a value are rejected. Later operations on the key, including lc, uc or encoding the hash again, die with a malformed UTF-8 error.
### References - https://github.com/rurban/Cpanel-JSON-XS/commit/c2cd02281b9d6904ca0aff2740154e742abc070c.patch (`patch`) - https://metacpan.org/release/RURBAN/Cpanel-JSON-XS-4.80/changes (`release-notes`) ## [CVE-2026-110681](https://tracker.security.nixos.org/suggestions/by-id/57218) ([NVD](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-110681))
Cpanel::JSON::XS versions before 4.80 for Perl use the parent interpreter's scalars from a parser object cloned into a new ithread Cpanel::JSON::XS versions before 4.80 for Perl use the parent interpreter's scalars from a parser object cloned into a new ithread. A parser object holds its callbacks and its incremental parse buffer as raw scalar pointers. When a thread is created, these are copied into the new interpreter unchanged, so the child's parser uses, and later frees, scalars that belong to the parent and may already have been freed there. A parser created before a thread starts and used inside it can call freed callbacks, corrupt reference counts and crash the process.
### References - https://github.com/rurban/Cpanel-JSON-XS/commit/c53eefbaa59c344abd4c71762118da04280987e8.patch (`patch`) - https://metacpan.org/release/RURBAN/Cpanel-JSON-XS-4.80/changes (`release-notes`) ## [CVE-2026-110688](https://tracker.security.nixos.org/suggestions/by-id/57220) ([NVD](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-110688))
Cpanel::JSON::XS versions from 4.51 before 4.80 for Perl allow quadratic CPU use by revalidating the remaining buffer per value in incr_parse Cpanel::JSON::XS versions from 4.51 before 4.80 for Perl allow quadratic CPU use by revalidating the remaining buffer per value in incr_parse. At the first non-ASCII byte in a string, the decoder validates UTF-8 from there to the end of its input. incr_parse decodes each buffered value with a fresh decoder, so every value revalidates the rest of the buffer, and doubling the input quadruples the work. A peer that sends about a megabyte of ordinary non-ASCII JSON in one read ties up the process for seconds of CPU time.
### References - https://github.com/rurban/Cpanel-JSON-XS/commit/384309f6a297384e69c851b5d64e1c421d9b2dcc.patch (`patch`) - https://metacpan.org/release/RURBAN/Cpanel-JSON-XS-4.80/changes (`release-notes`) ## [CVE-2026-110678](https://tracker.security.nixos.org/suggestions/by-id/57239) ([NVD](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-110678))
Cpanel::JSON::XS versions before 4.80 for Perl allow memory exhaustion by buffering incremental input past max_size in incr_parse Cpanel::JSON::XS versions before 4.80 for Perl allow memory exhaustion by buffering incremental input past max_size in incr_parse. The parser appends each chunk to its buffer. In scalar or list context, it compares max_size with how far it has progressed, not with the buffer length. A chunk that starts with a NUL byte stops the parser before it progresses, and a call in void context skips the check, so the buffer grows without limit. A peer streaming data to an incr_parse consumer can exhaust process memory regardless of max_size.
### References - https://github.com/rurban/Cpanel-JSON-XS/commit/d516f296b1714e06b0fb9eaae72f4558ae3d83d6.patch (`patch`) - https://metacpan.org/release/RURBAN/Cpanel-JSON-XS-4.80/changes (`release-notes`) ## [CVE-2026-110685](https://tracker.security.nixos.org/suggestions/by-id/57325) ([NVD](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-110685))
Cpanel::JSON::XS versions before 4.80 for Perl leak the decoded arguments of a tagged value when its THAW method dies in decode_tag Cpanel::JSON::XS versions before 4.80 for Perl leak the decoded arguments of a tagged value when its THAW method dies in decode_tag. With allow_tags, a tagged value's class name and argument array are decoded and passed to the class's THAW method. Both are released only after THAW returns, so a THAW that dies leaves the whole decoded argument structure allocated. Each rejected document leaks data of a size the sender chooses, so a process that catches the error and keeps running exhausts its memory.
### References - https://github.com/rurban/Cpanel-JSON-XS/commit/9ab010221c069a7af9ef7463454ecd3b8ace9c58.patch (`patch`) - https://metacpan.org/release/RURBAN/Cpanel-JSON-XS-4.80/changes (`release-notes`) ## [CVE-2026-110677](https://tracker.security.nixos.org/suggestions/by-id/57388) ([NVD](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-110677))
Cpanel::JSON::XS versions from 4.28 before 4.80 for Perl leak the array collecting duplicate key values under dupkeys_as_arrayref in decode_hv Cpanel::JSON::XS versions from 4.28 before 4.80 for Perl leak the array collecting duplicate key values under dupkeys_as_arrayref in decode_hv. With dupkeys_as_arrayref, the values of a duplicate object key are collected into a new array. An extra reference is never released, so the array and every value in it outlive the decoded structure. The array also leaks when decoding fails after a duplicate key. Repeatedly decoding untrusted JSON with a duplicate key holding a large value exhausts process memory.

[Nixpkgs security tracker issue](https://tracker.security.nixos.org/issues/NIXPKGS-2026-3110) ## [CVE-2026-110672](https://tracker.security.nixos.org/suggestions/by-id/57419) ([NVD](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-110672))
Cpanel::JSON::XS versions before 4.80 for Perl leak the decoded key of an object rejected for a duplicate key or a missing colon in decode_hv Cpanel::JSON::XS versions before 4.80 for Perl leak the decoded key of an object rejected for a duplicate key or a missing colon in decode_hv. A quoted key of 24 or more bytes, or one containing a non-ASCII byte or an escape sequence, is decoded into a new scalar. Nothing frees that scalar when the object is rejected for a missing ':' after the key or, from 4.09, for a duplicate key. Duplicate keys are an error unless allow_dupkeys, dupkeys_as_arrayref or relaxed is set. A process that keeps running after a failed decode retains one key per rejected document, with its size chosen by the sender. Repeated requests exhaust process memory.
### References - https://github.com/rurban/Cpanel-JSON-XS/commit/532b53cf8d2ca5ab6bc24048325566d1f7132425.patch (`patch`) - https://metacpan.org/release/RURBAN/Cpanel-JSON-XS-4.80/changes (`release-notes`) ## [CVE-2026-110673](https://tracker.security.nixos.org/suggestions/by-id/56996) ([NVD](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-110673))
Cpanel::JSON::XS versions before 4.80 for Perl allow stack exhaustion via nested tagged values under allow_tags in decode_tag Cpanel::JSON::XS versions before 4.80 for Perl allow stack exhaustion via nested tagged values under allow_tags in decode_tag. With allow_tags, "(" starts a tagged value. Its tag and value are decoded recursively, and each can start another tagged value. Unlike arrays and objects, this nesting is not counted against max_depth. A run of "(" bytes exhausts the C stack and triggers an uncatchable segmentation fault regardless of max_depth.
### References - https://github.com/rurban/Cpanel-JSON-XS/commit/995eb484a9351753e2a8ec3317918b5b4a4e086a.patch (`patch`) - https://metacpan.org/release/RURBAN/Cpanel-JSON-XS-4.80/changes (`release-notes`) ## [CVE-2026-110687](https://tracker.security.nixos.org/suggestions/by-id/57046) ([NVD](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-110687))
Cpanel::JSON::XS versions from 4.43 before 4.80 for Perl misorder byte-string keys during canonical encoding in utf16_cmp Cpanel::JSON::XS versions from 4.43 before 4.80 for Perl misorder byte-string keys during canonical encoding in utf16_cmp. canonical sorts keys by UTF-16 code units. When any key in a hash is UTF-8 flagged, every key is decoded as UTF-8 for the comparison, including byte-string keys that the encoder writes out as Latin-1 characters. A byte-string key whose bytes are valid UTF-8 is sorted out of order, and two keys that encode differently can compare equal and are left in hash order. The same data can encode to different canonical documents across processes.
### References - https://github.com/rurban/Cpanel-JSON-XS/commit/bb9da30b67f637f4d57922f0e043376363f28f0c.patch (`patch`) - https://metacpan.org/release/RURBAN/Cpanel-JSON-XS-4.80/changes (`release-notes`) ## [CVE-2026-110682](https://tracker.security.nixos.org/suggestions/by-id/57081) ([NVD](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-110682))
Cpanel::JSON::XS versions from 4.42 before 4.80 for Perl let input chunking change the decoded value of top-level numbers in incr_parse Cpanel::JSON::XS versions from 4.42 before 4.80 for Perl let input chunking change the decoded value of top-level numbers in incr_parse. allow_nonref is enabled by default and incr_parse inherits it. A top-level number, true, false or null has no closing delimiter, so the incremental parser decodes whatever has arrived. The bytes 12 decode as one value when read together, but as 1 and then 2 when split across two reads. A peer that can influence read boundaries can change how many messages a stream consumer decodes and what values they carry.
### References - https://github.com/rurban/Cpanel-JSON-XS/commit/f632d6690d82c14cd2d76d648805325201c52b83.patch (`patch`) - https://metacpan.org/release/RURBAN/Cpanel-JSON-XS-4.80/changes (`release-notes`) ## [CVE-2026-110680](https://tracker.security.nixos.org/suggestions/by-id/57111) ([NVD](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-110680))
Cpanel::JSON::XS versions from 4.20 before 4.80 for Perl write out of bounds when a tied or shared hash grows during canonical encoding in encode_hv Cpanel::JSON::XS versions from 4.20 before 4.80 for Perl write out of bounds when a tied or shared hash grows during canonical encoding in encode_hv. With canonical, the keys of a tied or threads::shared hash are counted before a second pass collects them for sorting. The encoder uses a fixed 64-entry stack array or, for larger counts, a heap array sized from the first pass. If the second pass exceeds that capacity, entries are written out of bounds before the counts are compared. This corrupts stack or heap memory and can crash the process.
### References - https://github.com/rurban/Cpanel-JSON-XS/commit/44c4591cc62ea7f453a0ed931abf24394e1560a1.patch (`patch`) - https://metacpan.org/release/RURBAN/Cpanel-JSON-XS-4.80/changes (`release-notes`) ## [CVE-2026-110686](https://tracker.security.nixos.org/suggestions/by-id/57183) ([NVD](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-110686))

A decode copies the parser's filter_json_object and filter_json_single_key_object callbacks without taking references to them. A filter callback that removes the last single-key filter frees the callback table while the decode in progress still uses it. ### References - https://github.com/rurban/Cpanel-JSON-XS/commit/c3e7e3c5b0b72d82b072c6a7cfb8c34cec4c7ea2.patch (`patch`) - https://metacpan.org/release/RURBAN/Cpanel-JSON-XS-4.80/changes (`release-notes`) ## [CVE-2026-110684](https://tracker.security.nixos.org/suggestions/by-id/57192) ([NVD](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-110684))

Cpanel::JSON::XS versions from 4.33 before 4.80 for Perl miss duplicate non-ASCII bare keys, allowing type confusion under dupkeys_as_arrayref in decode_hv Cpanel::JSON::XS versions from 4.33 before 4.80 for Perl miss duplicate non-ASCII bare keys, allowing type confusion under dupkeys_as_arrayref in decode_hv. ### References - https://github.com/rurban/Cpanel-JSON-XS/commit/c52037857d6a99d96ebd1ce3e2fa769505f028cf.patch (`patch`) - https://metacpan.org/release/RURBAN/Cpanel-JSON-XS-4.80/changes (`release-notes`) - https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-9334 (`related`) ## [CVE-2026-110676](https://tracker.security.nixos.org/suggestions/by-id/57302) ([NVD](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-110676))

### References - https://github.com/rurban/Cpanel-JSON-XS/commit/996ab96972b967a917536d291947b5f3cf42e960.patch (`patch`) - https://metacpan.org/release/RURBAN/Cpanel-JSON-XS-4.80/changes (`release-notes`) ## [CVE-2026-110675](https://tracker.security.nixos.org/suggestions/by-id/57343) ([NVD](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-110675))
