### References - https://github.com/rurban/Cpanel-JSON-XS/commit/c2cd02281b9d6904ca0aff2740154e742abc070c.patch (`patch`) - https://metacpan.org/release/RURBAN/Cpanel-JSON-XS-4.80/changes (`release-notes`) ## [CVE-2026-110681](https://tracker.security.nixos.org/suggestions/by-id/57218) ([NVD](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-110681))
Cpanel::JSON::XS versions before 4.80 for Perl use the parent interpreter's scalars from a parser object cloned into a new ithread Cpanel::JSON::XS versions before 4.80 for Perl use the parent interpreter's scalars from a parser object cloned into a new ithread. A parser object holds its callbacks and its incremental parse buffer as raw scalar pointers. When a thread is created, these are copied into the new interpreter unchanged, so the child's parser uses, and later frees, scalars that belong to the parent and may already have been freed there. A parser created before a thread starts and used inside it can call freed callbacks, corrupt reference counts and crash the process.
### References - https://github.com/rurban/Cpanel-JSON-XS/commit/c53eefbaa59c344abd4c71762118da04280987e8.patch (`patch`) - https://metacpan.org/release/RURBAN/Cpanel-JSON-XS-4.80/changes (`release-notes`) ## [CVE-2026-110688](https://tracker.security.nixos.org/suggestions/by-id/57220) ([NVD](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-110688))
Cpanel::JSON::XS versions from 4.51 before 4.80 for Perl allow quadratic CPU use by revalidating the remaining buffer per value in incr_parse Cpanel::JSON::XS versions from 4.51 before 4.80 for Perl allow quadratic CPU use by revalidating the remaining buffer per value in incr_parse. Cpanel::JSON::XS versions before 4.80 for Perl allow memory exhaustion by buffering incremental input past max_size in incr_parse Cpanel::JSON::XS versions before 4.80 for Perl allow memory exhaustion by buffering incremental input past max_size in incr_parse. Cpanel::JSON::XS versions before 4.80 for Perl use the parent interpreter's scalars from a parser object cloned into a new ithread Cpanel::JSON::XS versions before 4.80 for Perl use the parent interpreter's scalars from a parser object cloned into a new ithread. A parser object holds its callbacks and its incremental parse buffer as raw scalar pointers. When a thread is created, these are copied into the new interpreter unchanged, so the child's parser uses, and later frees, scalars that belong to the parent and may already have been freed there. A parser created before a thread starts and used inside it can call freed callbacks, corrupt reference counts and crash the process.
### References - https://github.com/rurban/Cpanel-JSON-XS/commit/c53eefbaa59c344abd4c71762118da04280987e8.patch (`patch`) - https://metacpan.org/release/RURBAN/Cpanel-JSON-XS-4.80/changes (`release-notes`) ## [CVE-2026-110688](https://tracker.security.nixos.org/suggestions/by-id/57220) ([NVD](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-110688))
Cpanel::JSON::XS versions from 4.51 before 4.80 for Perl allow quadratic CPU use by revalidating the remaining buffer per value in incr_parse Cpanel::JSON::XS versions from 4.51 before 4.80 for Perl allow quadratic CPU use by revalidating the remaining buffer per value in incr_parse. At the first non-ASCII byte in a string, the decoder validates UTF-8 from there to the end of its input. incr_parse decodes each buffered value with a fresh decoder, so every value revalidates the rest of the buffer, and doubling the input quadruples the work. ### References - https://github.com/rurban/Cpanel-JSON-XS/commit/384309f6a297384e69c851b5d64e1c421d9b2dcc.patch (`patch`) - https://metacpan.org/release/RURBAN/Cpanel-JSON-XS-4.80/changes (`release-notes`) ## [CVE-2026-110678](https://tracker.security.nixos.org/suggestions/by-id/57239) ([NVD](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-110678))
Cpanel::JSON::XS versions before 4.80 for Perl allow memory exhaustion by buffering incremental input past max_size in incr_parse Cpanel::JSON::XS versions before 4.80 for Perl allow memory exhaustion by buffering incremental input past max_size in incr_parse. The parser appends each chunk to its buffer. In scalar or list context, it compares max_size with how far it has progressed, not with the buffer length. A chunk that starts with a NUL byte stops the parser before it progresses, and a call in void context skips the check, so the buffer grows without limit. With allow_tags, a tagged value's class name and argument array are decoded and passed to the class's THAW method. Both are released only after THAW returns, so a THAW that dies leaves the whole decoded argument structure allocated. Each rejected document leaks data of a size the sender chooses, so a process that catches the error and keeps running exhausts its memory.
### References - https://github.com/rurban/Cpanel-JSON-XS/commit/9ab010221c069a7af9ef7463454ecd3b8ace9c58.patch (`patch`) - https://metacpan.org/release/RURBAN/Cpanel-JSON-XS-4.80/changes (`release-notes`) ## [CVE-2026-110677](https://tracker.security.nixos.org/suggestions/by-id/57388) ([NVD](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-110677))

## Summary

The "Browse" UI (agent/connector discovery) is slow to load — observed at approximately 17 seconds in a screen recording. This was flagged by Ulugbek with a recording and reproduced/confirmed in thread discussion.

## Details

- Jessie Houghton confirmed the connectors endpoint is slow, and that this loading time has been the same since the connectors feature was added by Paul.
- digitarald asked whether we're blocked on loading multiple feeds, or if it's the main agent finder request that's slow — worth root-causing which of these (or both) is the bottleneck.
- Megan Rogge suggested adding a progress indicator that shows something like "explored x of y" so users get feedback while the data loads, rather than staring at a long blank/loading state.

## Proposed work

1. Investigate why the connectors endpoint / agent finder request is slow, and determine if the two are independent latency sources.
2. Add progress indicators to the Browse UI so users get feedback during the ~17s load (e.g. "explored x of y" style messaging).

## Context

Originally reported in Slack thread by Ulugbek (with screen recording attached), discussed by Megan Rogge, digitarald, and Jessie Houghton.

## Feature request

Allow users to reorder the new-session composer pickers in the desktop Agents Window by dragging them, starting with moving Environment before or after Workspace.

The Environment picker is being introduced in #342686. That PR also adds a default-off experimental `sessions.chat.experimental.environmentPickerBeforeWorkspace` setting to compare the two orders. Drag-and-drop is intentionally a separate follow-up, not part of that PR.

## Proposed experience

- Provide a discoverable drag affordance on hover/focus and clear insertion feedback.
- Preserve ordinary picker clicks; starting a drag must not accidentally open or select a picker.
- Offer equivalent keyboard-accessible actions, such as Move Before Workspace and Move After Workspace, in the Environment menu.
- Persist the chosen order, ideally using the same ordering setting rather than a second source of truth.
- Keep visual order, DOM order, keyboard navigation, and accessibility help consistent.
- Preserve the prompt, attachments, selected workspace/environment/harness, and focus when reordering.
- Define behavior for expanded options, collapsed options/icon rails, narrow layouts, and unavailable or disabled pickers.

Related PR: #342686. This issue tracks the follow-up only and should not be closed by that PR."}

<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! feature_request_template ⚠️⚠️ -->
<!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/ -->
<!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. -->

## Feature request

Allow users to reorder the new-session composer pickers in the desktop Agents Window by dragging them, starting with moving Environment before or after Workspace.

The Environment picker is being introduced in #342686. That PR also adds a default-off experimental `sessions.chat.experimental.environmentPickerBeforeWorkspace` setting to compare the two orders. Drag-and-drop is intentionally a separate follow-up, not part of that PR.

## Proposed experience

- Provide a discoverable drag affordance on hover/focus and clear insertion feedback.
- Preserve ordinary picker clicks; starting a drag must not accidentally open or select a picker.
- Offer equivalent keyboard-accessible actions, such as Move Before Workspace and Move After Workspace, in the Environment menu.
- Persist the chosen order, ideally using the same ordering setting rather than a second source of truth.
- Keep visual order, DOM order, keyboard navigation, and accessibility help consistent.
- Preserve the prompt, attachments, selected workspace/environment/harness, and focus when reordering.
- Define behavior for expanded options, collapsed options/icon rails, narrow layouts, and unavailable or disabled pickers.

Related PR: #342686. This issue tracks the follow-up only and should not be closed by that PR.

### Nixpkgs version

- Unstable (26.11)

### Describe the bug

coolercontrol fails to launch

### Steps to reproduce

1. build system with packages.coolercontrol.enable = true; (on nixos-unstable-small, probably nixos-unstable as well)
2. run coolercontrol in terminal

### Expected behaviour

The GUI should launch normally and allow system fan configuration.

### Relevant log output

```console
coolercontrol FATAL [default]: The following paths were searched for Qt WebEngine Process:
  /nix/store/rwsdqvvsjc25l5rx4jxin502wqfpllwa-qtbase-6.12.0/libexec/QtWebEngineProcess
  /nix/store/rwsdqvvsjc25l5rx4jxin502wqfpllwa-qtbase-6.12.0/bin/QtWebEngineProcess
  /nix/store/39d300nylvajwk3kql9q25zgrfnn8xy4-coolercontrol-5.0.1/bin/QtWebEngineProcess
but could not find it.
You may override the default search path by using QTWEBENGINEPROCESS_PATH environment variable.

coolercontrol FATAL [default]: The following paths were searched for Qt WebEngine resources:
  /nix/store/rwsdqvvsjc25l5rx4jxin502wqfpllwa-qtbase-6.12.0/resources
  /nix/store/rwsdqvvsjc25l5rx4jxin502wqfpllwa-qtbase-6.12.0
  /nix/store/lfj7wg5brrfmljzdy9018xby590z72gq-coolercontrol-5.0.1/bin
  /home/user/.CoolerControl
but could not find any.
You may override the default search paths by using QTWEBENGINE_RESOURCES_PATH environment variable.
```

### Additional context

I was able to solve the issue with an overlay using overrideAttrs. 
Note: this was created with ChatGPT and I do not know if this is the optimal fix
```
(final: prev: {
      coolercontrol = prev.coolercontrol // {
        coolercontrol-gui =
          prev.coolercontrol.coolercontrol-gui.overrideAttrs (old: {
            nativeBuildInputs =
              (old.nativeBuildInputs or [ ])
              ++ [ final.makeWrapper ];

            postFixup = (old.postFixup or "") + ''
              wrapProgram "$out/bin/coolercontrol" \
                --set QTWEBENGINEPROCESS_PATH \
                  "${final.qt6.qtwebengine}/libexec/QtWebEngineProcess" \
                --set QTWEBENGINE_RESOURCES_PATH \
                  "${final.qt6.qtwebengine}/resources"
            '';
          });
      };
    })
```
### System metadata

 - system: `"x86_64-linux"`
 - host os: `Linux 7.3.0-rc6-cachyos, NixOS, 26.11 (Zokor), 26.11.20261018.713b207`
 - multi-user?: `yes`
 - sandbox: `yes`
 - version: `nix-env (Determinate Nix 3.23.3) 2.35.3`

### Nixpkgs version

- Unstable (26.11)

### Describe the bug

coolercontrol fails to launch

### Steps to reproduce

1. build system with packages.coolercontrol.enable = true; (on nixos-unstable-small, probably nixos-unstable as well)
2. run coolercontrol in terminal

### Expected behaviour

The GUI should launch normally and allow system fan configuration.

### Relevant log output

```console
coolercontrol FATAL [default]: The following paths were searched for Qt WebEngine Process:
  /nix/store/rwsdqvvsjc25l5rx4jxin502wqfpllwa-qtbase-6.12.0/libexec/QtWebEngineProcess
  /nix/store/rwsdqvvsjc25l5rx4jxin502wqfpllwa-qtbase-6.12.0/bin/QtWebEngineProcess
  /nix/store/39d300nylvajwk3kql9q25zgrfnn8xy4-coolercontrol-5.0.1/bin/QtWebEngineProcess
but could not find it.
You may override the default search path by using QTWEBENGINEPROCESS_PATH environment variable.

coolercontrol FATAL [default]: The following paths were searched for Qt WebEngine resources:
  /nix/store/rwsdqvvsjc25l5rx4jxin502wqfpllwa-qtbase-6.12.0/resources
  /nix/store/rwsdqvvsjc25l5rx4jxin502wqfpllwa-qtbase-6.12.0
  /nix/store/lfj7wg5brrfmljzdy9018xby590z72gq-coolercontrol-5.0.1/bin
  /home/user/.CoolerControl
but could not find any.
You may override the default search paths by using QTWEBENGINE_RESOURCES_PATH environment variable.
```

### Additional context

I was able to solve the issue with an overlay using overrideAttrs. 
Note: this was created with ChatGPT and I do not know if this is the optimal fix
```
(final: prev: {
      coolercontrol = prev.coolercontrol // {
        coolercontrol-gui =
          prev.coolercontrol.coolercontrol-gui.overrideAttrs (old: {
            nativeBuildInputs =
              (old.nativeBuildInputs or [ ])
              ++ [ final.makeWrapper ];

            postFixup = (old.postFixup or "") + ''
              wrapProgram "$out/bin/coolercontrol" \
                --set QTWEBENGINEPROCESS_PATH \
                  "${final.qt6.qtwebengine}/libexec/QtWebEngineProcess" \
                --set QTWEBENGINE_RESOURCES_PATH \
                  "${final.qt6.qtwebengine}/resources"
            '';
          });
      };
    })
```

{"body":"<!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates -->
<!-- Please attach logs to help us diagnose your issue -->

- Copilot Chat Extension Version: Not captured.
- VS Code Version: Insiders, commit `087f03b7b82a0c89753986603421c3d24a24cd41`, built 2026-10-20.
- OS Version: macOS, exact version not captured.
- Feature: Agents window > Customizations > Migration.
- Selected model: Not applicable.
- Logs: Agent Host debug export analyzed locally. The bundle is not attached because it contains sensitive session data.

Steps to Reproduce:

1. Open Customizations > Migration with user prompt files eligible for migration.
2. Open a prompt's context menu, choose Delete, and confirm.
3. Check the migration list. The deleted prompt can remain listed and still offer Delete.

Expected: Deleting a prompt removes its row and updates the migration counts.

Actual: The file is removed from disk, but the list can retain the row, making deletion appear unsuccessful. Repeating Delete can show another confirmation for the same prompt.

### Observed evidence

On October 20, local log timestamps show:

- 08:42:01: Delete confirmation for one prompt, followed by migration recomputation and a user-data filesystem change.
- 08:42:10: Delete confirmation for another prompt, followed by another filesystem change and multiple migration recomputations.
- 08:42:15 and 08:42:22: Delete confirmations appear again for the second prompt.

Both prompt files were absent on disk when checked after the capture. No matching filesystem-delete error appears in the renderer logs.

### RCA

A cancellation race was reproduced using the current source methods with controlled discovery timing. The relevant source matches the reported Insiders commit.

- [deleteCustomizationFile](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/087f03b7b82a0c89753986603421c3d24a24cd41/src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/aiCustomization/aiCustomizationManagementEditor.ts#L2338) deletes the file and refreshes Migration. An immediate refresh can still read pre-delete discovery results before watcher invalidation.
- [refreshCustomizationMigrationInfo](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/087f03b7b82a0c89753986603421c3d24a24cd41/src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/aiCustomization/aiCustomizationManagementEditor.ts#L1357) cancels the previous refresh when another invalidation arrives.
- [listPromptFiles](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/087f03b7b82a0c89753986603421c3d24a24cd41/src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/common/promptSyntax/service/promptsServiceImpl.ts#L377) shares an in-flight promise tied to its first caller's cancellation token. The replacement refresh can inherit that cancelled scan even though its own token remains live.
- [computeCustomizationMigrationInfo](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/087f03b7b82a0c89753986603421c3d24a24cd41/src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/aiCustomization/aiCustomizationManagementEditor.ts#L1475) ignores the resulting cancellation, leaving the previous rows without an error state or retry.

The controlled reproduction verified that both computations exit without applying updated candidates, while the replacement request's token is not cancelled. The logs are consistent with this race but do not record discovery cancellation directly, so attribution of this specific occurrence remains likely rather than conclusive. No live UI reproduction or fix validation was performed.

_🤖 Posted by GitHub Copilot on Harald's behalf._"}

- Copilot Chat Extension Version: Not captured.
- VS Code Version: Insiders, commit `087f03b7b82a0c89753986603421c3d24a24cd41`, built 2026-10-20.
- OS Version: macOS, exact version not captured.
- Feature: Agents window > Customizations > Migration.
- Selected model: Not applicable.
- Logs: Agent Host debug export analyzed locally. The bundle is not attached because it contains sensitive session data.

Steps to Reproduce:

1. Open Customizations > Migration with user prompt files eligible for migration.
2. Open a prompt's context menu, choose Delete, and confirm.
3. Check the migration list. The deleted prompt can remain listed and still offer Delete.

Expected: Deleting a prompt removes its row and updates the migration counts.

Actual: The file is removed from disk, but the list can retain the row, making deletion appear unsuccessful. Repeating Delete can show another confirmation for the same prompt.

### Observed evidence

On October 20, local log timestamps show:

- 08:42:01: Delete confirmation for one prompt, followed by migration recomputation and a user-data filesystem change.
- 08:42:10: Delete confirmation for another prompt, followed by another filesystem change and multiple migration recomputations.
- 08:42:15 and 08:42:22: Delete confirmations appear again for the second prompt.

Both prompt files were absent on disk when checked after the capture. No matching filesystem-delete error appears in the renderer logs.

### RCA

A cancellation race was reproduced using the current source methods with controlled discovery timing. The relevant source matches the reported Insiders commit.

- [deleteCustomizationFile](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/087f03b7b82a0c89753986603421c3d24a24cd41/src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/aiCustomization/aiCustomizationManagementEditor.ts#L2338) deletes the file and refreshes Migration. An immediate refresh can still read pre-delete discovery results before watcher invalidation.
- [refreshCustomizationMigrationInfo](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/087f03b7b82a0c89753986603421c3d24a24cd41/src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/aiCustomization/aiCustomizationManagementEditor.ts#L1357) cancels the previous refresh when another invalidation arrives.
- [listPromptFiles](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/087f03b7b82a0c89753986603421c3d24a24cd41/src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/common/promptSyntax/service/promptsServiceImpl.ts#L377) shares an in-flight promise tied to its first caller's cancellation token. The replacement refresh can inherit that cancelled scan even though its own token remains live.
- [computeCustomizationMigrationInfo](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/087f03b7b82a0c89753986603421c3d24a24cd41/src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/aiCustomization/aiCustomizationManagementEditor.ts#L1475) ignores the resulting cancellation, leaving the previous rows without an error state or retry.

The controlled reproduction verified that both computations exit without applying updated candidates, while the replacement request's token is not cancelled. The logs are consistent with this race but do not record discovery cancellation directly, so attribution of this specific occurrence remains likely rather than conclusive. No live UI reproduction or fix validation was performed.

Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Yes. The rendering happens in core chat (`ChatContentMarkdownRenderer`), so any chat response that contains such a table is affected. - VS Code Version: 1.143.0-insider (`087f03b7b82a0c89753986603421c3d24a24cd41`, 2026-10-20) - OS Version: macOS 26.7.1 (arm64) - Surface: Agents window (Copilot CLI agent). The same code path renders every chat response. - Model: Claude Opus 5.5 ### Summary When a chat response contains a markdown table with `
` inside a cell, the `
` is shown as literal text instead of a line break. A multi-line cell ends up as one paragraph full of `
` tags. Models emit `
` here on purpose. GFM table cells cannot contain newlines, so `
` is the de facto way to break lines in a cell, and GitHub renders it that way. ### Steps to Reproduce 1. Open a chat (I used the Agents window) and send: > Can you give me a table of content about the 5 highest GDP countries. In the last column, give a few bullet points describing some demographic info like population size etc 2. The model answers with a table whose last column uses `
` between bullets (row reconstructed from the rendered output): ```markdown | Rank | Country | Nominal GDP (2026 est.) | GDP per capita (approx.) | Demographics | |---|---|---|---|---| | 1 | 🇺🇸 United States | ~$31.8T | ~$93,000 | • Population: about 342M, the 3rd largest in the world
• Median age: about 39
• About 83% of people live in cities
• Still growing slowly, mostly through immigration | ``` **Expected:** each `•` bullet starts on its own line within the cell, as on GitHub. **Actual:** the cell renders verbatim as: > • Population: about 342M, the 3rd largest in the world<br>• Median age: about 39<br>• About 83% of people live in cities<br>• Still growing slowly, mostly through immigration Every row in the table is affected. The issue reproduces deterministically without a model: ```ts const md = new MarkdownString('| a | b |\n| --- | --- |\n| x | one
two |'); chatContentMarkdownRenderer.render(md, { markedOptions: { gfm: true, breaks: true } }); // one<br>two (expected: one
two) ``` ### Root cause 1. Chat renders agent markdown **without** `supportHtml` (correctly, because the content is untrusted), and [`getChatMarkdownRenderOptions`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/main/src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/widget/chatContentMarkdownRenderer.ts) sets `sanitizerConfig.replaceWithPlaintext: true`. 2. marked lexes `
` in a table cell as an inline `html` token. In [`createMarkdownRenderer`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/main/src/vs/base/browser/markdownRenderer.ts), when `supportHtml` is off, `renderer.html` returns `escape(text)`, which produces `<br>`. 3. `br` is already in `allowedChatMarkdownHtmlTags`, so the sanitizer would accept it, but it is escaped before reaching the sanitizer. Outside tables, chat already sets `breaks: true`, so a plain newline becomes `
` and models have no reason to write the tag. Table cells are the one place where `
` is the only way to get a line break. A second, latent issue affects any fix built on marked's `walkTokens` hook. While a response is streaming (`fillInIncompleteTokens: true`), `renderMarkdown` calls `marked.lexer()` and `marked.parser()` directly, and those skip extension `walkTokens` hooks, whereas `marked.parse()` runs them. Such a fix would therefore show the literal `
` during streaming and the correct rendering only after the response completes. ### Proposed fix - Add a table-scoped marked extension to the chat render options. Its `walkTokens` hook turns inline `html` tokens that are exactly `
`, `
`, or `
` (case-insensitive, including inside `**bold**`, links, and other nested inline tokens) into marked's native `br` token. - In `renderMarkdown`, run `walkTokens` on the `fillInIncompleteTokens` path to match `marked.parse()`, so streaming and final rendering agree. Scope and safety: - No other HTML is enabled. - `
` outside tables stays literal text. - `` `
` `` inside code spans and fenced code blocks stays literal. - The output is a plain `
` without attributes, which the sanitizer already allows for chat.

{"body":" Type: Bug In a long-standing copilot chat my MCPs Error the moment I click start with no output. In a fresh chat the MCPs all start fine and are usable. Steps taken and results Installed/launched a fresh copy of VS Code. The fresh app restored the existing chat history and allowed messages to be sent successfully. MCP failures persisted when switching to the existing SPARCK conversation. Tested MCP functionality in a new chat. MCP servers started successfully. Successfully fetched Jira issues, confirming that at least the Jira integration could work in a fresh chat. Compared behavior between new and existing conversations. In a fresh chat, MCPs showed as running and could successfully fetch Jira issues. In SPARCK, MCPs initially showed as running, but failed when invoked and then stopped or errored during startup. The SPARCK conversation itself continued to send and receive messages. Inspected GitHub Copilot Chat and Agent Host logs. Observed repeated errors: Cannot start an MCP server because the session runtime is no longer available. Observed ProtocolServer subscription failures with Resource not found for ahp-chat://subagent/... resources associated with the affected session. Observed a session configuration refresh with reason=clientPluginsChanged, followed by SDK session shutdown and resumption. The SDK resume reported outcome=success, and the built-in GitHub MCP subsequently reached connected (ready) in the log. Despite this, subsequent MCP tool invocations in SPARCK still failed. Tested the MCP Autostart setting. Changed Chat > MCP > Autostart from newAndOutdated to onlyNew. Retested the affected conversation; this did not resolve the issue. The setting can be returned to its original default, newAndOutdated. Inspected MCP and chat settings. Chat > MCP: Access was set to all. GitHub's built-in MCP support was enabled. Inspected the chat's Tool Sets menu; it offered options to create a tool set, but no existing tool set was available to inspect. Opened Agent Debug Logs, but the view prompted to enable logging in Settings, and searching Settings for agentDebugLog returned no matching setting. No additional debug logs were obtained through that view. Observed a Jira fallback error. After the Jira MCP tool became unavailable in SPARCK, the agent attempted a direct Jira REST API request and received 401 Unauthorized. This does not establish that the MCP's own authentication is broken, since the failure occurred on the direct REST API attempt. {"body":" Type: Bug In a long-standing copilot chat my MCPs Error the moment I click start with no output. In a fresh chat the MCPs all start fine and are usable. Steps taken and results Installed/launched a fresh copy of VS Code. The fresh app restored the existing chat history and allowed messages to be sent successfully. MCP failures persisted when switching to the existing SPARCK conversation. Tested MCP functionality in a new chat. MCP servers started successfully. Successfully fetched Jira issues, confirming that at least the Jira integration could work in a fresh chat. Compared behavior between new and existing conversations. In a fresh chat, MCPs showed as running and could successfully fetch Jira issues. In SPARCK, MCPs initially showed as running, but failed when invoked and then stopped or errored during startup. The SPARCK conversation itself continued to send and receive messages. Inspected GitHub Copilot Chat and Agent Host logs. Observed repeated errors: Cannot start an MCP server because the session runtime is no longer available. Observed ProtocolServer subscription failures with Resource not found for ahp-chat://subagent/... resources associated with the affected session. Observed a session configuration refresh with reason=clientPluginsChanged, followed by SDK session shutdown and resumption. The SDK resume reported outcome=success, and the built-in GitHub MCP subsequently reached connected (ready) in the log. Despite this, subsequent MCP tool invocations in SPARCK still failed. Tested the MCP Autostart setting. Changed Chat > MCP > Autostart from newAndOutdated to onlyNew. Retested the affected conversation; this did not resolve the issue. The setting can be returned to its original default, newAndOutdated. Inspected MCP and chat settings. Chat > MCP: Access was set to all. GitHub's built-in MCP support was enabled. Inspected the chat's Tool Sets menu; it offered options to create a tool set, but no existing tool set was available to inspect. Opened Agent Debug Logs, but the view prompted to enable logging in Settings, and searching Settings for agentDebugLog returned no matching setting. No additional debug logs were obtained through that view. Observed a Jira fallback error. After the Jira MCP tool became unavailable in SPARCK, the agent attempted a direct Jira REST API request and received 401 Unauthorized. This does not establish that the MCP's own authentication is broken, since the failure occurred on the direct REST API attempt. <!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! feature_request_template ⚠️⚠️ -->
<!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/ -->
<!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. -->

<!-- Describe the feature you'd like. -->

When viewing a Markdown document in Preview mode, have the Outline view display the table of contents exactly the same way it already does in Text Editor mode and Markdown Editor mode. It currently instead displays "The active editor cannot provide outline information."

This feature was previously requested in May 2026 but only got 16 of the 20 required votes: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/316113

So I'm creating this new issue to try again to get 20 votes, because this is really important for navigating long documents when using VS Code for reading Markdown (like the many Markdown documents that LLM's create).

Note that this issue was recently provided (literally last week) for Markdown Editor mode: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/328567

I tried using Markdown Editor mode, but it is not suitable because I want to basic viewing things like scroll downwards and upwards with the arrow keys or with space and shift+space, and Markdown Editor doesn't support any of those, even when in non-edit mode. Follow-up to #342686.

## Current limitation

Compare Agents must not be offered when Dev Container execution is selected. Normal composer drafts explicitly require container execution, but comparison creates fresh sessions without carrying that requirement. Hiding the comparison controls and rejecting stale comparison sends is the intentional interim behavior; a normal single-agent request remains available.

The comparison launch architecture may change soon, so defer full container integration rather than expanding that path in the Environment picker PR.

## Follow-up scope

- Carry explicit container execution intent through the comparison lifecycle and persisted state, including attempts, Judge/retries, and synthesis.
- Reuse the existing experimental container-worktree path (`chat.agentHost.devContainer.worktree.enabled`) where supported; preserve independent worktree isolation and never fall back to source-host or shared-folder execution.
- Preserve comparison attribution, participant identity/grouping, models, and permissions across the source-to-container session handoff. Validate access to attempt evidence from the Judge.
- Cover unsupported capabilities, partial launch failures, cancellation, reload/retry, and container/worktree cleanup.
- Restore comparison availability only for supported combinations; Dev Container samples currently do not support the worktree combination.

## Expected interim UX

Selecting Dev Container removes comparison setup and clears an existing comparison selection once configuration settles. Returning to a compatible non-container destination restores comparison availability under its existing gates. Stale comparison sends report an explicit error instead of launching on the host.

{"body":"## Summary

An Agent Plugin (OpenPlugin-style `plugin.json` that declares `hooks`, `mcpServers` and `rules` through `paths` + `exclusive`, with its content under a `com.github.copilot/` folder) works end to end in the **VS Code Local harness**: hooks run, MCP servers start, instructions load. The same installed plugin does **not** behave the same in:

1. VS Code **Copilot harness** (Copilot SDK / Agent Host)
2. **Copilot CLI**
3. **GitHub Copilot Desktop / Agents window**

Each surface seems to use its own plugin loader and its own hook format, so a plugin cannot be authored once and behave the same everywhere.

## Environment

- VS Code 1.142.x, GitHub Copilot Chat extension, Windows 11
- Copilot CLI 1.0.x
- Plugin installed from a marketplace into `~/.copilot/installed-plugins/<marketplace>/<plugin>`

## Observed behavior

| Capability | VS Code Local | Copilot harness (SDK / Agent Host) | Copilot CLI | Desktop / Agents window |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Hooks discovered | yes | yes (Customizations > Hook Discovery Results lists every file as loaded) | `/hooks` shows nothing from the plugin | not verified |
| Hooks executed | yes | **no** | **no** | not verified |
| Plugin MCP servers | yes | not started automatically | not verified | not shown |
| Plugin instructions / rules | yes | not loaded | n/a | not verified |
| Custom hook path (`hooks.paths`, `exclusive`) | honored | unclear | appears ignored | unclear |

## Likely causes (partly from reading existing issues, not all verified)

- **Different hook schemas.** The Copilot harness appears to honor only Copilot-style entries (`bash` / `powershell`) and ignore VS Code-style entries (`command` with `windows` / `linux` / `osx`). See #342664.
- **Non-standard plugin layout.** The Copilot CLI documents plugin hooks as `hooks.json` or `hooks/hooks.json` inside the installed plugin directory. A hooks file reached only through `plugin.json` `hooks.paths` (for example under `com.github.copilot/`) is not found, so `/hooks` stays empty. See #334153 for the same `com.github.copilot` layout problem.
- **Discovery is not execution.** The harness reports a hook file as loaded, but nothing runs. There is no log or UI signal explaining why. See #302865, #302350 and #342022.
- **Plugin MCP servers and agents.** Plugin-owned MCP servers are not auto-started in Agent Host (#342860); custom agents are not picked up (#342085); `${PLUGIN_ROOT}` is not expanded for canonical schema plugins (#335006).
- **Plugin source mismatch.** The Copilot harness only reads installs under `~/.copilot/installed-plugins` (#342671), and plugin sync can fail on some setups (#341862).
- **Instructions.** How instructions and `applyTo` rules are loaded in the Copilot harness is unclear (#342595).

## Expected behavior

A plugin that installs correctly should expose the same hooks, MCP servers, instructions and agents in every client, or the docs should state exactly which manifest fields and hook formats each client supports.

## Requests

1. Document, per client (Local, Copilot harness / Agent Host, Copilot CLI, Desktop), which `plugin.json` fields are honored: `hooks`, `mcpServers`, `rules`, `paths`, `exclusive`, and the `com.github.copilot/` folder convention.
2. Accept both hook entry formats (`command` plus per-OS overrides, and `bash` / `powershell`) in every client, or log a clear warning when an entry is skipped.
3. When a hook is discovered but cannot run, surface the reason in the Hook Discovery Results view and in the output channel.
4. Make Copilot CLI `/hooks` list hooks contributed by installed plugins, including those declared through `plugin.json`.
5. Provide a single supported way to declare plugin MCP servers and instructions that all clients load.

## Related issues

microsoft/vscode: #342664, #342022, #302865, #302350, #334153, #342860, #342085, #335006, #342671, #342595, #341862
github/copilot-cli: #4629, #4520
"}

## Summary

An Agent Plugin (OpenPlugin-style `plugin.json` that declares `hooks`, `mcpServers` and `rules` through `paths` + `exclusive`, with its content under a `com.github.copilot/` folder) works end to end in the **VS Code Local harness**: hooks run, MCP servers start, instructions load. The same installed plugin does **not** behave the same in:

1. VS Code **Copilot harness** (Copilot SDK / Agent Host)
2. **Copilot CLI**
3. **GitHub Copilot Desktop / Agents window**

Each surface seems to use its own plugin loader and its own hook format, so a plugin cannot be authored once and behave the same everywhere.

## Environment

- VS Code 1.142.x, GitHub Copilot Chat extension, Windows 11
- Copilot CLI 1.0.x
- Plugin installed from a marketplace into `~/.copilot/installed-plugins/<marketplace>/<plugin>`

## Observed behavior

| Capability | VS Code Local | Copilot harness (SDK / Agent Host) | Copilot CLI | Desktop / Agents window |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Hooks discovered | yes | yes (Customizations > Hook Discovery Results lists every file as loaded) | `/hooks` shows nothing from the plugin | not verified |
| Hooks executed | yes | **no** | **no** | not verified |
| Plugin MCP servers | yes | not started automatically | not verified | not shown |
| Plugin instructions / rules | yes | not loaded | n/a | not verified |
| Custom hook path (`hooks.paths`, `exclusive`) | honored | unclear | appears ignored | unclear |

## Likely causes (partly from reading existing issues, not all verified)

- **Different hook schemas.** The Copilot harness appears to honor only Copilot-style entries (`bash` / `powershell`) and ignore VS Code-style entries (`command` with `windows` / `linux` / `osx`). See #342664.
- **Non-standard plugin layout.** The Copilot CLI documents plugin hooks as `hooks.json` or `hooks/hooks.json` inside the installed plugin directory. A hooks file reached only through `plugin.json` `hooks.paths` (for example under `com.github.copilot/`) is not found, so `/hooks` stays empty. See #334153 for the same `com.github.copilot` layout problem.
- **Discovery is not execution.** The harness reports a hook file as loaded, but nothing runs. There is no log or UI signal explaining why. See #302865, #302350 and #342022.
- **Plugin MCP servers and agents.** Plugin-owned MCP servers are not auto-started in Agent Host (#342860); custom agents are not picked up (#342085); `${PLUGIN_ROOT}` is not expanded for canonical schema plugins (#335006).
- **Plugin source mismatch.** The Copilot harness only reads installs under `~/.copilot/installed-plugins` (#342671), and plugin sync can fail on some setups (#341862).
- **Instructions.** How instructions and `applyTo` rules are loaded in the Copilot harness is unclear (#342595).

## Expected behavior

A plugin that installs correctly should expose the same hooks, MCP servers, instructions and agents in every client, or the docs should state exactly which manifest fields and hook formats each client supports.

## Requests

1. Document, per client (Local, Copilot harness / Agent Host, Copilot CLI, Desktop), which `plugin.json` fields are honored: `hooks`, `mcpServers`, `rules`, `paths`, `exclusive`, and the `com.github.copilot/` folder convention.
2. Accept both hook entry formats (`command` plus per-OS overrides, and `bash` / `powershell`) in every client, or log a clear warning when an entry is skipped.
3. When a hook is discovered but cannot run, surface the reason in the Hook Discovery Results view and in the output channel.
4. Make Copilot CLI `/hooks` list hooks contributed by installed plugins, including those declared through `plugin.json`.
5. Provide a single supported way to declare plugin MCP servers and instructions that all clients load.

## Related issues

microsoft/vscode: #342664, #342022, #302865, #302350, #334153, #342860, #342085, #335006, #342671, #342595, #341862
github/copilot-cli: #4629, #4520

**Version**: VS Code Insiders 1.143.0-insider (20f16aa5, 2026-10-19), remote agent host over SSH, Copilot CLI provider. Client: macOS. Host: Linux.

### Symptom

When a remote agent-host session's customizations are listed, the remote host gets `resourceResolve` requests for the **client's** local plugin folders, and they fail:

```
[ProtocolServer] Request 'resourceResolve' id=29 failed Resource not found: file:///Users/<user>/.vscode-insiders/agent-plugins/github.com/microsoft/vscode-team-kit/github-inbox/agents
[ProtocolServer] Request 'resourceResolve' id=30 failed Resource not found: file:///Users/<user>/.vscode-insiders/agent-plugins/github.com/microsoft/vscode-team-kit/github-inbox/skills
[ProtocolServer] Request 'resourceResolve' id=31 failed Resource not found: file:///Users/<user>/.vscode-insiders/agent-plugins/github.com/microsoft/vscode-team-kit/github-inbox/commands
[ProtocolServer] Request 'resourceResolve' id=32 failed Resource not found: file:///Users/<user>/.vscode-insiders/agent-plugins/github.com/microsoft/vscode-team-kit/github-inbox/rules
[ProtocolServer] Request 'resourceResolve' id=33 failed Resource not found: file:///Users/<user>/.copilot/installed-plugins/azure-exp/azure-exp/agents
...
```

On the client, the same requests appear as `[RemoteAgentHostProtocol] Request N failed: {"code":-32008,"message":"Resource not found: file:///Users/..."}`. Each run sends 4 folders × 2 client plugins, twice (16 requests). It repeats every time the customizations are refreshed.

### Cause

Client-synced plugins (`customization.clientId !== undefined`) keep their original client-side URI (`file:///Users/...`). In `AgentCustomizationItemProvider.toRemoteUri` (`src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/agentSessions/agentHost/agentCustomizationItemProvider.ts`), only the synthetic synced bundle (`SYNCED_CUSTOMIZATION_SCHEME`) is left alone. Every other URI goes through `toAgentHostUri(original, connectionAuthority)`, including client-synced plugins:

```ts
private toRemoteUri(customizationUri: string): URI {
	const original = URI.parse(customizationUri);
	if (original.scheme === SYNCED_CUSTOMIZATION_SCHEME) {
		return original;
	}
	return toAgentHostUri(original, this._connectionAuthority);
}
```

`provideChatSessionCustomizations` then passes that URI to `AgentCustomizationContentExpander.expandPluginContents`. It assumes the URI is a remote root and resolves `agents/`, `skills/`, `commands/` and `rules/` through the agent-host filesystem, which points at the remote machine. Those paths exist only on the client.

### Impact

- The expansion fails quietly and returns `[]`, so the remote session's customization listing can't include those plugins' children. In this repro, `github-inbox` has 7 agents and 12 skills on the client and `azure-exp` has 4 skills, and none of them can be enumerated through the remote host.
- Each refresh sends useless round trips to the remote host, and both host and client log them as errors.

### Suggested fix

For client-synced customizations (`clientId` set), don't wrap with `toAgentHostUri`. Resolve them against the client's own filesystem, for example by keeping the original `file:` URI, or through whatever the synced-bundle path uses. The same applies to the other `toRemoteUri` call sites for client-owned items (`toItem`, children, `provideCustomAgents`).

{"body":"**Version**: VS Code Insiders 1.143.0-insider, Copilot CLI agent host (local and remote)

### Problem

`CopilotAgentSession` logs this at **info** for every `assistant.message` event (`src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/copilot/copilotAgentSession.ts`, in the `wrapper.onMessage` handler):

```ts
this._logService.info(`[Copilot:${sessionId}] Full message received: ${e.data.content.length} chars`);
```

Almost all of these lines say `0 chars`, because most model replies in an agent loop only call tools and contain no text. From a real overnight remote agent host log:

- `Full message received` made up **15,329 of 75,912 lines (20%)**.
- **14,528 (95%)** of those were `0 chars`.
- After a 0-char line, the next event for the same session is almost always `Tool started: …`. So the line adds nothing beyond the tool-start line that follows.

Costs:

- **Log retention**: the host log rotates by size. During that run, one rotated file covered only about 73 minutes, which made it hard to piece together an overnight incident afterwards.
- **It hides the case it should catch**: a truly empty reply (no text and no tool calls, i.e. the "no response" case) logs exactly the same as a normal tool-only reply.
- **The useful fields aren't logged**: `AssistantMessageData` already has `toolRequests`, `model`, `outputTokens`, `serviceRequestId` / `apiCallId`, and the event has `agentId` (main agent or subagent). None of these appear in the log, so you can't tell which agent replied or trace a bad reply on the service side.

### Suggested change

- Log tool-only replies (`content === ''` and `toolRequests?.length > 0`) at **trace**.
- Log other replies at **info** in one richer line, for example:
  `Model response: agent=<root|sub:agentId> model=<model> chars=<n> tools=<m> outTokens=<k> requestId=<serviceRequestId>`
- Make truly empty replies (no content, no `toolRequests`, last chunk) easy to find, for example `empty response` at info or warn. Chunked messages and model-less synthetic root messages, which the handler already detects, may need to be left out.
"}

**Version**: VS Code Insiders 1.143.0-insider, Copilot CLI agent host (local and remote)

### Problem

`CopilotAgentSession` logs this at **info** for every `assistant.message` event (`src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/copilot/copilotAgentSession.ts`, in the `wrapper.onMessage` handler):

```ts
this._logService.info(`[Copilot:${sessionId}] Full message received: ${e.data.content.length} chars`);
```

Almost all of these lines say `0 chars`, because most model replies in an agent loop only call tools and contain no text. From a real overnight remote agent host log:

- `Full message received` made up **15,329 of 75,912 lines (20%)**.
- **14,528 (95%)** of those were `0 chars`.
- After a 0-char line, the next event for the same session is almost always `Tool started: …`. So the line adds nothing beyond the tool-start line that follows.

Costs:

- **Log retention**: the host log rotates by size. During that run, one rotated file covered only about 73 minutes, which made it hard to piece together an overnight incident afterwards.
- **It hides the case it should catch**: a truly empty reply (no text and no tool calls, i.e. the "no response" case) logs exactly the same as a normal tool-only reply.

None of these appear in the log, so you can't tell which agent replied or trace a bad reply on the service side.

  `Model response: agent=<root|sub:agentId> model=<model> chars=<n> tools=<m> outTokens=<k> requestId=<serviceRequestId>`
- Make truly empty replies (no content, no `toolRequests`, last chunk) easy to find, for example `empty response` at info or warn. Chunked messages and model-less synthetic root messages, which the handler already detects, may need to be left out.

Type: Bug

After installing today’s VS Code updates, GitHub Copilot’s speech-to-text no longer works.

Voice input is unusable in GitHub Copilot Chat.

## Bug

With `workbench.browser.openLocalhostLinks` enabled, the Integrated Browser's localhost link opener is consulted before, and separately from, the external URI openers contributed by extensions. As a result, localhost links open in the Integrated Browser even when:

- the user configured another opener for the host in `workbench.externalUriOpeners`, or
- the caller explicitly requested an opener with `allowContributedOpeners: '<opener id>'`.

The Integrated Browser also never appears in the "How would you like to open" prompt.

## Expected

The Integrated Browser is an external URI opener like the others: preferred for localhost links when the setting is enabled, subject to the configured and requested opener, and chosen by the same selection rules.

This also lets one place decide which opener a link uses, which #342544 needs to list the available link handlers.

Part of #342050.

### Nixpkgs version

- Unstable (26.11)

### Steps to reproduce

1. Use nixpkgs nixos-unstable at revision 09063bd1f2b36fd9fd793c36dfade7bd40a93dfc (flake input `nixpkgs.url = "github:NixOS/nixpkgs/nixos-unstable"`)
2. Enable the service: `services.open-webui.enable = true;` with `nixpkgs.config.allowUnfree = true;`
3. Run `sudo nixos-rebuild switch --flake .#nixos`
4. The build of `open-webui-0.12.3` fails in the fixup phase

### Can Hydra reproduce this build failure?

Hydra doesn’t try to build the package.

### Link to Hydra build job

_No response_

### Relevant log output

```console
Builder called die: makeWrapper doesn't understand the arg --set FRONTEND_BUILD_DIR /nix/store/...-open-webui-frontend-0.12.3/share/open-webui
```

### Additional context

* The failure comes from this line in `pkgs/by-name/op/open-webui/package.nix 

makeWrapperArgs = [ "--set FRONTEND_BUILD_DIR ${frontend}/share/open-webui" ];


* It is one list element containing spaces resulting in makeWrapper to treat it as a single unknown argument.
* I managed to get a workaround working by using:
services.open-webui = {
  enable = true;
  package = pkgs.open-webui.overrideAttrs (_: {
    makeWrapperArgs = [
      "--set"
      "FRONTEND_BUILD_DIR"
      "${pkgs.open-webui.frontend}/share/open-webui"
    ];
  });
};

* I searched for open PRs and issues for open-webui + makeWrapper and found nothing that covers this issue. #575605 (PYTHONPATH) is open but unrelated, and it would likely need the same separate-element form for its new flag.
* This system is built from a flake tracking nixos-unstable at revision 09063bd1f2b36fd9fd793c36dfade7bd40a93dfc
* Not on Hydra: open-webui is unfree.

- system: `"x86_64-linux"`
 - host os: `Linux 7.2.9, NixOS, 26.11 (Zokor), 26.11.20261017.09063bd`
 - multi-user?: `yes`

本問はEだけ：本文が実現すべき状態を一つでも宣言しているか。完成状態の表・責務・式も宣言である。Goal等の見出しだけでYesにしない。本文にそのような期待がなければNo。実施済みと書いてあるだけなら期待ではない。

state.body:
Tracking issue for security fixes for [eMudhra Intermediate CA Compromise](https://emudhra.we-have-a-problem.com/)

Partial mitigation while channels are getting fixes:
```
security.pki.caCertificateBlacklist = [
  # CVE-2026-111943
  "Comodo AAA Services root"
  # https://hg-edge.mozilla.org/projects/nss/rev/26d38a0c3fb81e7fb2acedbaf4c42dd21dce0517
  "emSign ECC Root CA - G3"
  # https://hg-edge.mozilla.org/projects/nss/rev/8159223c48ceeb1273a1915bca95a517294ab0e0
  "emSign Root CA - C1"
  "emSign ECC Root CA - C3"
];
```

This mitigation was also implemented in:
- https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/pull/576390
- https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/pull/576401

specification.instruction: Read only the complete literal body, including HTML comments, tables, formulas and templates. Decide whether it contains at least one statement presented as a specification or operative contract: a rule, expected or acceptable condition, responsibility, functional capability, input/output mapping, interface purpose, or condition or limitation of use. A stated expected-outcome caption or interface text declaring an action's purpose can qualify. No formal specification label, generality, adoption, implementation, must-word or future tense is required. Distinguish the role of the relationship being stated. Declaring what a function does or what condition applies counts; merely describing what happened, is happening, used to happen or regularly happens in observed execution does not by itself declare a specification. A performed configuration, measured value, comparison or causal explanation does not supply an unstated applicable contract. These are role distinctions, not rules excluding particular headings, formats, tenses or words: a report may also contain a genuine specification, and an ordinary capability statement can declare one without requesting a change. Read each statement in context; one qualifying declaration anywhere is sufficient and observations elsewhere do not cancel it. Quoted or hypothetical text counts when used to declare the specification, but not when displayed only as an illustration. Synthetic contrast: 'This dial sets the sampling interval' declares a function; 'I turned the dial and the reading changed' alone reports an observation. A request or a subject's goal alone does not establish this specification role. Do not consult external content.

options.yes: The complete body contains at least one statement presented as a specification or operative contract of the kind defined in the instruction. It declares the relationship itself; merely reporting a performed action, observed configuration or value, observed result, or a causal explanation of an observed event does not by itself establish that role. A genuine declaration still counts inside a report, quotation or template when the body uses it to declare that relationship.
options.no: The complete body contains no statement presented as a specification or operative contract of the kind defined in the instruction. Answer no only for absence throughout the body; observations elsewhere do not cancel a genuine declaration.

request.instruction: Read only the complete literal body, including HTML comments, tables, formulas and templates. Decide whether it contains at least one genuine request for an action, answer, submission, improvement or remedy, or explicitly presents an action or state as a subject's intended goal or need. Count indirect requests and actual conditional reporting or submission directions, including directions carried by a template or HTML comment whether or not the requested information has been supplied. No addressee, stated reason, fully identified final goal, solution, adoption or implementation is required. Distinguish a relationship presented as a target or request from wording that only locates the circumstances of a reported event or explains a necessary response to it. An incident, inability, missing feature, risk, complaint, category or recipient mention alone does not declare the desired opposite or request its correction. Merely explaining what was necessary to obtain an observed result or work around it does not by itself declare an intended goal. Do not exclude a genuine goal or request merely because it appears within a report or a subordinate clause; do not infer one solely from modality, tense, a heading, mention, imperative form or question mark. A specification or expected caption alone does not establish this request or subject-goal role. One qualifying statement anywhere is sufficient and observations elsewhere do not cancel it. Quoted or hypothetical text counts when the body uses it to make an actual request or goal declaration, but not when shown only as an illustration. Synthetic contrast: 'I need a cost estimate before ordering the materials' declares a goal or need; 'The estimate arrived late, so I postponed the order' alone reports an event and response. Do not consult external content.

options.yes: The complete body contains at least one genuine request or declaration of a subject's intended goal or need of the kind defined in the instruction. This includes actual reporting or submission directions before the requested information is supplied. Merely naming a category or recipient, reporting an incident or inability, or explaining a necessary workaround does not itself establish this role.
options.no: The complete body contains no genuine request or declaration of a subject's intended goal or need of the kind defined in the instruction. Answer no only for absence throughout the body; a report or subordinate clause does not cancel an actual request or goal.

### Nixpkgs version

- Unstable (26.11)

### Describe the bug

Upon switching Darktable from Nixpkgs Stable to Unstable, it fails to launch. It displays the splash screen for a second and then dumps the following to the console:

```
ERROR: something wrong with flag 'flagfile' in file '/build/source/src/gflags.cc'.  One possibility: file '/build/source/src/gflags.cc' is being linked both statically and dynamically into this executable.
```

### Steps to reproduce

1. Install darktable from Nixpkgs stable
2. Launch and notice no errors
3. Install Darktable from Nixpkgs unstable
4. Launch and notice the programme does not launch with the aforementioned error

```nix
